### 4.108 Native x87 exceptions and BIOS INT 10h routing

Native DOS installed its BIOS video gate over IDT vector 10h, which is also
processor exception 16, `#MF`. An unmasked x87 error therefore entered the
software video vector instead of the client's exception chain. The
[Intel SDM, Volume 3A, Interrupt 16](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/835754/253668-sdm-vol-3a.pdf)
defines this as a fault when CR0.NE is set: a waiting x87 instruction or FWAIT
reports the pending error, without a CPU error code. Saved CS:EIP identifies
that waiting instruction, not the earlier arithmetic operation.

The native gate table now leaves the kernel's DPL0 #MF entry intact. Hardware
faults reach the existing DPMI exception bridge, while software `CD 10` reaches
the bounded #GP instruction decoder. That path now uses the existing default
DPMI reflector for translated services without a registered protected vector;
interpreter and direct native service gates retain their fast path. The native
IDT backup shrinks from 13 to 12 entries; EXEC's size-derived backup follows it.
No video API, arithmetic result, fault IP or application name is special-cased.

`dpmi_x87_route.S` builds `dpmf16.com` and `dpmf32.com`, both USE32 native
clients, with SS16/SS32 respectively. SS16 keeps BEEFh in the high half of ESP.
The probes test default BIOS calls before 0205h registration, application
software handlers, and the restored 0204h vector, including 15-byte prefixed
INT instructions. Invalid-operation and zero-divide errors are unmasked and
raised at FWAIT. The exception handler checks status, zero error code, original
CS:EIP/SS:ESP and RF, clears the pending condition with FNCLEX, and returns to
the unchanged FWAIT. Software frames must instead contain next-IP and no RF.
CR0.NE absence is explicitly rejected, not reported as success.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 dos-x87-routing-test
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 -j4 build/kernel.elf
# Inside the booted native test VM:
dosrun dpmf16.com
dosrun dpmf32.com
```

The final kernel is 6,255,840 bytes, SHA256
`481aec37c3404ce8638818d84f81494ae56be3e50939c140bde0539c52307fe1`.
`dos-x87-route-control2-20260910` uses the previous 52166a18 kernel and the
same final probes: both report `DPMI MF MISROUTED TO BIOS` and exit 71h.
The intermediate ed9f4eca kernel fixed #MF but rejected an unregistered BIOS
translator: native `dpvgamem.com` failed at its INT 10h at 00BF:01CB.
Its `run1`/`tcg1` evidence is retained and excluded from final validation.

Final `dos-x87-route-run2-20260910` completes 64 selected commands: 63 passes

probes pass six executions across KVM, TCG and the post-DOOM KVM sequence.

### 4.109 Native DOS floating-point state across services and EXEC

`dos_int_common` saved only integer and segment registers before calling C.
Vectorized host code could overwrite the client's XMM/YMM registers, while
client rounding modes and pending unmasked exceptions remained live in the
host. Raw PM-to-RM transitions abandoned the native stack with `longjmp`, so
adding only a normal-return save/restore would still lose the register file.

Each native service entry now reserves a private 64-byte-aligned FP image on
IST2, saves it before any C call and restores it after the last one. The path
uses XSAVE/XRSTOR with the existing kernel XCR0=7 policy, or FXSAVE/FXRSTOR on
CPUs without AVX. XSAVE reserved header bits are cleared before saving. Host C
runs with an initialized x87 environment and default MXCSR; client state,
including pending exception status, is restored on return to the client.
The integer-frame ABI is unchanged; the FP image is a third dispatcher argument.

A lazily allocated, direct-mapped backing page retains the image across
non-local suspensions and subsequent native entry. The first entry initializes
a clean register file. Native backend exit restores the saved host x87 control
word and MXCSR. EXEC snapshots retain the parent's backing page, children own
independent pages, and parent restoration/root cleanup release the departing
image. The existing 137-check EXEC-continuation matrix now also checks that
child activation detaches the FP image and preserves all 1,024 parent bytes.

`dpmi_fp_state.S` builds five 3,036-byte COMs: `dpfp16`, `dpfp32`, `dpfpr16`,
`dpfpr32` and the `dpfpc32` EXEC child. Both main probes are USE32, with SS16
(BEEFh in ESP's high half) or SS32. Checks cover initial control/status,
repeated DPMI services, DOS version, BIOS video, a software handler making
nested services, four raw PM/RM round trips, MMX aliases, all eight x87 and
XMM registers, MXCSR, diagnostic x87 pointers/opcode, and conditional YMM upper
halves. An unmasked invalid operation must survive INT 31h and reach #MF at
the unchanged FWAIT. The EXEC child terminates with an unmasked error pending;
the parent's complete saved state must survive its native execution and exit.
The raw-only pair isolates the non-local transition from ordinary services.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 dos-fp-state-test
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 -j4 build/kernel.elf
# Inside the booted test VM; dpfpc32.com must be present for EXEC:
dosrun dpfp16.com
dosrun dpfp32.com
dosrun dpfpr16.com
dosrun dpfpr32.com
```

The final kernel is 6,255,936 bytes, SHA256

### 4.110 Interpreter x87 and real/protected-mode ownership

The software CPU previously advertised no FPU and delivered #NM for every x87
escape. An application doing floating-point work before entering DPMI, or in a
real-mode callback, could not share the native register-preservation work above.
`dos_fpu.c` and `dos_fpu_host.S` now mediate x87 instructions through a trusted,
fixed host-opcode table. This is hardware-assisted execution, not a new floating-
point arithmetic library and not a claim of a bit-exact historical Pentium.

The decoder validates the guest opcode and the complete 2/4/8/10/14/28/94/108-byte
operand span before loading guest FP state. Host instructions see a staging
buffer, never a guest address. A fault on the second page cannot consume ST(0),
modify the destination or mark the first page dirty. Completed stores use the
existing guest memory path, preserving VGA and JIT write mediation. Unmasked
invalid/overflow/underflow stores do not commit; precision exceptions can commit
the rounded result and pop, as required by the instruction contract.

The assembly gate saves the host register file using XSAVE or FXSAVE, disables
maskable interrupts, restores the VM image, executes one validated operation,
saves the result, clears pending host FP exceptions and restores the host image.
No C or interruptible window runs with the guest image loaded. The VM's existing
FP backing page is shared with native entry, raw switches and EXEC ownership;
native service snapshots now also capture legacy FCS/FDS using FNSTENV.
This does not resolve the separate general nested kernel-ISR/NMI ownership audit.

Environment save/restore translates protected and real-address formats with
both operand sizes, including full tag words and the 80-byte register payload.
Diagnostic IP, data pointers, selectors and opcode refer to the guest, not the
kernel thunk or staging buffer. Integer/real/BCD conversions, x87 stack operations,
rounding, transcendental instructions, conditional moves and flag comparisons
use the host arithmetic. FISTTP uses truncating RC around a FISTP host operation.
The mediated FCOMI path explicitly enforces Intel's FLAGS/C1 semantics, including
an unmasked invalid comparison, independently of the host's result flags.

CR0.EM/TS still produce #NM; invalid encodings and LOCK produce #UD. Pending
unmasked errors reach #MF when NE is set. In legacy mode they assert the virtual
AT FERR/IRQ13 latch; port F0 acknowledges it and enables IGNNE recovery. The ROM's
IRQ75h handler acknowledges both PICs and chains the installed INT02h math-error
handler. FWAIT retains its faulting IP and RF while stalled. DPMI entry sets NE
for the protected client while preserving the real-mode control image for raw
returns. BIOS INT11h and the BDA equipment bit now report the implemented FPU;
the virtual CPUID adds the on-chip-FPU bit, without claiming MMX/SSE/FXSAVE.

`dos-fpu-test`, also included in `dos-api-test`, has 1,856 assertions covering
real/USE16/USE32 execution, rounding and precision, BCD, stack/tag behavior,
environment formats, masked and unmasked exceptions, RF, #NM/#UD, memory-fault
atomicity, IGNNE, and all register encodings and memory opcode groups. The
`dos_x87.S` COMs preserve a real-mode result into protected mode, execute a hot
x87/JIT loop, save/restore around a DOS service, and exercise the BIOS IRQ13
chain. USE16 enters native execution through a USE32 alias and returns to its
actual 16-bit code segment. Both protected hot loops retire 414 JIT instructions
when run with `--emulate` and without a step limit.

```sh

make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 -j4 build/kernel.elf
# In the guest:
dos-fpu-test
dosrun --emulate --max-steps 100000 dofprm.com
dosrun --emulate dofp16.com
dosrun --emulate dofp32.com
dosrun dofp16.com
dosrun dofp32.com
dosrun dofpe32.com
```

### 4.111 Native DOS ISR floating-point ownership and data mediation

Native DOS now uses a private, aligned FP image for each generic BSP interrupt,
as it already did for its DOS service gates. Both paths use the same assembly
save/restore helpers, including XSAVE/AVX or FXSAVE/SSE and the legacy FCS/FDS
snapshot. Host C runs with initialized x87 and default MXCSR controls; a pending
client exception cannot leak into the dispatcher. The normal process/scheduler
FP-slot path is unchanged when no native DOS session is published.

The generic ISR bridge only imports a CPL3 client's image when its CR3 and
active VM match. It exports the image again after dispatch, so an interpreted
data operation updates the registers eventually restored to native code.
Interrupts inside host C retain their own FP image without replacing the
client's. VM pointers are dereferenced only after switching to the kernel CR3.

This enables checked x87 memory mediation on the virtual VGA aperture, alongside
the existing integer path. D8h-DFh operands use the existing interpreter decoder,
address validation and staging; no guest operand becomes a host pointer. Vector
memory operations remain outside that admission path. `dpmi_fp_memory.S` tests
integer/real/80-bit loads and stores, arithmetic, FSAVE/FRSTOR, rounding, a
repeated mediated loop and retained SSE registers, using 16- and 32-bit stacks.
Each native COM completes 139 mediated accesses and exits 2Ah. A variant without
SSE exercises the same arithmetic through the strict interpreter.

`dos-fpu-test` adds two assertions around a real generic INT FFh inside a
simulated service-gate save/restore. Separate host and client images, an outer
pending x87 exception, all 16 XMM registers and enabled YMM upper halves must
survive. This is a bounded nesting test, not an exhaustive NMI/scheduler proof.
The complete matrix now has 1,858 assertions.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 -j4 build/kernel.elf dos-fp-state-test
# In the guest:
dos-fpu-test
dosrun --emulate --max-steps 100000 dpfmi32.com
dosrun dpfm16.com
dosrun dpfm32.com
```

### 4.112 DPMI coprocessor controls and native host-entry policy

INT 31h/0E00h and 0E01h now implement the selected [DPMI 1.0 coprocessor contract](https://www.sudleyplace.com/dpmione/dpmispec1.0.pdf),
superseding the outstanding controls noted in 4.111. MP/EM requests belong to
the current client, not to a temporary CPU snapshot. Raw-mode transitions,
host-call returns and EXEC preserve that policy; a new client's changes do not
overwrite its suspended parent's request. Without an explicit 0E01h request,
the virtual CPU retains its existing control-register behavior, including
standalone guest-IDT/VCPI execution. Status reports the integrated hardware x87
used by both backends. MP=0 does not discard saved FP state: the specification
permits that optimization but does not require it. The host still reports its
existing DPMI version; these extensions do not advertise complete DPMI 1.0.

Native entry and return apply client MP/EM/TS to hardware CR0. The private FP
entry record retains the interrupted CR0, and assembly clears EM/TS before any
XSAVE/FXSAVE, x87 or C code. The final assembly return restores the outgoing
policy after restoring the FP image. Generic interrupts inside host services
retain their own control state. Termination and non-local raw/EXEC suspension
restore host control state before releasing the backing image.

Other host ABI entries cannot bypass that guard. While the BSP owns a native
DOS session, non-DOS IDT gates are DPL0; software INT 2Eh/80h consequently uses
the existing DOS #GP/vector reflection path. Native ownership also clears
EFER.SCE and, when physical CPUID reports SEP, IA32_SYSENTER_CS. Detaching restores
the saved IDT and fast-entry policy. The [Intel instruction reference](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/www/public/us/en/documents/manuals/64-ia-32-architectures-software-developer-vol-2b-manual.pdf)
documents the disabled SYSENTER/SYSCALL fault behavior. This extends the existing
global native table ownership, not the scheduler's SMP concurrency contract.

`dpmi_coprocessor.S` builds `dpcp16.com` and `dpcp32.com` (USE32 code with both
stack widths) plus the EXEC child `dpcpc32.com`. Both interpreted and native
parents check all MP/EM combinations, unaffected registers/FLAGS, SMSW, #NM
skip/retry and retained x87 arithmetic. They exercise private INT 2Eh/80h
handlers, SYSENTER/SYSCALL rejection, BIOS/DOS services, raw switching and EXEC.
An installed 0213h handler reflects real-mode #NM, changes EM and retries the
instruction; the full CPU restore must not undo its new policy. The child and
parent exit with EM set. The host FPU matrix additionally tests stale snapshots,
host-activation restoration and all eight MP/EM/TS combinations across a real
generic interrupt. It now contains 1,931 assertions.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 -j4 build/kernel.elf dos-fp-state-test
# In the guest, with dpcpc32.com beside both parents:
dos-fpu-test
dosrun --emulate dpcp16.com
dosrun --emulate dpcp32.com
dosrun dpcp16.com
dosrun dpcp32.com
```

### 4.113 Native DPMI virtual-interrupt contract versus virtual IOPL3

The previous references to native `dpflags32.com` exit 71h as a DPMI gap were
too broad. The [DPMI 1.0 specification, Virtual Interrupts and 0902h](https://www.sudleyplace.com/dpmione/dpmispec1.0.pdf)
explicitly permits hosts to keep physical IF enabled, report that physical
state through PUSHF, and leave virtual IF unaffected by POPF or ordinary IRET.
Clients must use CLI/STI or 0900h/0901h to change virtual IF and 0902h to read it.
Hardware handlers enter with virtual interrupts disabled; portable handlers
explicitly execute STI before IRET. The previously implemented private locked
return also restores its recorded caller state; that host assistance is not a
reason for clients to depend on unprivileged IRET changing IF.

`dpflags16.com` and `dpflags32.com` remain unchanged. They test the software
CPU's stronger virtual-IOPL3 instruction profile, including POPF restoring IF.
Native exit 71h is still recorded, but no longer mislabeled as a DPMI failure
or counted as a conformance pass. Conversely, the new native-profile COMs must
reject the interpreter's IOPL3 FLAGS image. Neither profile has been changed
to make the other's test green, and native I/O privileges have not been raised.

`dpmi_native_if.S` builds `dpnif16.com` and `dpnif32.com`: both are 32-bit DPMI
clients with USE32 code and SS.B=0/1 respectively, not 16-bit DPMI clients.
They additionally call a USE16 code alias to exercise 16-bit PUSHF/POPF/IRET
defaults. The probes check physical IF/IOPL, virtual IF before and after POPF
and ordinary IRET, returned AH/AL and upper EAX for 0900h-0902h, unchanged
general registers, DF, and stack balance. Software handlers observe the
caller's virtual IF; nested software entry inside IRQ0 retains the disabled
state. BIOS time advances for three ticks with interrupts virtually disabled
without entering the installed IRQ0 handler; enabling permits multiple timer
deliveries. Both the API path and CLI/STI are exercised.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 dos-flags-test

dosrun dpnif16.com
dosrun dpnif32.com
# Unchanged software-CPU profile:
dosrun --emulate dpflags16.com
dosrun --emulate dpflags32.com
```

### 4.114 BIOS extended-memory block moves

INT 15h/AH=87h previously returned AH=0/CF=0 without reading the descriptor
table or copying any bytes. It now implements the classic AT contract from
the [IBM PS/2 and PC BIOS Interface Technical Reference, May 1988, pages 2-85 through 2-88](https://bitsavers.org/pdf/ibm/pc/ps2/15F0306_PS2_and_PC_BIOS_Interface_Technical_Reference_May88.pdf):
ES:SI addresses a 48-byte table, with source and target descriptors at 10h
and 18h. CX counts words, up to 8000h. The descriptors have 24-bit physical
bases, 16-bit limits, access 93h and a clear reserved word. This does not
silently opt into a different 386 descriptor extension.

The implementation snapshots the table, validates both complete payload
ranges and their VM backing, then copies forward words. Overlap has MOVSW
semantics, not memmove semantics; an output aliasing the table cannot change
the already admitted descriptors. It uses the existing physical-memory
helpers, including EMS/VBE aliases, rather than dereferencing guest addresses
in host memory. Invalid descriptors, counts and unbacked spans return
AH=2/CF=1/ZF=0 without changing the payload. Successful copies return
AH=0/CF=0/ZF=1 and preserve other registers and FLAGS, including DF and IF.

Protected callers use their DPMI client width for ES:SI/ES:ESI. The small
`dpmi_read_service_record` wrapper reuses checked service-buffer admission,
page translation, A-bit updates and exception handling. A table can cross
noncontiguous mapped pages; its payload bases remain physical addresses,
not aliases in the caller's page tables. A cancelled service fault is not
overwritten with fabricated BIOS success. No host GDT/CR0 transition is
needed for these VM-owned copies.

`dos-bios-test` runs the existing BIOS contracts plus 160 block-move cases:
40 scenarios across the four initial CF/ZF combinations. Each compares the
entire CPU record and a separate 1.5 MiB expected memory image. Cases cover
zero/one/maximal counts, short limits, reserved bits, non-present/read-only
descriptors, 24-bit overflow, backing boundaries, odd-address overlap,
table aliasing, EMS frame crossings, invalid VBE banks, wrapped/truncated
tables and DPMI16/32 tables split across noncontiguous pages. The paged cases
deliberately leave payload linear addresses unmapped and check read A bits.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 build/kernel.elf dos-bios-move-test
# In the guest:
dos-bios-test
dosrun --emulate bmovrm.com
dosrun --emulate bmov16.com
dosrun --emulate bmov32.com
dosrun --emulate bmovs32.com
```

### 4.115 Native IRQ probes use clock deadlines

The SS16 hardware-IRQ failures from 4.114 needed diagnosis before changing
the return path. Conditional diagnostics in `dpmi_native_irq.S` record the
stage, first bad extended frame, expected CS/SS/ESP/RF, trace count, TSC,
virtual IF and PIC mask/ISR/IRR. The original four COMs were byte-identical
while collecting this evidence. The `dos-irq-diagnostic-kvm-20260912` run
completed 20 commands with five failures; all diagnosed SS16 failures were
stage 5/reason 4, waiting for IRQ0, not a malformed return frame. A later
`dos-irq-timing-kvm-20260912` run passed 40 commands after adding a BIOS
query before the loop, showing that instrumentation itself changed timing.

The decisive `dos-irq-state-kvm-20260912` capture removes that query from
the positive path. Of 20 commands, 19 pass and one diagnostic SS16 command
fails. ECX entered the wait with all 200,000,000 iterations and reached zero;
virtual IF is 1, physical FLAGS 246h, and PIC mask/ISR/IRR are all zero.
The six software/nested #DB returns are correct, hardware_seen is zero,
and ESP remains ABCD8000h. The TSC delta is 0A65DB39h. With **that boot's**
3995 MHz calibration it spans about 43.67 ms, less than the default PIT
period of 54.93 ms. The previous estimate of 45.91 ms used another boot's
3800 MHz value. An iteration count cannot establish that an IRQ period has
elapsed. Neither this capture nor the earlier failures show a corrupt IRQ
return frame; they are not sufficient evidence to change kernel IRQ code.

The hardware probes now map segment 0040h using
[DPMI 1.0 function 0002h](https://www.sudleyplace.com/dpmione/dpmispec1.0.pdf#page=57)
and read the BIOS tick counter at FS:006Ch. They first observe a fresh tick
with virtual interrupts disabled, preventing an initially stale BDA value
from shortening the deadline. After enabling virtual IF, a native PAUSE
loop waits for the handler or four further ticks. There is no BIOS/DPMI
call inside that loop. A separate bounded watchdog reports reason 5 rather
than falsely reporting the reason-4 IRQ deadline if the clock wait cannot
finish. All existing RF/TF, CS/SS, full-ESP and trace-count assertions remain.
The software-only `dpirq32.com` and `dpirqs16.com` are still byte-identical.

`dpirqd32.com` and `dpirqds.com` retain failure diagnostics for both stack
widths. `dpirqoff.com` deliberately invokes 0900h instead of 0901h, without
changing the PIC mask. It must reach four ticks with no hardware IRQ, six
software traces, an expected count of seven and matching ABCD8000h stack
values, then return FAIL/71h. The checker validates the elapsed ticks,
remaining watchdog count and disabled virtual IF. This is a negative
control, not a successful application execution.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 dos-native-irq-test
# Native guest executions; repeat the first four to exercise timing:
dosrun dpirqh32.com
dosrun dpirqhs.com
dosrun dpirqd32.com
dosrun dpirqds.com
dosrun dpirqoff.com  # Intentional stage-5/reason-4 failure, exit 71h.
```

the other 216 are unchanged. Source snapshots include the checker.

### 4.116 A20 bus gating and DOS transfer buffers

The previous goal turn verified disk cleanup without changing the DOS layer.
This follow-up implements the previously disconnected A20 path. GitNexus was
unavailable; manual impact analysis covered CPU memory helpers, JIT source
validation, the per-VM chipset, BIOS dispatch and INT 21h transfer buffers.
No Win32 compatibility behavior or persistent application disk was changed.

The 8042 D0h/D1h output-port commands and DDh/DFh shortcuts now affect guest
memory. Port 92h supplies the second enable source. The two sources are ORed,
as specified by the [Intel ICH2 processor interface and PORT92 register](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/doc/datasheet/82801ba-i-o-controller-hub-2-82801bam-i-o-controller-hub-2-mobile-datasheet.pdf#page=128).
The post-boot default remains enabled (8042 output 03h, port 92h zero).
INT 15h/2400h-2403h supplies disable, enable, query and method discovery;
unsupported subfunctions return AH=86h/CF=1. BIOS disable clears both enable
sources without consuming pending keyboard data or resetting other bits.

The cached latch belongs to the VM, not a saved CPU or DPMI client. CPU bus
cycles clear bit 20 only, preserving all other address bits. Masking precedes
VGA/EMS/VBE mapping, so device-selected backing memory is not masked again.
The software page walker masks PDE/PTE accesses and the translated physical
result, while retaining the original linear fault address and permission
checks. Instruction fetches, operand probes and JIT source checks use the same
effective address policy; read-ahead does not enter aliased device windows.

[DPMI's HMA contract](https://www.sudleyplace.com/dpmione/dpmispec1.0.pdf#page=11)
keeps A20 enabled for protected-mode execution under a host. Osito-K uses that
policy for both software and native DPMI, without simulating a PM 1 MiB wrap.
The real-mode latch survives the PM interval. A simulated real-mode procedure
sees that latch, and its caller resumes with unmasked PM memory. Guest-owned
protected-mode CPUs are modeled with physical bit-20 masking; this is not a
claim that real processors define A20M behavior in every protected-mode case.

BIOS 87h uses explicit unmasked chipset accesses for its descriptor table and
forward word copies. This matches [SeaBIOS's enable/copy/restore sequence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreboot/seabios/master/src/system.c),
without temporarily mutating the VM's latch. The checked 24-bit spans and
overlapping MOVSW behavior from 4.114 remain in place.

`dos_mem_guest_span` preflights backing page by page. It returns a borrowed
pointer only for contiguous RAM without VGA effects. File/device transfers
retain that zero-copy path and allocate a bounded temporary buffer otherwise;
copies then pass through the byte accessors. AH=0Ah writes edited characters
directly into guest memory, preserving partial input on Ctrl+C and wrapping
correctly across A20. EXEC and path-buffer preflight also honor the mask.
This is a physical-span helper, not a replacement for a full paged linear
INT 21h buffer contract.

The new `dos_a20_test.c` matrix covers 84 gate/BIOS/memory/JIT cases and six
console/device cases, including bounds failures before input consumption,
partial console input, unmasked BIOS moves, page-table A/D writes and VM
isolation. `dos_a20.S` builds real-mode, DPMI16 and two DPMI32 stack-width
programs. They perform wrapped file write/read round trips, change both gate
sources and compare PM memory with 0301h real-mode procedure results. The
11-command matrix passes on both final backends: eight explicit software
executions, one default DPMI16 software execution and two actual native
DPMI32 executions. Default DPMI16 is not mislabeled as native execution.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 build/kernel.elf dos-a20-test
dos-bios-test
dosrun --emulate --max-steps 100000 a20rm.com
dosrun --emulate a20p16.com
dosrun a20p32.com
dosrun a20ps16.com
```

### 4.117 XMS control entry and shared extended-memory ownership

`dos_xms.c` adds a VM-owned XMS manager, discovered through INT 2Fh/4300h
and 4310h. Its real-mode far entry at F000:20C0 has the five patchable bytes
used for hook chaining. The private F8h service recognizes the entry address;
it does not intercept arbitrary guest F8h instructions. Version, HMA, A20,
memory handles, move/lock/resize and UMB services use the
[original XMS 3.0 calling contract](https://www.phatcode.net/res/219/files/xms30.txt),
including the extended 88h, 89h, 8Eh and 8Fh register forms. Unimplemented
function numbers return an error rather than fabricated success.

The manager initializes after the virtual chipset and is released by VM
cleanup. Its state is not copied with CPU or DPMI client snapshots. Metadata
grows in host pages, supports more than 256 concurrent handles, and respects
the 16-bit handle ABI. A zero-KB allocation owns a valid handle without
consuming guest pages. Lock counts, invalid handles, arithmetic bounds and
allocation failure are checked; failed reallocations retain the old block.
Cleanup releases its allocations even when a guest omitted unlock/free,
without releasing another manager's allocations.

HMA reservation and XMS blocks share the existing DPMI/EMS/VCPI physical-page
bitmap. The first 64 KiB above 1 MiB is excluded from ordinary allocations;
claim/release controls its exclusive use. Allocation and in-place resize use
checked shared-pool operations, with allocate/copy/free relocation when needed.
Free-memory queries exclude reserved pages. Function 88h's highest physical
address still includes reserved RAM, and remains valid when the pool is empty.
This does not enlarge the existing DOS-visible 16 MiB RAM model.

Global and counted local A20 requests reconcile the physical gate with their
references. A20 queries read the actual effective latch. The first non-version
control call activates the BIOS 88h zero-memory response; BIOS 87h retains its
unmasked copy and A20 preservation. Startup and HMA claims check VDISK-style
headers before permitting conflicting ownership. The tests use synthetic
headers, not a real historical VDISK installation, so broader VDISK allocation
scheme compatibility remains unverified.

Moves validate the complete parameter record and both endpoints before copying.
The DS base-plus-offset calculation cannot wrap into unrelated low memory.
The new `dos_phys_guest_span` shares the existing span implementation but
does not apply A20 masking. XMS uses it for physical transfers, preserving the
caller's latch and handling conventional, extended and contiguous EMS aliases.
Copies support overlap and provide guest IRQ windows between 8 KiB chunks.
Internal pins prevent reentrant free/resize of in-flight blocks. Handle IDs
are resolved again after a window because an interrupt handler can grow the
metadata table. The forced IRQ test frees a pinned block unsuccessfully,
allocates 400 zero-KB handles, resumes the copy and verifies its contents.

XMS UMB functions allocate, release and resize paragraph runs in the virtual
board's D0000h-DFFFFh RAM. This is separate from the E0000h EMS frame. Splits,
coalescing, exhaustion, interior-pointer rejection and failure-atomic growth
are covered. DOS INT 21h/AH=58h upper-memory linking and the upper MCB chain
are **not connected yet**; this is an XMS UMB API, not completed DOS UMB support.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 build/kernel.elf dos-xms-test
dos-xms-test
dosrun --emulate --max-steps 100000 xmsrm.com
dosrun --emulate xmsp16.com
dosrun xmsp32.com
dosrun xmsps16.com
```

the cases above, HMA absence, complete pool exhaustion, 512 concurrent handles,
lock-count overflow, small/zero-size reallocations and initialization conflicts.
Four COM probes additionally check actual far entry/RETF, patch chaining,
register upper halves, CF/DF, DPMI 0301h calls, SS16/SS32 and allocation
non-overlap. All eleven command variants pass on both final backends: eight
explicit software runs, one default DPMI16 software run and two actual native
DPMI32 runs. The old kernel fails all eight software variants at XMS discovery,
stage 1/exit 71h. That negative control proves the missing entry contract,
not every individual memory operation.

### 4.118 DOS upper-memory arenas and process-owned cleanup

`dos_mem.c` now joins DOS allocation to the XMS UMB provider through real
MCB chains. The nine allocation policies and unlinked high-memory fallback
follow the [MS-DOS 5 Programmer's Reference, pp. 69 and 347-351](https://ftpmirror.your.org/pub/misc/bitsavers/pdf/microsoft/msdos_5/Microsoft_-_MS-DOS_Programmers_Reference_1991.pdf).
Low policies search conventional RAM; high-first searches upper RAM before
falling back, and high-only searches upper RAM exclusively while linked.
INT 21h/5803h links or unlinks the chain; 5802h and the List of Lists publish
the state. Invalid strategies/link requests fail, rather than silently changing
the allocation policy. Alloc/free/resize propagate arena, block and capacity
errors as 7/9/8 instead of flattening them into out-of-memory errors.

The implementation reserves a bridge paragraph below A0000h before loading a
COM. On the first successful 5803h request, DOS claims currently free XMS UMB
runs. Host-owned extent boundaries remain independent of guest-editable MCBs.
DOS-owned gaps have system bridge MCBs, with headers only in DOS-reserved RAM;
VGA, ROM, the EMS frame and foreign XMS allocations are never used for headers.
Validation bounds each chain against its actual reserved extents, including
when upper memory is unlinked. Free and resize reject system bridge blocks.
XMS cannot release or resize a DOS reservation through its public UMB entry.
Unlinking retains the reservation and allocations; it does not give live DOS
blocks back to XMS. VM reset/cleanup releases the ownership metadata.

Owner cleanup scans both arenas regardless of the current link or allocation
policy. EXEC can therefore free a terminating child's PSP, environment and
extra high blocks without releasing its parent's allocations. The COM loader
also places its initial zero return word at the end of the allocated block,
capped at 64 KiB, instead of writing past short blocks into another mapping.
The initial SP is now block-end minus two, including the ordinary FFFEh case.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 build/kernel.elf dos-umb-test
dos-umb-test
dosrun --emulate --max-steps 100000 umblink.com
dosrun --emulate umblink.com
dosrun umblink.com
```

The C matrix reports 371 checks and zero failures on KVM and TCG. It covers
all nine linked/unlinked policies, fragmented XMS ownership, zero-size blocks,
exhaustion, failure-atomic resize, corrupted MCBs, protected bridges, unlinked
owner cleanup, DPMI high allocation/resize/free, short COM stacks and a fully
occupied XMS UMB pool. The 469-byte COM performs three sequential EXEC child launches
per execution, with child PSP/environment allocations in upper RAM. Children
leave an extra block allocated and unlink the arena before terminating; the
parent verifies its retained data and unchanged available memory. All three
execution variants pass on both backends. These are real-mode software/JIT
runs, not native DPMI32 UMB execution coverage.

The development C run retained nine failed checks caused by expecting AH=52h
to clear carry. Its returned pointer/data were correct; the test now checks
those outputs without assigning AH=52h a carry-result contract. The initial
COM assembler size assertion also failed before QEMU launch; the Makefile
now checks the linked binary's size. Neither failed attempt is a positive run.

TCG again lost serial output, including the result suffix/prompt. A captured
graphical console showed PASS and the returned prompt; klog recovered the
original 371/0 result without rerunning the test. An accidentally overlapping
reader left a partial command, producing a usage error on the first recovery
attempt. Those logs remain separate from the successful recovered COM runs.
The local serial checker now takes a per-run nonblocking lease before opening
the socket; a host negative test confirms that a competing reader is rejected
before connecting. This prevents reader overlap but does not fix the kernel's
serial-output loss. The strict serial matcher has not been weakened.

### 4.119 Buffered UART output and trustworthy DOS test captures

The COM1 driver no longer silently abandons a byte after 4096 status polls.
All its public emitters now reserve bounded records in a 16 KiB TX queue;
one consumer owns the UART. A preempted producer's unpublished reservation
cannot be skipped or overwritten. Consumers use try-acquisition, including
on reentry, rather than writing without ownership after a lock timeout.
Hexadecimal and decimal formatting also enter this queue. Text keeps CRLF
translation and `serial_write` keeps its existing embedded-NUL filtering;
raw `serial_putc` still transmits NUL. Long writes stream through multiple
64-byte records, not a new line-length limit.

The FIFO depth is detected through IIR. A verified 16550 FIFO accepts up to
16 bytes after THRE; otherwise the driver uses single-byte operation. TEMT
is checked for flush completion, independently of an empty software queue.
These distinctions follow the [TI PC16550D register contract, sections
8.6.3-8.6.5](https://media.digikey.com/pdf/Data%20Sheets/Texas%20Instruments%20PDFs/PC16550D.pdf).
The BSP timer retries pending output through a nonblocking, 64-byte poll.
A synchronous flush has a 20 ms elapsed-time budget; expiration retains
unsent bytes. Before TSC calibration it only polls, without inventing a
time limit from CPU iterations. Early driver objects use general registers
only, verified in their disassembly before relying on pre-SSE boot output.

`serial-stats` exposes accepted, sent, pending, dropped, timeout and busy
counters, capacity, FIFO depth and presence. Queue exhaustion or an absent
UART is an explicit counted loss, not a claim of unbounded lossless logging.
The klog tee remains independent of UART availability. Unused direct syscall
emitters were removed; the graphics module's diagnostic bridge now uses the
already-exported kernel serial function. That bridge compiles and its imports
resolve to existing exports; a graphics renderer was not exercised here.
Pre-BSS/kexec assembly probes intentionally remain direct port writes.

```sh
make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 build/kernel.elf
make -C arch/x86 HOST_CC=clang \
    SERIAL_HOST_SANITIZERS=-fsanitize=address,undefined serial-host-test
make -C arch/x86 HOST_CC=gcc serial-host-test
# In the guest:
serial-test
serial-stats
# Against a booted diagnostic VM; captures are never overwritten:
python3 arch/x86/scripts/check-serial-test.py "$run" --repeat 3
python3 arch/x86/scripts/check-serial-test.py "$run" --suite dos --repeat 3
```

The queue matrix has 106 checks and the host UART/formatting matrix has 17;
both pass with clang ASan/UBSan and GCC. They exercise a UART which stays
busy past 4096 polls, deadlines and later recovery, a missing clock, FIFO
and single-byte writes, saturation, ring/counter wrap, publication holes,
reentrant producers, TEMT and absent hardware. The unchanged previous driver
fails the delayed-UART control: its wire output loses a result digit while
the memory tee retains it. This negative control is not a passing old driver.

Each new backend completes three serial stress rounds: four producers emit

record, exact per-producer order, counts, formatting and the guest's counters.
All 1,536 received records are complete. Five offline mutations (missing,
duplicate or corrupt record, truncated number, pending-data counter) are
rejected by that same checker. No klog or screenshot fills a new-kernel
serial result. Each backend also completes three standalone repetitions of

### 4.120 Mediated x87 transfer stack faults and inhibited stores

`dos_fpu_execute` now checks physical x87 tags before loads, stores and
comparisons, independently of the host CPU/emulator. Masked stack faults
produce the destination-format indefinite value or unordered comparison;
unmasked faults retain TOP and operands and set the deferred exception state.
The existing guest memory probe, FWAIT/#MF and IRQ13 paths still own access
validation and delivery. The register image keeps logical register order while
its abridged tags remain physical; push/pop rotates the image accordingly.

This covers FLD/FILD/FBLD and constants, real/integer/BCD stores, register
FST/FSTP, FCOM/FUCOM/FICOM/FTST and FLAGS comparisons. An inhibited memory
store or FLAGS comparison also restores the host's speculative stack effect,
not just rejects its staged bytes. Precision exceptions still permit the
rounded store/pop. No QEMU, manufacturer or application-name branch was added.
The contracts follow [Intel SDM Volume 1, 4.7 and 8.5.1](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/843827/253665-sdm-vol-1-dec-24.pdf)
and the individual [Volume 2A instruction entries](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/868140/253666-089-sdm-vol-2a.pdf).

masked/unmasked operation, holes in the physical tags, all supported transfer
formats, comparison source holes, unchanged neighboring registers and memory,
and overflowing/underflowing narrow stores. Each final KVM/TCG run passes the
matrix three times: standalone, in the complete DOS API suite, and after the
regression sequence. KVM's last invocation follows DOOM and the PE32 probes.

### 4.121 Mediated x87 arithmetic stack faults

The physical-tag checks in `dos_fpu_execute` now also cover arithmetic,
FXCH, FCMOV and double-result instructions. Masked arithmetic underflow
writes the destination indefinite value and applies the specified pop;
unmasked faults retain TOP, tags and register contents while setting the
deferred exception state. Healthy operands still use the isolated host
arithmetic path. No host-vendor, QEMU or application-specific branch is added.

FCMOV checks both source tags even when its condition is false. FXCH replaces
only empty inputs before exchanging, preserving a valid input. Masked stack
faults in FPTAN, FXTRACT and FSINCOS produce two indefinite results, including
the occupied push slot. If ST(0) is empty as well, underflow takes priority
over overflow. Defined C1/C2 responses are checked separately from undefined
condition bits. These contracts follow [Intel SDM Volume 1](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/843827/253665-sdm-vol-1-dec-24.pdf)
and the individual [Volume 2A entries](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/868140/253666-089-sdm-vol-2a.pdf).
The [official Bochs implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bochs-emu/Bochs/master/bochs/cpu/fpu/fpu_trans.cc)
and 220 raw observations from a separate AMD Linux-host probe corroborate the
less obvious pair-result and source-tag responses; they are not an all-CPU
numeric oracle. No external implementation was copied.

The new matrix enumerates 256 opcode/ModRM forms, all eight TOP positions,
masked/unmasked operation, every relevant source-hole combination, full/free
push destinations and all CF/ZF/PF combinations for FCMOV. It checks integer
FLAGS, control/status, physical tags, untouched live registers, indefinite
outputs and unchanged memory inputs. There are **355,209 new checks per mode**
(real, USE16, USE32), **1,099,358 total** including the preceding 33,731 checks.
Each final backend passes it standalone, inside the full DOS API suite and
after regressions. Diagnostics sample the first twelve failures per mode;
aggregate failure counters are not sampled.

FYL2XP1. KVM passed, but TCG reported 96 failures at the healthy-input
assertion. Both instructions now receive a value near one eighth. This
corrects the fixture without relaxing assertions or changing production code.
The initial failed checker, kernel and logs remain archived. Undefined
out-of-domain numeric results are not treated as a portable stack contract.

### 4.122 Mediated x87 numerical exception inhibition

`dos_fpu_execute` now preserves the live register stack on unmasked numeric
#I/#D/#Z, including arithmetic, comparisons, pushes and pops. The checkpoint
is needed only when a result-inhibiting exception is unmasked. Exception
status and diagnostic pointers remain visible; the next waiting instruction
delivers the deferred fault. Narrow memory stores also remain inhibited on
unmasked #O/#U. The change adds no application, host-vendor or QEMU branch,
and does not change a public ABI, disk format or the host arithmetic thunk.

There are instruction-specific exceptions to rollback: FLD m32/m64 pushes a
normalized denormal even with DM clear; #P completes the instruction; #O/#U
register results must be stored with the architectural exponent adjustment.
FUCOMIP with unmasked #D updates comparison FLAGS but must not pop. These
rules follow [Intel SDM Volume 1, sections 8.5.1.2-8.5.6](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/843827/253665-sdm-vol-1-dec-24.pdf)
and the specific [Volume 2A FLD and instruction entries](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/868140/253666-089-sdm-vol-2a.pdf).
The specific FLD denormal note overrides the general no-stack-update rule.
Loads/copies of raw 80-bit values do not acquire the m32/m64 conversion faults.

The shared test-only `dos_fpu_numeric_cases.h` defines 43 vectors with exact
encoded operands. The guest matrix covers eight TOP positions, four rounding
modes and masked/unmasked operation in real, USE16 and USE32 modes. It adds
**30,976 checks per mode**, yielding **1,192,286 total** with all preceding
checks retained. It covers status, tags/TOP, unaffected live registers,
FLAGS, memory write inhibition, denormal load normalization, selected exact
biased register results and deferred FWAIT/#MF. A separate AMD Linux probe
retains 344 raw observations from the same vectors. It corroborates the
tested contracts, not every CPU's transcendental rounding or FLAGS profile.

have the same new tests, fixtures and remaining sources. Their 6,452,840-byte

The ten remaining TCG cases, with failures per mode, are:

- FMULP overflow: 32; FMULP underflow: 32; FADDP overflow: 32; FDIVP overflow:

Those assertions have not been dropped or relaxed. The fix enforces result
inhibition when an exception is reported; it cannot reconstruct numerical
exceptions or biased results that the host did not compute. Mask-aware
extended-precision evaluation, exception priority (including spurious #P on
unmasked #D), and broader transcendental coverage remain work for the layer.
No QEMU source or external numerical implementation was changed or copied.

### 4.123 Mask-aware extended-precision DOS arithmetic

The mediated DOS x87 path now evaluates 171 arithmetic forms using integer-only
extended-precision software: register and m32/m64/i16/i32 add, multiply,
subtract and divide, plus FSQRT, FRNDINT and FSCALE. Stack tags, checked guest
memory, inhibited updates, diagnostic pointers and deferred exception delivery
remain owned by `dos_fpu.c`. Unsupported operations still use the isolated
host thunk. Direct native instructions are not redirected by this change.

The numeric core is a selected BSD-3-Clause subset of
[Bochs' Berkeley SoftFloat3e fork](https://github.com/bochs-emu/Bochs/tree/dafbd06bf89fcd15b34cefcdf345fd0f30870de0/bochs/cpu/softfloat3e),
pinned to `dafbd06bf89fcd15b34cefcdf345fd0f30870de0`. All 39 imported files
are verbatim; the file list, SHA256 manifest, notices and local configuration
are in `arch/x86/lib/softfloat3e/`. No LGPL Bochs CPU instruction implementation
is imported. Its explicit per-operation status includes exception masks,
rounding control, precision control and C1; no global numeric state is shared
between DOS clients. The kernel builds it freestanding without exceptions or
RTTI. Object disassembly confirms 31 numerical objects, 2,908 instructions,
no x87/MMX/SIMD instructions, no external symbols, initialization arrays or
exception tables. This is a correctness change, not a performance claim.

This implements unmasked #O/#U exponent adjustments, including exact underflow
and FSCALE results still outside the representable range after adjustment.
The adapter also respects operand order independently of result destination,
exception priority and the original signaling class of widened memory NaNs.
In particular, a quiet NaN operand takes precedence over a signaling NaN;
widening must not erase that distinction before arithmetic selection. These
contracts follow [Intel SDM Volume 1, table 4-7 and section 8.5](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/843827/253665-sdm-vol-1-dec-24.pdf).
There are no application-specific or QEMU-specific branches.

produce **6,952,176 checks**. Exact status/C1 and completed 80-bit results are
compared with the host's isolated x87 execution. Clang and GCC both pass; GCC's
intentional upstream fallthrough warning remains visible and nonfatal only
for vendor objects. Our adapter/test retain `-Werror`. This is not exhaustive
input coverage or an assertion that every CPU has identical transcendental
behavior. TOP/tag faults remain covered by the separate guest matrix.

### 4.124 Mediated x87 trigonometric execution

The mediated DOS path now evaluates FSIN, FCOS, FSINCOS and FPTAN in software,
in addition to the 171 arithmetic forms from 4.123. `dos_fpu_soft_evaluate()`
returns explicit result-write, push and condition-code effects; the DOS layer
owns register rotation, TOP/tags and deferred exception delivery. An out-of-range
finite argument sets C2 without writing a result or pushing. Invalid inputs
produce the appropriate indefinite/quiet NaN, including both result lanes;
unmasked operand faults still restore the pre-instruction registers and TOP.
Precision exceptions complete their results and defer #MF to WAIT.

The arithmetic is pinned to Bochs commit
`dafbd06bf89fcd15b34cefcdf345fd0f30870de0`. Twenty-two additional verbatim
quad-precision dependencies expand `lib/softfloat3e` to 61 upstream files.
The separate `lib/bochs-transcendental` directory contains seven mathematical
sources/headers plus upstream COPYING. It is **not uniformly BSD**: its
SoftFloat Release 2b derivative notices and LGPL terms are retained and
identified in its README. No Bochs CPU execution runtime is imported.

Local derivative changes supply fixed-width port types, retain the product
invariant with a freestanding compiler trap instead of libc assert, preserve
tiny directional corrections through extended round/pack, and evaluate the
FSINCOS cosine lane before the sine lane. The latter retains sine's final C1.
All four instructions use extended precision independently of CW.PC; CW.RC
and exception masks remain per-operation state. Tiny sine/tangent results
support gradual masked underflow and the unmasked exponent-biased result.
The instruction contracts and two-result sequencing are documented in
[Intel SDM Volume 2A, FSIN/FCOS/FSINCOS/FPTAN](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/868140/253666-089-sdm-vol-2a.pdf).

`arch/x86/scripts/test-dos-fpu-trig.sh NEW_LOG` uses host-only MPFR, not a
kernel dependency. It checks 4,186 signed inputs, 598,272 evaluations and
**3,660,160 assertions**: exact special/tiny results, exception priority,
C2/write/push effects, immutable input, PC independence and approximation
error. Edge inputs use all 64 mask combinations; deterministic samples and
the 1/256 grid with both adjacent representable neighbors use masked and
unmasked precision. Tiny references raise MPFR precision to retain corrections
far below one extended-format ulp; 69,120 exact and 601,920 approximate result
lanes are checked. MPFR's rounding contract is described in its
[manual](https://www.mpfr.org/mpfr-current/mpfr.html#Rounding).

The reference uses mathematical sin/cos/tan for |x| <= 1. Beyond that, it uses
an independently computed remainder/quadrant with the 66-significant-bit
x87 pi/2 constant, not an infinitely accurate pi. This explicitly tests the
finite-pi model; it does not claim libm accuracy over the whole hardware
instruction range. Bounds are <1 ulp nearest and <1.5 ulp directed for the
reduced calculation, following
[Intel SDM Volume 1, sections 8.3.8 and 8.3.10](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/843827/253665-sdm-vol-1-dec-24.pdf).
Clang and GCC with ASan/UBSan both pass. Largest sampled errors are
0.675893590 ulp nearest and 1.153566516 ulp directed. The unchanged 171-form
arithmetic domain still passes **6,952,176** strict host comparisons with both
compilers; new approximate trig encodings are tested separately, not added
to that bit-exact arithmetic oracle.

The strict AMD hardware probe is intentionally still a separate observation:
184,320 comparisons show **3,840 status and 6,144 result differences**, not a
PASS. Before the local tiny/C1 changes these were 21,888 and 16,704. Small
FPTAN directed rounding and approximate last bits need not be identical to
that CPU's internal calculation; the MPFR bounds are checked independently.
Failed probe/compiler logs are retained. The initial kernel compile also
exposed the hosted assert dependency; it was fixed before either guest boot.
A separate 24-case hardware observation confirms that full-stack faults take
priority even for out-of-range pair arguments, matching the existing stack
precheck. It is not substituted for guest conformance tests.

The candidate kernel is **6,498,432 bytes**, SHA256
`082994e0e96c8cf2ade632682207bc991e408ca6861e90da5f09a1beb951c57a`.
An additional guest matrix covers signed zero, tiny normals/subnormals,
infinity, NaNs, unsupported encodings and range rejection across all TOP,
RC and supported PC values, four mask configurations and all three CPU modes.
It checks both result lanes, unchanged registers/memory/FLAGS, instruction
pointers and deferred WAIT delivery: 297,984 assertions per mode. The previous
355,209 stack and 30,976 numerical assertions per mode are retained.

### 4.125 Mediated x87 exponential, logarithmic and arctangent execution

`dos_fpu_soft_evaluate()` now handles F2XM1, FYL2X, FYL2XP1 and FPATAN with
integer-only extended arithmetic. The unary instruction writes ST(0); the
binary instructions write ST(1) and pop. CW.RC and exception masks are local
to each operation, while these instructions ignore CW.PC. The existing DOS
checkpoint retains registers/TOP on unmasked operand faults and completes
biased overflow/underflow or precision results before deferred WAIT delivery.
The instruction-specific special values, pop effects and defined domains follow
[Intel SDM Volume 2A](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/868140/253666-089-sdm-vol-2a.pdf).
This does not intercept additional direct-native instructions.

The same Bochs commit `dafbd06bf89fcd15b34cefcdf345fd0f30870de0` supplies
the new table-driven functions and FPATAN's remainder helper. Two additional
verbatim dependencies bring the BSD subset to 63 original files; the separate
math manifest has 15 originals including COPYING. Its SoftFloat-2b/LGPL
notices remain separate from the BSD subset. No CPU runtime is imported.

Validation found three mathematical/port defects. An exact zero remainder
was sent to a nonzero normalizer, causing a shift by 64 under UBSan; the
caller now returns signed zero directly. FYL2X's approximation could fall
just below the exact integer logarithm of a power of two, misclassifying
the normal/subnormal boundary; normalized powers now use their exponent.
FPATAN's tiny exact ratio lost the negative infinitesimal correction, giving
the wrong inward result, C1 and sometimes underflow. Exact tiny quotients
now retain that correction through final rounding; sufficiently small
nonexact quotients retain division residue. Larger nonexact ratios continue
through the existing polynomial. No application-specific input is recognized.

The initial host matrix recorded 9,216 failures and undefined shifts. That
count included both implementation failures and a reference error: a tiny
transcendental result can raise U/P even when its mathematical formula is
exact. The corrected reference accounts for transcendental precision behavior,
as described in [Intel SDM Volume 1, section 8.5.6](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/843827/253665-sdm-vol-1-dec-24.pdf),
and independently observed on the host CPU. FYL2X with zero x and infinite y
remains an infinity without Z, consistent with the SDM's result table; it was
not changed to match a guessed zero-divide rule.

Host success initially hid a freestanding initialization error. A global
minus-one constant called an out-of-line pack helper, leaving F2XM1's
translation-unit constants dependent on C++ startup. The initial kernel
`ef7dfa2d640fdf9b5265452faa754622a9e0cf3457a5a9828b4ced2b128b1cc7`
failed 1,728 guest assertions, all in the unsupported-input result case.
The constant is now static aggregate data. The new persistent build audit
`arch/x86/scripts/check-dos-fpu-build.py` rejects constructors, destructors,
exception tables, external numeric symbols, FP/SIMD instructions and stale
numeric objects/kernel. It covers the numerical objects, not all kernel code.

`arch/x86/scripts/test-dos-fpu-elementary.sh NEW_LOG` uses host-only MPFR.
The current matrix checks 31,944 input pairs, 10,132,272 evaluations and
**66,756,396 assertions** per compiler: signed class combinations, all 64
exception masks for edges, four RC modes, three PC settings, a deterministic
full-exponent sample and a 1/256 grid with adjacent representable neighbors.
Cancellation-safe `exp2m1`/`log2p1` references and adaptive precision for tiny
atan corrections use [MPFR's arithmetic](https://www.mpfr.org/mpfr-current/mpfr.html).
There are 6,007,908 exact special/power/tiny result comparisons and 3,364,044
approximate comparisons. Finite F2XM1 and FYL2XP1 inputs outside their
documented domains are not counted as conformance evidence.

The sample passes the test's <1 ulp nearest and <1.5 ulp directed thresholds;
largest observed errors are 0.742186640 and 1.210992261 ulp respectively.

In particular, the SDM permits up to 1.35 ulp nearest for FYL2X/FYL2XP1 with

### 4.126 Mediated x87 remainder and exponent extraction

`dos_fpu_soft_evaluate()` now handles FPREM, FPREM1 and FXTRACT without
executing host floating-point instructions. The remainder operations preserve
ST(1), return an exact ST(0), and expose completion through C2 and quotient
bits Q2/Q1/Q0 through C0/C3/C1. FPREM truncates the quotient; FPREM1 selects
nearest-even. Neither uses CW.RC or CW.PC. Partial reductions accept the
implementation-dependent N=32..63 contract from
[Intel SDM Volume 2A](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/868140/253666-089-sdm-vol-2a.pdf).
Undefined condition bits on exceptional operands retain the existing explicit
DOS policy; they are not claimed as portable native CPU results.

FXTRACT places the integer exponent in the former ST(0), then pushes the
signed significand. Its signed-zero, infinity, NaN and denormal cases use
the verbatim `extF80_extract.cc` from Bochs commit
`dafbd06bf89fcd15b34cefcdf345fd0f30870de0`. The BSD subset now contains 64
original files; the separately licensed math subset still has 15 originals.
The DOS checkpoint continues to inhibit writes/pushes on unmasked operand
faults and delivers pending exceptions through WAIT. No direct-native
instruction interception or public ABI/disk-format change was introduced.

A native AMD edge probe exposed two early returns in the existing remainder
helper: a subnormal dividend with an infinite divisor, and an exponent
difference below -1. Returning the operand directly missed unmasked
underflow's exponent-biased result. Both paths now use the existing mask-aware
extended round/pack helper. Masked exact subnormal remainders still raise
neither U nor P; unmasked U delivers the biased value, unless an earlier
unmasked operand exception inhibits it. This numerical helper is also used
by FPATAN, so its full regression was repeated. The 144-row observational
probe is retained separately; it is not itself a conformance PASS.

`arch/x86/scripts/test-dos-fpu-reduce.sh NEW_LOG` uses independent host-only
[MPFR arithmetic](https://www.mpfr.org/mpfr-current/mpfr.html). For partial
remainders it computes all 32 permitted reduction candidates, rather than
copying the production helper's N-selection algorithm. Completed reductions
use `fmodquo`/`remquo`; extraction uses `frexp`. Classes include signed zero,
subnormals, pseudo-denormals, normal boundaries, infinity, NaNs and unsupported
encodings. The matrix covers all 64 exception masks on class combinations,
four RC modes, three supported PC settings, half-way quotients with adjacent
representable neighbors and deterministic full-exponent inputs.

both FXTRACT outputs, mask-aware exceptions and RC/PC independence are checked.
Both compilers also pass the unchanged 6,952,176 arithmetic, 3,660,160 trig
and 66,756,396 elementary-math assertions, including FPATAN.

### 4.129 Mediated x87 register and control state

The new integer-only `dos_fpu_state_step` handles the remaining 122 register
and seven canonical memory forms: raw register moves/exchanges, conditional
moves, sign changes, constants, TOP rotation, tag release, legacy control
NOPs, initialization/exception clearing, and control/status/environment
load/store. The mediated decoder's **408 forms** now have exactly one software
handler: 279 numerical and 129 state/control forms. The native thunk table and
fallback are no longer linked into the kernel; an unexpected admitted opcode
without a handler stops that DOS CPU with a diagnostic. The assembly thunks
remain available only to host tests. Native DOS execution itself is unchanged.

The helper preserves physical register payloads while changing logical TOP,
leaves MXCSR/XMM state alone, reconstructs full tags on environment saves,
and compresses incoming tags by empty/nonempty state. Control/environment
loads normalize reserved control bits and recompute pending exceptions;
FNSTENV masks exceptions after saving, while FNSAVE resets x87 state only
after staging the old environment and all eight register payloads. Guest
memory validation, environment widths, pointers/selectors, store commit,
stack faults and deferred #MF/IRQ13 remain owned by the existing outer layer.
FISTTP no longer temporarily changes the guest control word: its numerical
handler already selects truncation explicitly.

The [Intel instruction reference](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/868140/253666-089-sdm-vol-2a.pdf)
defines constant loads using internal 66-bit constants and CW.RC, without
raising precision or setting C1 for rounding. The host oracle computes final
64-bit results independently with MPFR and checks them against native FLD
instructions. Rounding a mathematical value to 66 bits first is not a valid
oracle: it double-rounded FLDLG2 incorrectly. The first implementation also
rounded FLDL2T upward in nearest mode. Both mistakes were exposed and fixed;
initial failing logs are retained. No CPU instruction implementation or new
vendor source was imported.

under ASan/UBSan: **4,915,200 cases / 93,174,649 assertions each**. An independent
physical-register model crosses TOP, RC, PC, raw operand classes, sticky
status and integer conditions; no-wait operations also start with pending
unmasked exceptions. It sweeps all 65,536 control words for FLDCW/FLDENV/FRSTOR,
all 65,536 full tag words, and rejects 65,246 non-state opcode/ModRM pairs
without changing state, memory or result. The host success matrix has 128
forms: FLD ST(7) necessarily underflows or overflows, so the existing guest
stack-fault matrix owns that form. The 4,259,840 native differences in
undefined condition codes are observations, not conformance failures or
extra passes. Padding, memory guards, AX, integer flags and SSE state are
checked separately; FXSAVE's host-supplied MXCSR mask is not mistaken for
guest-writable state.

### 4.130. Native x87 diagnostic state and backend limits

The native DOS bridge now retains the legacy x87 diagnostic environment
alongside its full XSAVE64/FXSAVE64 register image. This is a correction to
the bridge, **not complete native x87 compatibility**: the final strict
probes still expose limitations of the tested virtualization backends.

The architectural distinction matters. The 64-bit restore format and the
compatibility format do not have the same FIP/FDP/FCS/FDS contract. Intel
documents the layouts in SDM volume 1, section 8.1.8. Older AMD implementations
can also omit error pointers without a pending exception; `XSaveErPtr`
advertises the unconditional behavior. The tested Ryzen/WSL host advertises
that feature, so the failures below must not simply be attributed to all AMD
CPUs. [Intel SDM](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/868137/325462-089-sdm-vol-1-2abcd-3abcd-4.pdf),
[AMD system programming manual, section 11.4.4.3](https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/sD1_QL~h4Afq2_tvzxqqSQ/content),
[AMD XSaveErPtr definition](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/processor-tech-docs/programmer-references/56255_OSRR.pdf).

`dos_fpu_capture_native` imports 32-bit FIP/FDP, FOP and the selectors from
the entry's FNSTENV snapshot. Both service and generic interrupt capture use
this helper. `dos_native_fp_return` exports a complete legacy environment
from the canonical client image. The final assembly restore first restores
the full vector/register image, then uses FNCLEX/FLDENV for compatibility
diagnostics; the saved control/status restore any client pending exception.
Host pointers with nonzero upper halves retain the 64-bit restore path.
The save sequence excludes maskable IRQs, restores the entry flags for host
C, and the final restore leaves IF clear until the assembly return tail.
There are no application names, synthetic success paths or vendor switches
in this change. General NMI ownership is not validated here.

The focused native selftest compares direct hardware restores against the
gate for full-width host pointers and legacy client selectors, including a
pending exception and a nested INT FFh. It also checks that preparing the
return does not rewrite the canonical 1024-byte image. Its four assertions
extend the existing matrix from 188,900,658 to **188,900,662** checks; these
are not 188 million newly added native-format cases. The final kernel reports
`failure-mask=0`, with pointer/selector coverage 7 on KVM and 0 on TCG. Zero

### 4.131 Real-mode TSR lifetime and global DOS file ownership

`INT 21h/AH=31h` now terminates with return type 3 while retaining the
current PSP allocation, its other owned blocks, environment, external JFT
and file references. The requested allocation has the DOS 3+ minimum of six
paragraphs. A failed resize leaves the existing allocation resident;
successful resizing updates PSP:0002. `INT 27h` rounds the byte offset up to
paragraphs, returns code zero and uses the caller's PSP. Both its direct
interrupt and PUSHF/CALL FAR ROM entry work; the bridge reads the checked
outer return CS instead of treating the ROM code segment as a PSP.
These size/return rules follow Microsoft's [MS-DOS process implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/MS-DOS/main/v4.0/src/DOS/PROC.ASM)
and [Function 31h documentation](https://www.pcjs.org/documents/books/mspl13/msdos/dosref40/).

The previous EXEC implementation saved and restored the entire SFT. That
rollback discarded files opened by resident descendants when a later child
or intermediate parent returned. EXEC now pins only entries referenced by
the suspended parent's actual JFT. Pins keep slots and their single host
file retain alive, without reverting positions, flags or reference counts
shared with other DOS processes. Normal termination closes the departing
PSP's complete JFT and releases its MCBs; resident termination does neither.
Failed loads only release inherited handles after acquisition succeeded.
Inheritance preflight counts duplicate entries before modifying counters,
so multiple aliases cannot wrap a nearly full 16-bit reference count.

Malformed guest JFTs remain untrusted: a forged alias can over-close an SFT,
but a pinned parent's slot cannot be recycled. On resumption its actual JFT
supplies the reference floor. A legitimate close made under the parent's
PSP is not resurrected. This is local hardening, not a claim that arbitrary
guest-written JFTs can always be repaired. VM destruction still closes all
SFT host references, including those held by resident code.

Build the six new COM fixtures with `make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 dos-tsr-test`.
`tsrtest.com` and `tsrload.com` cover EXEC 4B00/4B01 respectively. Each
executes AH=31h, INT 27h, the ROM call, and an intermediate parent which
leaves a resident grandchild. They check type/code consumption through
4Dh, PSP/MCB sizes and ownership, environment/extra blocks, inherited file
position, parent stdout, a retained handle at slot 31, and further file
reads after a normally terminating MZ child. These are real-mode programs;
default `dosrun` does not make them native protected-mode TSRs.

The in-kernel `[DOS-TSR]` suite adds 330 checks for sizes, failed growth,
rounding at FFFFh, protected-mode rejection, reference overflow, pinned
alias recovery, legitimate parent closes and final SFT cleanup.

The older `dosexec.com` fixture also needed a test correction, not a loader
change: its three FFFAh expectations were stale. For a 64-KiB COM stack,
DOS puts the zero return word at FFFEh, then the load-only initial AX at
FFFCh. This follows [MS-DOS EXEC](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/MS-DOS/main/v4.0/src/DOS/EXEC.ASM),
specifically `exec_read_com` and the no-execute return path. The frozen
pre-TSR kernel reproduces the old assertion failure with exit 16 after
1,212 instructions. The corrected fixture passes in software on KVM and
both software/native paths on TCG. KVM's existing native DPMI debug failure
still exits 7Ch in the child and 49 in the parent; `exec-audit.log` records
it as a known gap, not a conformance pass. The initial strict `exec.log`
failure is retained as well.

`a755224ccf1b794dff47acf3ee6f90158c45225adc393854488fc3b19e6faf1c`.
Both backends pass all six TSR commands and the 30 selected primary/unwind
EXEC commands. KVM's positive software EXEC command is separate from its
known native failure; TCG passes both. The negative kernel
`632efd7dfc0d4bbfb8f5c9255f308fb9fb61f25a8ba54236e6f85fec89c4f68f`

sequence. Earlier `baseline`/`initial` runs hit an overly restrictive file
sharing mode in the new fixture and are not valid TSR controls. The
`corrected` diagnostic run caught the missing INT 27h ROM source filter;
that failure is also preserved, not described as a final pass.

defines a separate resident-provider contract. [DPMI specifications](https://docs.pcjs.org/specs/dpmi/1991_03_12-DPMI_Spec_v10.pdf).

### 4.132 Independent native debug diagnosis and WSL KVM candidate

The native ICEBP failure from 4.42 is now reproduced without QEMU, Osito-K,
DPMI or a guest debugger. `test-dos-debug-native-host.sh` builds a Linux
`/dev/kvm` host program and a small 64-bit exception handler. Every case
creates a fresh 2-MiB, one-vCPU VM and reports the original hardware frame;
the handler neither repairs the saved RIP nor returns through it. No
`KVM_SET_GUEST_DEBUG` is used. Hardware breakpoint cases use the guest's
architectural debug registers through `KVM_SET_DEBUGREGS`.

The 120-case matrix crosses five profiles (64-bit CPL0/CPL3, compatibility
32-bit CPL0/CPL3, and compatibility CPL3 with nonzero CS base), two IDT gate
types, two stack paths (ordinary privilege stack / IST), and six causes:
plain ICEBP, 66h-prefixed ICEBP, adjacent ICEBP instructions, TF on a NOP
immediately before ICEBP, an instruction breakpoint, and a data breakpoint.
It checks saved RIP, CS, SS, SP, FLAGS and DR6 cause bits. Separately, a
Linux userspace SIGTRAP probe checks the same instruction outside KVM.

On `6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2-udmabuf+`, the final ordinary and traced
runs both produce:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Linux userspace ICEBP | Correct following RIP |
| KVM ICEBP forms | 60 failures: RIP remains 8000h, expected 8001h/8002h |
| KVM single-step / instruction / data breakpoints | 60 passes |

The process exits 1, not a conformance pass. The current instruction itself
is not enough to classify a debug exception: the successful TF case also
returns at an ICEBP, and the adjacent-ICEBP case legitimately needs to return
at another ICEBP. Do not add a general RIP increment to the DOS #DB handler.
The initial exploratory fixture incorrectly expected RF=1 for instruction
breakpoints; the final fixture follows the architectural exception for #DB,
which leaves setting RF for retry to the debugger. [Intel SDM, debug exceptions](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/850979/253669-087-sdm-vol-3b.pdf),
[AMD APM, RFLAGS](https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/sD1_QL~h4Afq2_tvzxqqSQ/content).

A private tracefs instance captures SVM exiting with `DB excp rip 0x8000`
before KVM injects #DB. Subsequent nested page faults during vectoring
reinject that event at the same RIP. Thus the incorrect address already
exists before guest exception delivery, independently of the DOS layer's
frame construction, selector base calculation, DR6 handling or QEMU. This
isolates the failure to the current nested KVM/SVM environment; it does not
establish which AMD/Hyper-V component first violates the trap semantics.
An earlier per-PID trace was empty and is not used as evidence.

`arch/x86/scripts/patches/wsl-6.6-kvm-svm-icebp.patch` is a candidate backport
of the [upstream SVM ICEBP interception fix](https://github.com/kvm-x86/linux/commit/ec9a16c6aeba8e19ce98c58a1ac255681a4dd0ac).
It targets WSL source `427645e3db3a8896714f22a3d3fe0c3f7b317ad4`. The new
instruction-specific intercept advances through the existing NextRIP/decoder
path before injecting #DB, leaving other debug causes alone. The backport
also preserves 6.6's instruction-skip failure return. Upstream describes a
task-gate failure; our reproducer uses only ordinary long-mode gates, so
the patch is a candidate for this environment, not a proven deployed fix.

`git apply --check` passes against the untouched WSL source. An isolated
copy of `svm.c` compiles with the exact saved GCC flags and generated headers
of that kernel, including `-Werror`. This is translation-unit validation
only: no full kernel was linked, installed or booted. The original WSL source,
running kernel and `.wslconfig` were not edited. Manual impact covers only
new diagnostic entry points and the proposed `init_vmcb`, ICEBP handler and
SVM dispatch-table change; GitNexus was unavailable. No DOS kernel function
was changed in this follow-up.

```bash
git -C /root/src/WSL2-Linux-Kernel apply --check \
```

The software failure needs a focused IRQ-return regression. The software
locked-stack IRET currently targets the host's executable return stub,
whereas the native alias is retired directly by
`dos_pm_interrupt_return_iret()`. IRQ admission between the software IRET
and the private return INT can therefore retain the previous frame.
Repeated hardware-reflector entries precede the observed exhaustion.
This is a code-supported diagnosis, not a verified fix or proof that the
host patch caused the software failure. The tested kernel is unchanged.

overlapping snapshots plus the initial capture retain the full API record.
The original 3,600-second checker timed out before completion, and its

regression suite starts only after that verification and an idle prompt.
The final API UART snapshot has pending zero, 63,654 dropped bytes and 7,317
flush timeouts. The UART contains 147 matrix headers versus 184 in klog:
37 successful headers were missing on the wire. API correctness here is

### 4.135 Atomic software DPMI interrupt return

`dos_pm_interrupt_return_iret()` now recognizes the software host-owned
return selector as well as the native private alias. It finishes the locked
frame inside the validated IRET transaction, before the next IRQ admission
point. It does not wait for execution of the private INT at offset 0150h.
The host selector must retain HOST ownership, the return address must match,
and the existing stack-balance and destination checks remain mandatory.
Guest-IDT operation is excluded. There is no IRQ masking workaround, larger
stack limit or application-specific branch.

The RF regression now requires restoration after one IRET. Added cases
force 34 consecutive STI/IRET returns with 16/32-bit clients and stacks,
virtual IF clear/set, and an already-nested interrupt. Rejection cases check
that invalid stack/destination/ownership and foreign return targets leave
CPU registers, depth and virtual IF unchanged. The IRQ matrix contains 152
cases; the complete RF suite also retains native-alias and RF/TF coverage.

Build: `make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 build/kernel.elf`.
The corrected binary is 6,694,960 bytes, SHA256
`81956134dce8ddd86f7324c39c2729696eb9e2d723758c3043f604dbb4f3a72b`.
The numeric-object audit still passes 73 objects / 12,122 instructions with
no FP/SIMD operations, external numeric symbols or native fallback.

`dos-irq-return-direct-20260913` validates this binary on a disposable direct
QEMU 10.2.0 KVM VM with 8 GiB / four CPUs. This uses the unchanged active WSL
host, not the candidate Linux host. The full RF suite passes, including
IRQ 152/0 and native-alias 296/0. Twenty-nine additional probes pass across
software EXEC, single-step, handoff, IRET, raw-client routing, debug routing,
software frames and recovery before/after DOOM. Explicit software-only
selection excludes native executable probes; it does not relax their oracles
or reinterpret the original host's known ICEBP failure.

Software DOOM (`-config audio.cfg -nomusic`) reaches over 700 million
instructions, displays animated gameplay, accepts F10/Y and returns exit 0
to the shell. The first checker returned 1 because this QEMU was built
without PNG support. A separately archived observer attached to the same

This verifies output signal, not subjective audio fidelity or music support.
PE32 SEH3/SEH4 and software FLAGS probes also pass after game teardown.

PIT period, virtual IF, pending IRQ and PIC state. It does not print from the
probe, record every timer poll, change device semantics or alter the VM ABI.

a QMP memory copy is not presumed atomic. Live reads use CPU1's kernel CR3.

### 4.141. Event-driven xHCI polling and USB DOOM recovery

`evt_poll` previously wrote IMAN and read USBSTS on every call, even with no
DMA events. DOS invokes this common input path during interrupt service;
the shell, compositor and Win32 message loop also use it. GitNexus tooling
was unavailable, so this caller scope was checked manually. No DOS CPU,
PIC, PIT, guest executable or interrupt-admission policy changes accompany
this correction.

The poller now probes the volatile event cycle in coherent memory first.
An empty ring performs an MMIO health check at most once per 100 ms, while
ready events bypass that deadline. Halt/error detection remains active, and
IE/INTE remain enabled. The DMA acquire barrier follows ownership detection.
EINT is acknowledged before IP; ERDP is written once per bounded batch of
up to 16 events, naming the last consumed entry or the cycle-mismatch entry
when empty, never an unconsumed valid entry. Empty health checks do not
rewrite ERDP. These rules follow
[xHCI 1.2b, sections 4.9.4, 4.17.2, 5.4.2 and 5.5.2.3.3](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/625472/625472_xHCI_Rev1_2b.pdf).
This limits idle register traffic, not USB input or guest IRQ frequency.

`test-xhci-poll.sh` compiles the production driver with recorded MMIO and the
real HID parser under GCC and Clang. Both pass: 100,000 empty calls without
MMIO; the zero-time/100 ms boundary; ready-event bypass; EINT/IP order;
40-event batching; event/transfer ring wrap; arrival during IP/ERDP writes;
reentrant polling; keyboard make/break and short completions; and halted or
faulted controllers. The touched header is normalized to LF; its semantic
change is three register definitions and two per-controller status fields.

Closed evidence: `~/.local/share/osito-k/test-evidence/xhci-idle-20260914`.

`83047456ec9af5f655a8b0a2f0686666d42b1856edf0f2b4ffc6d96ad35da97a`.

The cause is a dependency on free application DOS MCB space in the console
translator, not evidence that the preceding VBE LFB operations failed.
`dos_load_com_process` normally gives a COM program the largest available
block. `dpmi_dos_console` subsequently tries to obtain its temporary stack
and buffer from that same arena. `dpmi_dos_file_io` has a related allocation
dependency to address in the same ownership review. The next fix should
provide host-managed translation storage with nested-call ownership,
bounded copying, real-mode hook behavior and correct EXEC/exit cleanup.
It must not require shrinking this test or accepting its zero exit as success.
The [MS-DOS API Extensions for DPMI Hosts, sections 5, 6 and 8](https://docs.pcjs.org/specs/dpmi/1991_03_11-MSDOS_DPMI_EXTENSIONS.pdf)
assign copying and pointer translation to the host; callers use protected
selectors and need not manage the real-mode transfer buffers themselves.
