### 4.143 Host-owned DOS transfer storage

The console-allocation defect from 4.142 is corrected in the shared DPMI
console/file translator. Temporary storage no longer competes with a COM
program's conventional DOS MCB allocation. The kernel is 6,707,384 bytes,
SHA256 `2d3610914f2e679c310da31b6f488afcb282cfdba526b028b21a86f8db6a3f7d`,
built with `CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 DOS_IRQ_TRACE=0`.

GitNexus is unavailable. Manual impact review covers the console/file
translators, EXEC save/restore, VM teardown and their regression tests.
The new Makefile target only builds test COMs; the running kernel is frozen.

`dos_transfer_acquire` manages a VM-private 64 KiB real-mode window at
C0000h-CFFFFh. This range is unused in the current emulated platform; it is
not an adapter ROM mapping or a specification-mandated address. Compile-time
guards exclude VGA, the XMS/DOS UMB pool, EMS and host ROM. Payloads prefer
16 KiB chunks, with a 4 KiB real-mode stack per outstanding call. A smaller
free extent can satisfy a splittable transfer. Exhausting this finite pool
returns DOS error 8; the implementation does not claim unbounded nesting.

Reservation metadata and copy snapshots remain kernel-owned. Monotonic
generation IDs reject stale or repeated releases after address reuse. EXEC
records the generation checkpoint, preserves older parent reservations and
reclaims child calls on restoration; final VM teardown reclaims everything.
The existing pointer validation, page-fault repair, real-mode hooks, partial
I/O, FLAGS and console-line semantics are retained. No application name or
test-specific bypass selects this path.

The new `[DOS-TRANSFER]` matrix passes all 63 checks: exhausted conventional
memory, alignment and chunk sizes, gaps, nested allocation, clean exhaustion,
reuse, generation overflow, scrubbing, MCB integrity and region boundaries.
The existing EXEC continuation matrices still pass 137 checks each, with
additional parent/child reservation assertions in their ownership cases.
The I/O service matrix retains its 13,648 checks and 928 recovery cases,
with no pending transfer reservations after a call. Large-transfer fixtures
use the new provider's chunk boundary rather than an available-MCB estimate.

Evidence is in
`~/.local/share/osito-k/test-evidence/dos-transfer-v1-20260914`; the frozen
payload is in `~/.local/share/osito-k/host-builds/dos-transfer-v1-20260914`.
Unassisted boot reaches JIT PASS (13,620 instructions) and an idle shell in
96.550 seconds. All six runs of the unchanged console probes now pass, including

runs also pass: normal USE16/USE32 and software USE32, each with retained or
released conventional memory. They verify a 20 KiB NUL write across chunks,
NUL read EOF, close, protected console output and exit 42.
`make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 dos-file-pressure-test` builds the four new COMs;
their bytes match the running fixtures. Independent extraction confirms that
all 244 original disk files remain unchanged and exactly those four files
were added. The original `dpmi_vbe.com` now prints its required PASS and
exits 00h without being modified or shrinking its DOS arena.

RF passes the same 11 exact matrices. API passes 185 exact matrices in

All 47 groups complete, with 2,230.698 seconds of aggregate group time.
The untouched live checker records 247 passes and five failures. One is a

### 4.144. Cross-route x87 diagnostic regression controls

The four remaining native diagnostic failures are not repaired or removed
from the oracle. This follow-up adds independent guest comparisons and repeats
the Linux/WSL control from 4.130 using the current environment. The production
kernel remains byte-identical to 4.143, SHA256
`2d3610914f2e679c310da31b6f488afcb282cfdba526b028b21a86f8db6a3f7d`.
No DOS production source, native admission policy or active WSL kernel was changed.

`test/dpmi_x87_diagnostic.S` deliberately does not require FXSAVE, SSE or AVX.
Four 32-bit-code COMs cover 16/32-bit stacks and masked/pending x87 exceptions;
a fifth real-mode COM changes the register file before exiting as an EXEC child.
The parent seeds exact FIP/FDP/FOP/FCS/FDS fields and rejects an unaccepted
seed. It compares every defined environment field and all 80 register bytes,
excluding reserved environment words. Its 135 snapshots cover the seed,
64 DPMI/DOS service pairs, four raw PM/RM round trips, 100,000 CPUIDs and a
fifth round trip containing EXEC. The upper ESP sentinel is checked with the

| Interpreter, `--emulate --max-steps 2000000` | 4 | 0 | 135 samples each, over 400,000 interpreted instructions |
| JIT, `--emulate` | 4 | 0 | 135 samples each, over 300,000 JIT PM instructions |
| Native | 0 | 4 | Cases `1E`, `3E`, `2E`, `2E`; exit 71h and shell recovery |

All eight software runs execute the child and all five raw round trips.
The native masked cases lose FIP/FDP/FOP and both selectors; pending cases

The four original numerical state probes still pass.

The unchanged `test/dos_fpu_native_host.c`, compiled separately with GCC and

independent reproduction rules out attributing the entire problem to the DOS
bridge, but does not identify Hyper-V, WSL/KVM scheduling or hardware as the

4.130; no vendor hardcode or synthetic restoration of lost state was added.

`dos-fpu-test` still reports `188900662 failures=0`, native gate failure mask

The full 47-group suite and DOOM were not rerun in this test-only follow-up;

The closed audit verifies all command spans, decoder events, native failures,

### 4.145. Process-owned thread teardown across identical PEB VAs

After the xHCI private-stack DMA fix, Steam advanced on the P1 and then the
machine stopped responding locally and over SSH. The following cold boot's
saved diagnostics were recovered in
`arch/x86/build/p1-steam-reset-diag-20260926-r1/`; the previous boot ends at
`winexec-start`. It does not contain the final fault. The earlier live tail
reached `SteamServiceTmp.exe /Update`, which alone does not identify a cause.

An isolated USB-storage QEMU run with the same kernel reproduced a concrete
Win32 teardown defect while Steam's `steamsysinfo.exe` child exited. Both
processes have PEB VA `0x4000002000`, in different address spaces.
`win32_terminate_process_threads` selected threads by PEB pointer equality,
so child exit also terminated a parent-owned worker. TLS cleanup then read
the parent's private vector using the child's CR3 and faulted at
`win64_tls_detach_thread+665`. Evidence, including registers and the saved
fault, is in `arch/x86/build/steam-usb-freeze-qemu-20260926-r4/`.

The internal teardown contract now accepts the Win32 process ID. All three
call sites (normal child exit, forced child termination and main-process
cleanup) pass their explicit owner ID; selection uses `ctx->owner_pid`.
No Steam-specific path, address or process name is part of the fix. This
does not claim to audit every foreign-address-space TLS/reaper path.

`test/thread_owner_pe64.c` builds parent and child probes. They verify the
same PEB VA, create a worker in each process, exit the child, require the
parent worker to remain active, then signal and join it with its expected
exit code. `OSITO_SSH_TEST_THREAD_OWNER=1` selects this focused test in
`scripts/test-ssh-qemu.sh`; it can use either supported test storage mode.

- `build/thread-owner-before-20260926-r1/`: old kernel stops both workers;
  the parent reports `THREAD-OWNER64 FAIL 07`. This is an expected negative
  baseline, not a passing run.
- `build/thread-owner-after-20260926-r1/`: the same probe passes on USB, and
  authenticated SSH still responds after both processes finish.

The tested candidate is 7,151,008 bytes, SHA-256
`8706df69ef1ef22dbaa400432029bdb47c607bb437fddc27a76c397178992cd5`.
The repeated Steam diagnostic in
`build/steam-usb-owner-fixed-qemu-20260926-r1/` no longer shows that TLS page
fault. SSH still answers at 180 seconds. Steam itself raises an application
fatal-exit exception (`0x40000015`), so this is not a successful Steam UI test.
The QEMU payload and physical P1 installation are not identical; their
different startup paths must not be treated as equivalent reproductions.

The candidate was uploaded to `/kernel-thread-owner-20260926.elf`, installed
with `kupdate --file ... --no-kexec` (both OsitoFS and EFI verified), then
booted with `kexec`. Wi-Fi and SSH returned automatically. Deployment logs
are `build/p1-thread-owner-{upload,install,kexec}-20260926.log`.

The physical Steam retest still lost SSH while loading children. The host
saved two complete `dmesg` responses and a third partial response in
`build/p1-steam-thread-owner-retest-20260926-r1/`. The partial log includes
`steamerrorreporter64.exe` (PID 2), `steamwebhelper.exe` (PID 3), a scheduled
`SteamService.exe /RunAsService` (PID 4), and the beginning of PID 3's PE64
thunk allocations. It contains no final CPU exception or new xHCI fatal
message; absence from a partial capture does not exclude either. The third
read stalls after 98,277 stdout bytes, and subsequent connections time out.
The last emitted allocation is not evidence that allocation caused the hang.

The ownership regression is fixed and tested, but the physical P1 lockup
remains unresolved. GitNexus was unavailable; manual impact covered the
selector and all three references. No broader TLS/reaper correctness or
successful Steam startup is claimed.

The user subsequently confirmed a completely unresponsive machine for about
30 minutes, with no on-screen exception, then cold-rebooted it. An opt-in
[AP/NMI stall diagnostic](x86-lockup-diagnostics.md) was implemented and
validated separately. Its idle sample works on the P1; a new monitored Steam
run again lost SSH after scheduling `SteamServiceTmp.exe /Update`. The saved
host log is not a CPU snapshot, and the visible NMI report must be collected
before assigning a cause to that lockup.

### 4.146 Private I/O guards caused the P1 Steam lockup (2026-09-26)

The physical NMI photograph now identifies an IRQ-off spin in
`file_lock_cancel_waiters+0x52`, RIP `FFFF8000021C1D12`, on the exact kernel
SHA-256 `4202d369d566208b07e0ad7239f28a064af8a80c8a92a26be30dee230d5ffc5d`.
R12 is `g_file_range_lock`; FLAGS is `200002`, CR3 `981F6000`, and the last
fault address is `4000A2E778`. Full transcription and limitations are in
[the lockup diagnostic record](x86-lockup-diagnostics.md).

`NtReadFile` and `NtWriteFile` placed `NT_FILE_IO_GUARD` on their callers'
stacks. `nt_file_io_guard_begin` linked that address into a global list. A
Win32 shim runs on a process-private PE64 stack; another process's CR3 can
leave the address unmapped or map unrelated contents at the same VA. A scan
of this list can therefore fault while holding the range-lock spinlock.
Non-local process exception cleanup then tries to cancel file locks and
spins forever reacquiring that lock with IRQs disabled. A timeout or forced
unlock would not make the list valid.

The manager now allocates resident kernel entries before taking its lock.
Only a unique opaque cookie remains on the private stack. Global traversal,
unlink and process retirement use kernel-owned memory. End is idempotent;
old cookies cannot remove a later allocation, and cookie exhaustion fails
without wrapping. Failed allocation/conflicting lock/zero-length paths do
not publish a node. Allocations, frees and completion callbacks stay outside
the spinlock. The public Windows API and byte-range conflict rules do not
change, and there is no application-specific branch.

Process handle cleanup retires abandoned guards after workers stop and
pending lock requests are cancelled. Final environment release repeats the
retirement defensively for early forced child exit. Neither path reads the
old private cookie. This narrowly fixes guard ownership; it does not claim
to audit all in-flight I/O cancellation, file-object lifetime, or user-buffer
fault unwinding in the compatibility layer.

Evidence:

- `build/filelock-negative-20260926-r1/`: the old manager faults in
  `file_lock_conflicts_locked` when the issuing guard page becomes
  inaccessible. ASan identifies the read at guard+8.
- `build/fileguard-negative-qemu-20260926-r2/`: the exact physical kernel,
  separate PE64 CR3s and a private guard at `6000000000`. The NMI captures
  `RIP=FFFF8000021C1D12`, `FLAGS=2`, `CR2=6000000008`. This is the expected
  negative baseline, not a successful application run. The initial r1
  harness read the frame's error-code offset instead of RIP; r2 corrects
  that test-only offset and preserves the full failing-kernel result.
- `bash arch/x86/scripts/test-filelock.sh`: GCC/Clang normal and ASan/UBSan,
  18,550 checks per final variant (`build/filelock-host-20260926-r3/`). Tests
  inaccessible/aliased private tokens, range boundaries, read/write conflicts,
  queued grants/cancellation with reentrant completion, allocation failure,
  cookie exhaustion, owner-filtered retirement, late end and reclamation.
  The initial host harness exported `sched_yield` and could collide with the
  sanitizer runtime; its stub now has a test-private name.
- `build/fileguard-qemu-20260926-r1/`: corrected kernel on USB storage,
  two parent/child cycles with distinct CR3s, a conflicting range denied
  while I/O is active and granted afterwards, and process exit after the
  private token is unmapped. QMP verifies both global lists are empty.
  The existing native `win32-file-test` and PE32 file-lock contract pass,
  and authenticated SSH remains available afterward.

The QEMU-only fixture obtains internal SysV function addresses from its exact
ELF. It must not be run on a physical installation. Test runners use managed
scratch disks and stop their VM even on failure.

Candidate: 7,164,208 bytes, SHA-256
`45c57470cfed528667ae1fed5a4db05abad699b52d0bc7db435f590af3ba9671`.
The same binary also passes the USB same-PEB teardown regression in
`build/fileguard-owner-qemu-20260926-r1/`.

It was uploaded as `/kernel-fileguard-20260926.elf`. Two standard 32-KiB
SSH uploads closed unexpectedly while the machine remained responsive;
a local diagnostic wrapper splitting only W requests into 4-KiB pieces
completed, keeping the existing full SHA-256 verification. This is not a
transport fix or a performance claim. `kupdate --file ... --no-kexec`
verified both the OsitoFS and EFI copies, then `kexec` restarted the P1.
Wi-Fi and SSH returned automatically. Deployment logs are
`build/p1-fileguard-{upload-20260926-small,install-20260926}.log` and
`build/p1-fileguard-afterboot-20260926.log`. The remote kexec session itself
ended without captured stdout; the subsequent fresh boot log is the evidence
of return, not that transport disconnect alone.

The monitored physical Steam rerun in
`build/p1-steam-fileguard-retest-20260926-r1/` completed all 18 dmesg polls
and periodic ps requests, extending past the old freeze point. At the next
status query the watchdog was still armed with no captured stall
(`build/p1-fileguard-watchdog-20260926.log`). The final console query reports
Steam still running, not returned to the shell.

New, separate failures are now observable without losing the whole machine:
Steam Service repeatedly fails its pipe/load path and spawns update/service
children; `gldriverquery64.exe` (Win32 PID 21) calls address zero with return
address `1400B73AE`. Its child teardown completes and logs VM reclamation.
These are follow-up compatibility problems, not proof that the Steam UI
has started or that all possible kernel hangs are fixed.

The observer subsequently expired normally after its bounded 300-second
window: state=4, observer_running=0, no NMI snapshot, with live ticks and
switches (`build/p1-fileguard-watchdog-final-20260926.log`). SSH remained
available for a later full log and screen download. The checked 1920x1080
GOP capture `build/p1-steam-fileguard-20260926.png` shows the desktop and
fault messages, not a Steam window. Snapshot uptime was 186,613 ms; the
4-KiB stop-and-wait transfer took 147.281 seconds for 101,973 compressed wire
bytes (6,220,800 decoded RGB bytes, SHA-256
`c4eec2d8e3b77ebefaf3f0fda57b6938a9f40cb59d01657624543de336bb5cb7`).

The later `build/p1-steam-fileguard-late-20260926.log` preserves the next
failures: a NULL call returning into `libcef.dll+13D104B` (owner 3), then
`win64_tls_detach_thread` at `FFFF80000220C989` on the exact new ELF.
The latter runs as reaper PID/TGID 7 with kernel CR3 `983FF000`, attempting
to read private TLS address `40017F2000`. This differs from the earlier
same-PEB wrong-process selection regression, which still passes; the reaper
address-space/lifetime path remains to be corrected. Steam Service continues
retrying, and the log also records missing PE32 thunk metadata for
`WININET.dll!InternetReadFile`. None of these follow-ups is silently treated
as a successful Steam launch.

GitNexus was unavailable (no tool or CLI). Manual impact covered all guard
begin/end references (disk read/write in `ntsyscall.c`), the manager's waiter
traversal, and callers of the two process-cleanup hooks in `winexec.c`.
Scheduler, IRQ handling, storage transport, lock retry policy and Steam
parameters are unchanged by the fix.

### 4.147. P1 Steam NULL imports and private TLS reaping (2026-09-27)

The three faults after the file-guard correction have separate causes. The
exact deployed ELF is `build/fileguard-qemu-20260926-r1/kernel.elf`, SHA-256
`45c57470cfed528667ae1fed5a4db05abad699b52d0bc7db435f590af3ba9671`.

- `gldriverquery64.exe` calls NULL with return address `1400B73AE`. Disassembly
  shows an indirect call through IAT `1400B8368`, whose import is
  `MSVCR120.dll!_ismbblead`. This happens in command-line parsing, before a
  conclusion about GPU initialization can be drawn.
- CEF calls NULL with return address `1813D104B`. The instruction at
  `1813D1045` calls IAT `18C8C7E68`, identified by the PE import directory as
  `KERNEL32.dll!QueryProcessCycleTime`. The local libcef image matches the
  logged base `180000000` and size `D3CA000`; its timestamp is `1721069550`.
  The caller checks the BOOL result and branches to a failure path.
- The subsequent group termination makes the reaper retire Win32 workers.
  `win64_tls_detach_thread` at `FFFF80000220C989` reads private TLS VA
  `40017F2000` while reaper PID/TGID 7 uses kernel CR3 `983FF000`. The source
  vector belongs to owner 3 / CR3 `98224000`. The reaper itself dies; the
  later physical `ps` snapshot (`build/p1-pagefault-ps-20260927.log`) confirms
  its ZOMBIE state and accumulation of unreaped tasks.

The TLS vector-release helpers now use the immutable `ctx->owner_cr3` and
`paging_copy_between_cr3` to read and clear target slots before freeing their
blocks. No CR3 switch, process-identity substitution or guest callback occurs
on the abnormal-cleanup path. Scheduler peer ordering in `proc_free` already
keeps the target page tables alive until these thread cleanups complete.
An inaccessible slot is logged and not dereferenced or freed speculatively.
This is not a general audit of corrupted TLS pointers, forced-thread-exit
locks, or all process-wide resource retirement paths.

`_ismbblead` is exported with one cdecl argument and implements the invariant
C/POSIX single-byte locale already exposed by `setlocale`; no DBCS locale or
`_setmbcp` support is claimed. `QueryProcessCycleTime` is exported with two
stdcall arguments, validates the output argument and process-handle type,
ownership and query access, and returns FALSE / ERROR_CALL_NOT_IMPLEMENTED
without changing the output for a valid unsupported measurement. It does not
invent CPU cycles from uptime. Real per-process CPU accounting remains open;
the pre-existing `QueryThreadCycleTime` approximation is unchanged.
The PE32 gateway zero-extends arguments, so the current-process pseudo-handle
is normalized from `FFFFFFFF` only for a compat32 caller.

Contracts consulted:
[Microsoft _ismbblead](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/c-runtime-library/reference/ismbblead-ismbblead-l)
and [QueryProcessCycleTime](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/realtimeapiset/nf-realtimeapiset-queryprocesscycletime).

Validation:

- `build/tls-reap-negative-20260927-r3/` uses the exact old ELF and reproduces
  the reaper fault at the exact same RIP `FFFF80000220C989`, now accessing the
  fixture's private slot `4000442038`. SSH observes the reaper become ZOMBIE.
  Earlier r1 stopped at a fixture link error; r2 revealed that the current
  shell starts the reaper only after `desktop`. Neither was counted as a
  successful negative reproduction.
- `build/tls-reap-positive-20260927-r1/` passes the corrected kernel: a real
  PE64 child registers static TLS, returns normally once, and then has three
  workers stopped through the scheduler's abnormal-exit path. The actual
  reaper releases each private TLS environment, signals the thread handles,
  and stays live. Attach/detach callback counts verify that forced cleanup
  does not execute guest callbacks. No page fault or inaccessible-slot log.
- The same run checks all byte inputs plus out-of-range values for
  `_ismbblead`, process-query access masks, invalid handles, NULL output,
  unsupported-cycle error, and unchanged output storage.
- `build/pagefault-fileguard-regression-20260927-r1/` passes both cross-CR3
  file-guard cycles, the native NT file contract and the PE32 file-lock test.
- `build/pagefault-contracts-20260927-r3/` repeats the PE64 cleanup and API
  tests on the final kernel, and passes 300 repeated PE32 static-import
  calls through both cdecl and stdcall thunks. The first combined run (r2)
  failed its PE32 check and exposed the pseudo-handle normalization omission;
  that failure was fixed, not waived.
- `build/pagefault-owner-regression-20260927-r1/` passes the same-PEB-VA
  child-exit isolation test again on the final ELF.

The corrected kernel is 7,164,400 bytes, SHA-256
`f9be44f6074c754fc8752a86fa2c292e638a05da7548e5966300c5a237c7648d`.
The initial PE64-only and file-guard runs used the earlier image ending in
`56f8f897`; only the new API's PE32 pseudo-handle handling changed afterward.
The QEMU-only fixture receives internal SysV entry addresses from that run's
ELF; it must not be run on the physical development machine. Kernel build and
`git diff --check` pass. The initial deployment was blocked by the P1's busy
console (request 2); the user subsequently restarted it. These test results
do not claim that Steam launches or that its other unresolved imports are fixed.

The attempted SSH file-sync push to `/kernel-pagefault-20260927.elf` acknowledged

`build/p1-pagefault-upload-20260927.log`; use the frozen final QEMU ELF for the
next upload after a physical restart has released the busy console.

(`build/p1-pagefault-upload-20260927-r2.log`). `kupdate --file

### 4.148. P1 renderer capability and CEF CPU-cycle fatal (2026-09-27)

The two failures left by 4.147 have now been traced separately. The exact
`gldriverquery64.exe` initializer first resolves and calls `glGetString` for
`GL_VERSION`; a NULL result exits the initializer before it ever populates
the `glDisable` slot. On a GOP-only machine the shim had published a WGL
context without a renderer, then exposed Mesa entry points without a native
Mesa context. Adding another `glDisable` export would not fix that contract.

WGL context creation now requires a real rendering backend and a successful
native context allocation. No backend returns NULL / ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED;
invalid DCs and allocation failures also fail without publishing a context.
Pixel-format queries no longer advertise OpenGL, double buffering or a GDI
software renderer when none exists. `glGetString` without a current context
returns NULL. This does not add a native NVIDIA or software OpenGL driver.
The existing Venus success path still needs a separate accelerated regression.

`build/p1-cef-log-20260927.txt`, retrieved through SSH file-sync while Steam
held the foreground console, identifies the other failure as
`FATAL:process_metrics_win.cc(191)] Check failed: false`. The current records
are at the start of this reused log; its tail also contains older runs.
Disassembly of the actual CEF DLL shows `QueryProcessCycleTime` at
`1813D1045`, the FALSE branch at `1813D10F3`, and the fatal logger receiving
line 191 (`R9D=BF`). INT3 `18691AD97` is the logger's no-handler fatal path,
not the adjacent libc++ string-view assertion. Returning unsupported in
4.147 avoided a NULL import call but did not satisfy Chromium's requirement
that this query work for a valid process handle. See the corresponding
[Chromium 126 CPU metric implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/126.0.6478.183/base/process/process_metrics_win.cc).

The BSP scheduler now accounts task runtime in TSC ticks at current-task and
state transitions, with a snapshot of the currently executing slice. Blocked
time and unrelated tasks are not charged. The ledger is out-of-line so the
existing `process_t` layout remains unchanged. NT thread objects bind to a
kernel task before it becomes runnable, freeze the count at termination,
and transfer it into their owner's retired total when the object is released.
Queries include both live and retired threads. The legacy primary NT object
spans successive shell launches; its cumulative total is retained, but the
shell time between launches is excluded. AP compute jobs are not accounted
to Win32 tasks. `GetProcessTimes`/`GetThreadTimes` approximations are unchanged.

`QueryProcessCycleTime` and `QueryThreadCycleTime` now use this ledger, validate
handle ownership/type/query rights, and normalize their respective PE32
pseudo-handles. The NT object-type mismatch translation is ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE.
Contracts: [process cycles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/realtimeapiset/nf-realtimeapiset-queryprocesscycletime)
and [thread cycles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/realtimeapiset/nf-realtimeapiset-querythreadcycletime).

Validation on isolated QEMU USB disks:

- `build/wgl-helper-negative-20260927-r1/` reproduces the exact NULL call with
  return address `1400B6E57` using the old kernel and real Steam helper/module.

### 4.149. CEF worker identity and non-faulting diagnostic reads (2026-09-27)

The next two physical failures are not the old WGL or CPU-query problems:

- `chrome_elf.dll+73424` reports INT3 immediately after a failed VirtualFree
  MEM_DECOMMIT. Disassembly of the actual DLL identifies the one-page
  decommit wrapper and its GetLastError/error-breakpoint path. The worker is
  running under CR3 `8A8A9000`, but module diagnostics attribute it to the
  earlier webhelper process (NT PID 5, CR3 `9820F000`).
- An error-reporter worker later calls `chrome_elf.dll+7E8F0` with
  DLL_THREAD_ATTACH, although its private CR3 `98014000` does not map that
  DLL. The diagnostic code then dereferences the same unmapped RIP while
  printing code bytes, producing a second #PF in isr_handler. The saved
  report therefore describes the diagnostic fault rather than the original
  foreign DLL callback.

`win32_current_child()` used the current TEB's PEB pointer to identify worker
ownership. All PE64 children place their PEB at virtual address `4000002000`
in separate address spaces, so the first matching child won. The existing
primary-task kernel PID check remains; workers now resolve through their
immutable process ID in the scheduler-thread context. Memory ownership,
handle checks and DLL callback selection receive the correct process without
changing scheduler selection or private address-space layout.

The expanded ordinary PE64 owner fixture keeps one child alive while a
second child's worker checks GetCurrentProcessId, decommits its own page,
recommits it, verifies zero contents, and releases it. Earlier parent-exit
and survivor checks remain. `build/p1-worker-identity-negative-20260927-r1/`
reproduces FAIL 11 (wrong worker process ID) on the deployed f995 kernel;
`build/p1-worker-identity-positive-20260927-r2/` passes on the final kernel.
This proves the identity defect locally. Its role in the physical CEF
decommit/callback failures still needs a corrected hardware rerun.

Fatal exception diagnostics now resolve code, stack words and frame links
through the active CR3 before reading via the physical map. Unmapped,
noncanonical or overflowing addresses terminate that portion of the dump.
Word reads crossing a page boundary are conservatively omitted. Existing
stack/frame bounds remain. This does not make absent pages readable or
swallow the application's original exception.

The new nonprivileged PE32/PE64 fixtures run as children with private page
tables. They call a reserved, uncommitted page and separately execute INT3
in the final byte of a committed page, leaving the saved RIP on an unmapped
page. The initial correction exposed another raw dereference in the compat
EBP walker; stack/frame reads are now guarded too. Validation:

- `build/p1-fault-read-negative-20260927-r2/` reproduces nested exceptions for
  all four cases on the f995 kernel.
- `build/p1-fault-read-positive-20260927-r3/` records exactly one original
  exception per case, prints `<unmapped>`, terminates the child, and returns
  the launcher to the shell with exit code 0. SSH remains available. Win32
  child recovery occurs before the generic crash-file path, so this test
  does not require or claim a separate crash summary file.
- `build/p1-worker-identity-cycles-20260927-r1/` passes the PE32 and PE64 CPU
  accounting contracts on this final image, including rights and lifetimes.
- `build/p1-worker-identity-tls-20260927-r1/` passes PE32 imports and the
  private-address-space TLS normal/forced-exit and reaper regressions.
- `build/p1-worker-identity-wgl-20260927-r1/` passes both no-renderer WGL
  contracts; the real Steam GL helper exits with code 2 without an exception.

All five final-image QEMU runs use isolated USB scratch images and finish
with SSH responsive. The kernel builds with only the existing packed-TSS
member warnings in idt.c; `git diff --check` passes.

The final image is 7,168,992 bytes, SHA-256
`8d707e811c06fcd7f02a21b1e74f2894c0a67d6fa3c492f7c67da72d1ec30988`,
frozen in `build/p1-fault-read-positive-20260927-r3/kernel.elf`. At this point
it is not deployed: the P1 stopped responding after Steam was closed, and
the user was asked to restart into the shell. GitNexus is unavailable; manual
impact analysis covered current-child consumers and all changed diagnostic
read sites in the shared exception handler. No Steam-specific success stub
or application argument workaround was added.

### 4.150. GL helper duplicate-free provenance (2026-09-27)

While the P1 remained unreachable, two QEMU/GDB runs traced the caught
`HEAP-INVALID-FREE` left by 4.148. Both use the unchanged 8d707e kernel and
real `gldriverquery64.exe` with no renderer. Evidence is in
`build/helper-free-gdb-20260927-r1/heap-gdb.log` and
`build/helper-free-gdb-20260927-r2/heap-gdb.log`.

The first run breaks at `heap_trace_invalid`. The second breaks at crt_free
for the same run's allocation `4000242270` before each free. The first call
returns to `14004456D`, after the helper's window-creation error path calls
its platform destructor `140044030`. That destructor frees driver data via
the guest's free trampoline `14001F530`. The later generic window destructor
calls the same platform destructor again, with crt_free returning to
`140015D2A`. The block tag is valid before the first free and zero before
the second; the driver-data pointer in the helper remains unchanged. This
is a duplicate cleanup in the embedded helper code, not a second free
performed spontaneously by Osito-K's CRT.

The helper returns code 2, with no exception or corrupted heap in these
runs. Keep the heap guard and no-renderer capability reporting intact; no
binary patch, fake GL context, or successful duplicate-free result was
introduced to hide the diagnostic. The pixel-format best-match result alone
does not promise all requested attributes: callers must inspect the actual
format, per [ChoosePixelFormat](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-choosepixelformat).
This does not explain or resolve the later physical Steam freeze.

### 4.151. CEF AttachConsole and startup handle contract (2026-09-27)

The full Steam USB/QEMU run on the 8d707e image reaches CEF children, beyond
the earlier process-cycle fatal. `build/steam-worker-identity-qemu-20260927-r1/`
captures a NULL instruction fetch from `libcef.dll+68F6736`: the preceding
instruction calls IAT entry `libcef+0C8C75C0` with ECX=FFFFFFFF. The PE import
table identifies that entry as `kernel32!AttachConsole`, which was absent.
A separate framebuffer-visible fault at `FFFF80000227FE81` resolves to the
call of spi_trace_nonclient from SystemParametersInfoW. Its full frame was
not available in that serial log; it must not be attributed to stack growth
or buffer corruption without more evidence.

AttachConsole now checks the calling process's existing association, a live
target's console state, and the recorded parent PID for ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS.
It returns ACCESS_DENIED, INVALID_HANDLE, or INVALID_PARAMETER for their
distinct failure cases, and updates both native and compat PEB parameters
after a successful association. Child startup flags and standard handles
are decoded before the child is made runnable. STARTF_USESTDHANDLES preserves
redirected handles on attachment/allocation, while missing console endpoints
are populated. Normal standard-handle inheritance retains only objects
marked inheritable when bInheritHandles is true; merely copying a numeric
handle in STARTUPINFO does not grant the child access.

The new PE32/PE64 console_attach_pe fixture uses dynamic export lookup as a
negative control. `build/attach-console-negative-20260927-r1/` confirms the
missing export on 8d707e. `build/attach-console-positive-20260927-r2/` passes
parent/explicit PID attachment, duplicate/invalid/unattached targets, PEB
consistency, inherited/detached/no-window children, redirected-file I/O,
non-inheritable and bInheritHandles=false rejection, allocation after detach,
parent independence, and exited-target lifetime. SSH remains responsive.
The tested image is 7,173,176 bytes, SHA-256
`34c7c7572f335bbb6e946d72c9c1f7f0a9e411ea45dabb19f699e4cb11817311`.

This extends the existing shared console endpoint model; it does not add
separate console windows/buffers, complete general handle inheritance, or
claim that Steam's UI now works. The existing unattached FreeConsole behavior
is unchanged. Contract references:
[AttachConsole](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/attachconsole),
[GetStdHandle attachment semantics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/getstdhandle).
GitNexus was unavailable; manual impact analysis covered console state,
CreateProcessA/W and the single win32_spawn_child caller, PE32 ABI export
metadata, and the opt-in SSH/QEMU test path.

### 4.152. P1 CEF font recursion and unavailable D3D9 contract (2026-09-27)

at SystemParametersInfoW, RSP=40013E1000 and CR2=40013E0FF8. The fault is
the return-address push into the bottom guard page of the child's one-MiB
stack, not a write past NONCLIENTMETRICS. Repeated calls from libcef+158E240
consume 0x700 bytes each; the bounded SPI trace reaches 64 entries. Binary
inspection also identifies the preceding DirectWrite factory vtable slot 22
call with method=2, CreateNumberSubstitution(NONE), which returned E_NOTIMPL.
The existing system font catalog could not open its Segoe UI candidate.
Together these observations locate a failing font-initialization/fallback
path that recursively enters Chromium's system-font initialization.

CreateNumberSubstitution now implements the locale-independent NONE mode
with a real refcounted IUnknown/IDWriteNumberSubstitution object, interface
identity, output clearing and invalid-method rejection. Modes FROM_CULTURE,
CONTEXTUAL, NATIONAL and TRADITIONAL remain E_NOTIMPL: this is not an NLS or
contextual shaping implementation, nor a claim of PE32 DirectWrite COM support.
The PE64 fixture calls the actual factory slot and tests 160 object lifetimes,
valid/empty/invalid/NULL locale inputs, interface identity and error outputs.
The same executable passes against native Windows DirectWrite. A separate
Windows probe confirms that NONE accepts these locale inputs whereas the
other supported Windows modes validate their locale.

backend exists. Direct3DCreate9Ex returns D3DERR_NOTAVAILABLE and clears its
output, or D3DERR_INVALIDCALL for a NULL output. PE32 writes only four bytes

### 4.153. VirtIO network CPU mappings under private CR3 (2026-09-27)

Full Steam USB/QEMU tests exposed two independent low-identity-pointer bugs
in virtio_net, which the P1's AX200 path does not use. RX/TX buffers returned
by mem_alloc_aligned were stored as physical pointers although net_poll can
execute from a Win32 child's private CR3. The capability walker also kept
raw BAR addresses for COMMON, NOTIFY and DEVICE registers. On q35 the
notification region was 380000003000; private page tables deliberately lack
that low identity mapping. The second fault persisted after fixing buffers:
`build/steam-font-positive-qemu-20260927-r2/serial.log` captures a write #PF
at virtio_net_recv's queue notification (RIP FFFF800002162459).

Buffers and capability regions now retain PHYS_TO_VIRT aliases for CPU
access. paging_map_mmio already installs the uncached upper-half mapping;
the caller now checks its declared int result. Queue descriptors and buffer
DMA addresses still use physical addresses through kvirt_to_phys. Shared
virtqueue primitives already used the upper-half alias and are unchanged.
No private process receives an extra low identity mapping.

The opt-in vnet_private_pe fixture starts a child with private page tables,
connects to a loopback-only host echo service through QEMU's user network,
and verifies 65,536 patterned bytes across 128 send/receive rounds. Both
PE32 and PE64 run, child exit status is checked, and SSH is tested afterward:

```
OSITO_SSH_TEST_VNET_PRIVATE=1 OSITO_SSH_TEST_STORAGE=usb \
  bash arch/x86/scripts/test-ssh-qemu.sh <new-output-directory>
```

The negative run `build/vnet-private-negative-20260927-r1/` on d8de7b58
reproduces the MMIO write fault in both children. The positive run
`build/vnet-private-positive-20260927-r2/` passes both 64-KiB transfers,
host byte counts and SSH on SHA-256
`45daab3266ceb427cff1820cf88dfdcb07943e57e9347855a20488f53c44fcf5`
(7,177,672 bytes). That newer image has not yet been deployed to the P1.
This validates address-space independence, not general NIC concurrency,
throughput or Steam stability. Earlier live-GDB Steam runs stopped while
waiting for reg_store_lock; a run without that tracer progressed further
and exposed the MMIO fault. No registry-lock cause or fix is claimed.
Manual impact review covered all capability consumers, notification calls,
buffer CPU/DMA aliases and the isolated test branch; GitNexus was unavailable.

### 4.154. CEF delay-load failure: USER32 character casing (2026-09-27)

The targeted hardware breakpoint in
`build/steam-delay-qemu-20260927-r1/delay-trace.log` stops at libcef+59EF780,
before the deterministic crash at +59EF806 seen on the P1. Its live
DelayLoadInfo contains reason=4, dwLastError=127, `USER32.dll!CharUpperW`.
This identifies a missing export, not a graphics-driver failure. The binary's
ERROR_COMMITMENT_LIMIT test and DelayLoad/ModuleName crash key match
[Chromium 126's failure hook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/126.0.6478.183/chrome/common/win/delay_load_failure_support.cc).
The hook and the caller binary remain unmodified.

USER32 now exports CharUpperW, CharLowerW, CharUpperBuffW and CharLowerBuffW
with correct stdcall argument counts. The string APIs distinguish a low-word
character operand from a pointer, convert in place, stop at NUL and preserve
pointer identity. Counted APIs also process embedded NULs and return the
supplied count. UTF-16 pairs are decoded only within the supplied bounds;
unpaired surrogates are preserved. No normalization, expansion or ANSI-codepage
conversion is implied.

The existing CRT casing covers only ASCII/Latin-1, and LCMapStringW currently
copies its input. Neither could implement this missing contract. The new
USER32-local table records observable non-linguistic mappings for all scalar
values and lone UTF-16 code units from native Windows 10.0.26200, compacted
to 135 ranges per direction. `scripts/generate-user32-casemap.py` reproduces
the table through public CharUpperBuffW/CharLowerBuffW calls and `--check`
verifies it without writing. No Microsoft implementation or NLS-file contents
are copied. This is a versioned behavior baseline, not a locale-sensitive
LCMapString implementation or a promise to match every Windows NLS version.
Notably dotless i and final sigma are not changed by the tested non-linguistic
mapping; substituting generic Unicode simple-uppercase data would differ.

The identical PE32/PE64 fixture passes natively on Windows and in
`build/user32-case-positive-20260927-r1/`. It checks 100 rounds of character
operands, return pointers, Latin/Greek/Cyrillic cases, supplementary Deseret,
embedded NULs, unchanged sentinels, zero lengths and incomplete pairs.
`build/user32-case-negative-20260927-r1/` confirms the missing exports on
45daab32. Both runs retain SSH. The positive image is 7,178,056 bytes,
SHA-256 `934347ddf6c9a900fcf1bd97e26164fbcfeab93a60ea91838522ffd3857b074c`.

```

```

`build/dwrite-number-case-positive-20260927-r1/`. A bounded full Steam run

### 4.155 Registry hive waiters must yield across filesystem I/O (2026-09-27)

An additional Steam run on the frozen 934347dd kernel,
`build/steam-user32-case-logs-qemu-20260927-r1/`, stalled at the same
`reg_store_save+0xdd` instruction at 120 and 360 seconds. GDB identified
`RegCloseKey -> reg_store_save`, reg_store_lock=1, reg_lock=0, thirteen ready
tasks, and sched_tick_active=sched_preempt_depth=0. The other CPUs were idle.
The lock owner can yield inside filesystem publication; the PE32 waiter
busy-spins on IST1, where timer preemption is intentionally deferred unless
the shim cooperatively yields. Timer ticks continue, but the suspended writer
cannot resume. This is a scheduler/lock contract violation, not a GPU fault.

`reg_store_save` now retries the atomic lock with `sched_yield`; it retains
exclusive publication, the generation check, error paths, and the existing
hive format. `reg_init` also yields while another task loads the persistent
hive. This does not alter the scheduler, short registry critical sections, or
application binaries. The synchronous flush contract is retained, rather
than reporting success while another writer still owns the store. Reference:
[RegFlushKey](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winreg/nf-winreg-regflushkey).

Validation:

- `test-registry-store.sh` compiles the production registry code against a
  deterministic cooperative I/O fixture. One writer is suspended in a mocked
  disk write, another changes the generation and attempts publication. Both
  must complete without dropping the newer value. A separate case suspends
  the initializer in a hive read. Allocation, write and rename failures must
  preserve dirty state, release the lock and permit a retry.
- The pre-fix source extracted from HEAD blocks in both contention and
  initialization cases under GCC/Clang, normal/UBSan; the external two-second
  timeout confirms each baseline stall. The corrected source passes all four

### 4.156 IP Helper exposes the configured IPv4 DNS server (2026-09-27)

While examining the spinner, the adapter contract was found to omit
`FirstDnsServerAddress` entirely. Chromium's Windows configuration reader
uses `GetAdaptersAddresses` with flags 0x27; these skip unicast/anycast/multicast
and friendly names, not DNS. An otherwise populated adapter therefore had no
name server for Chromium's DNS configuration. This is a confirmed ABI gap,
not proof of the remaining Steam spinner's cause or a replacement for the
system resolver fallback.

The shim now reads the live IPv4 DNS setting through `net_dns_get_server`,
which copies under the existing DNS lock. It returns a caller-buffer-owned
DNS node and sockaddr using the correct PE32/PE64 layout and alignment.
`GAA_FLAG_SKIP_DNS_SERVER` and an unconfigured 0.0.0.0 server omit the list;
skipping unicast does not omit DNS. There is no hardcoded resolver or new
IPv6, registry-notification or hosts-file-watch implementation.

Validation uses public-ABI PE32/PE64 fixtures, also run successfully on native
Windows. In `build/iphlp-dns-positive-20260927-r1/`, the kernel with SHA-256
`efe84a73de5fa79e0cd0a40e0a7a89c79e21d9b051597e69edb62a1ca2acf9c8`
passes both architectures with DNS 10.0.2.3, 192.0.2.53 and 0.0.0.0. Tests cover
AF_UNSPEC/AF_INET, flags including Chromium's 0x27, size probes, short-buffer
non-mutation, ULONG canaries, pointer bounds, node termination and sockaddr
contents. All 12 SSH/ABI gates pass. The pre-fix 6aceae11f image reproduces
the missing-DNS-list failure for both architectures in
`build/iphlp-dns-negative-20260927-r1/`. The kernel getter/link-state host suite
passes 41 checks under GCC/Clang, normal and ASan/UBSan.

GitNexus was unavailable. Manual impact review covered the DNS configuration
lock, adapter payload sizes and caller-owned pointer layouts. Sources:
[GetAdaptersAddresses](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/iphlpapi/nf-iphlpapi-getadaptersaddresses),
[DNS node ABI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/iptypes/ns-iptypes-ip_adapter_dns_server_address_xp),
[Chromium Windows DNS settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/126.0.6478.183/net/dns/public/win_dns_system_settings.cc).
Physical Steam behavior remains unvalidated; remote-maintenance independence
is the current priority.

The saved delay-load frame in

libcef.dll in the immutable test payload identifies `UpdateLayeredWindow`.

values. This establishes one missing API in the saved failure, not that every
spinner or GPU-process exit has this cause. A later pre-fix trace in

source surface into owned SHM before publication, preserving premultiplied
32-bit alpha and DIB orientation. The compositor handles per-pixel opacity,
constant opacity and an exact RGB color key without changing its existing
straight-alpha control path. Position-only updates retain the image, and
layered windows become renderable after initial presentation/attributes.

layered style is reset. Transparent input regions are excluded from hit tests;
the USER32 pixel lookup also checks allocated, not just requested, dimensions.

### 4.158 Finite IOCP deadline accounting (2026-09-27)

Review of the Steam I/O wait path exposed a separate, reproducible Win32
contract defect. `iocp_wait_packet` compared the just-completed wait slice
against the newly reduced remainder. A 200 ms wait therefore expired after
100 ms, and a 500 ms wait after 400 ms. Both GetQueuedCompletionStatus and
GetQueuedCompletionStatusEx used this helper. The fix removes that second
expiration rule and retains the absolute elapsed-tick deadline. Immediate
dequeue, zero-time polling, 100 ms socket-service slices, event wakeups and
infinite-wait handling are unchanged. This is not evidence that the CEF
watchdog or null-pointer fault above was caused by the early timeout.

`test/iocp_deadline_pe.c` imports the public KERNEL32 APIs without hooks. In
each ABI it checks seven empty timeouts per API (0, 50, 150, 200, 250, 350 and
500 ms), a packet posted after Sleep(425) within a 500 ms deadline, and an
already queued packet with timeout zero: 18 scenarios. A 20 ms measurement
tolerance accommodates clock granularity, and each empty wait is bounded
to three seconds. Both binaries pass on native Windows; preserved executables
and output are in `build/iocp-deadline-fixture-20260927-r1/`.

The same fixtures on frozen pre-fix kernel `9bae99f7` produce 12 failures per
ABI: ten early empty waits and two missed late packets. Both negative-control
gates and six base SSH gates pass in
`build/iocp-deadline-negative-20260927-r1/`. With kernel SHA-256
`1ccbee9a6c353180281901148c44a3427385bb2561d0441eea403aa664cbc894`
(7,220,032 bytes), both public-ABI matrices pass, with measured empty waits
matching the requested deadlines. The existing in-kernel IOCP suite passes
20 checks and Winsock passes 87 checks, including pending I/O cancellation,
FIFO and blocking completion. All ten focused SSH/contract gates pass in
`build/iocp-deadline-positive-20260927-r1/` on isolated USB/QEMU storage.
The native/negative/positive PE images differ only in their COFF build
timestamps. SHA-256 after zeroing those four header bytes is
`9711193e515016e759328c233a0a9ee02752fe220e3563fa13246c07173794a2`
for PE32 and
`81fa8bc99eb6ffc45bd55703b445abf8cae4d08a161caf97d830a8bdf57cbba1`
for PE64 in all three builds.
The same ELF passes all 28 general SSH gates in
`build/ssh-iocp-deadline-full-20260927-r1/`, including commands and captures
while the local shell is busy, output isolation, binary/delta transfers,
cold boot and automatic pinned-key reconnection after remote kexec. The
remote-shell policy suite again passes 155 checks per GCC/Clang build,
normal and ASan/UBSan, in `build/shell-remote-iocp-20260927-r1/`.

Reproduce the focused suite with:

```sh
OSITO_SSH_TEST_IOCP_DEADLINE=1 OSITO_SSH_TEST_STORAGE=usb \
  bash arch/x86/scripts/test-ssh-qemu.sh NEW_EVIDENCE_DIRECTORY
```

The negative mode additionally sets `OSITO_SSH_TEST_IOCP_DEADLINE_NEGATIVE=1`
and `OSITO_SSH_TEST_KERNEL` to the frozen old ELF. Default SSH tests are
unchanged when the opt-in variable is absent. GitNexus was unavailable;
manual impact review covered both API consumers, their public PE32/PE64
exports, and existing socket and pipe completion tests. P1 deployment and
the effect on real Steam startup remain unverified.
References: [GetQueuedCompletionStatus](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ioapiset/nf-ioapiset-getqueuedcompletionstatus),
[GetQueuedCompletionStatusEx](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ioapiset/nf-ioapiset-getqueuedcompletionstatusex).

### 4.159 Append-only access and atomic EOF writes (2026-09-27)

The fifteen-minute `steam-iocp-fault-qemu-20260927-r1` run exposed misleading
CEF diagnostics: new September 27 messages appeared at the start of
`cef_log.txt`, followed by old March 9 messages at its tail. Chromium 126 opens
that log with FILE_APPEND_DATA and issues ordinary WriteFile calls. NtWriteFile
previously ignored the handle's granted access and wrote from its file-object
position, initially zero. Different process opens could therefore overwrite
each other's records as well as the historical log. This is a reproduced file
contract defect, not a proven explanation of Steam's startup spinner.

Disk writes now use the calling process's handle access, including reduced
access on DuplicateHandle. FILE_APPEND_DATA without FILE_WRITE_DATA always
selects EOF, regardless of the supplied offset or current pointer. A handle
with neither write right is rejected. GENERIC_WRITE retains ordinary overwrite
semantics, and the explicit FILE_WRITE_TO_END_OF_FILE sentinel also selects
atomic append. Console/pipe behavior and zero-length NT writes are unchanged.

The new OsitoFS v2/v3 append operation compares the expected EOF while holding
the existing filesystem mutation lock, then uses the existing write path.
A changed EOF returns OSFS_APPEND_RETRY without mutation. NtWriteFile releases
its old byte-range I/O guard, rereads EOF and checks the new range before
retrying. This avoids a per-handle-only lock that would still race independent
opens, normal extending writes and truncation. File timestamps, journaling,
durability policy and the on-disk format are unchanged; this is not a crash
consistency redesign or a starvation bound for unlimited concurrent writers.

`test/file_append_pe.c` imports public KERNEL32 APIs in PE32 and PE64. Both
fixtures pass on native Windows, with evidence in
`build/file-append-fixture-20260927-r2/`. Tests cover independent opens,
ignored explicit offsets, reduced-access duplicates, EOF range locks,
ordinary overwrite, the explicit append sentinel, denied read-only writes,
and four concurrent writers producing 128 distinct 16-byte records. The
frozen pre-fix `1ccbee9a` kernel produces 17 failures per ABI in
`build/file-append-negative-20260927-r2/`, including incorrect contents/size,
the wrong lock range and lost concurrent records. Native, negative and
positive executables are byte-identical, built with a zero COFF timestamp:
PE32 SHA-256 `db990bac97f4c8d81cdc02a2ddfe5b549f259a9e94d388ff8c10aca1c1ead580`;
PE64 SHA-256 `6f48ebd098aeacad2ce3e4c8a5b36f3a1d24b71f2ce3ae167053dcd535182bd2`.

The final kernel is 7,224,376 bytes, SHA-256
`9f6e1ef736dd268b86de629324ff2a76aabc5483530e443455569b5759b5da97`.
Both ABI tests and all 59 NT file checks pass on OsitoFS3 in
`build/file-append-positive-20260927-r3/` and OsitoFS2 in
`build/file-append-v2-20260927-r1/`: nine focused SSH/contract gates each.
The NT suite includes deterministic stale-EOF rejection, unchanged contents
and revision on retry, truncation detection and zero-length append behavior.
The earlier `4268dbfd` image additionally passes all ten private-CR3 file-guard
gates in `build/fileguard-append-20260927-r1/`; the final change only prevents
a zero-length OsitoFS2 append from incrementing its file revision. Host tests
pass 18,550 file-lock checks and 155 shell policy checks under GCC/Clang, normal
and ASan/UBSan. `git diff --check`, shell syntax and Python compilation pass.
All 28 general SSH gates also pass on the final ELF, with a successful runner
exit, in `build/ssh-append-full-20260927-r2/`. This includes file/capture access
while the foreground shell is busy, cold boot and remote kexec reconnection.

The six-minute real-Steam run in `build/steam-append-qemu-20260927-r1/` verifies
the logging fix on the final ELF. Comparing the extracted CEF log byte for
byte with the untouched base image preserves its complete 99,030-byte prefix
and adds 13,107 bytes (112,137 total). The pre-fix fifteen-minute control
retained a 99,030-byte file but differed starting at byte 2. The comparison is
saved in `append-prefix-check.json`. New records now appear at the tail,
including GPU initialization/command-buffer and disk-cache errors. The final
capture still has no main Steam window; fixing append has not established a
startup fix. All twenty maintenance probes, authenticated capture, exclusive

```sh
OSITO_SSH_TEST_FILE_APPEND=1 OSITO_SSH_TEST_STORAGE=usb \

```

Negative mode adds OSITO_SSH_TEST_FILE_APPEND_NEGATIVE=1 and selects the

was modified. Physical P1 deployment and repeatable Steam initialization

References: [NtWriteFile](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/ddi/ntifs/nf-ntifs-ntwritefile),
[Chromium 126 log file handling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/126.0.6478.183/base/logging.cc).

### 4.160 Child termination must not abandon host locks (2026-09-27)

The ten-minute `build/steam-freshcache-qemu-20260927-r1/` run on the
`9f6e1ef7` kernel passes 25 maintenance probes and authenticated capture,
but its accepted `console stop` never completes. SSH echo/dmesg still work.
Its disposable disk preserves the old htmlcache under another name and
starts with an empty directory. This does not remove CEF's disk-cache errors
or establish cache corruption as the startup cause. The prelaunch Win32 cache
fixture also changes runtime initialization, so this is not a cache-only
causal comparison against earlier runs without that fixture.

Read-only task snapshots and `owner-gdb.log` establish a different deadlock:
the browser primary task (kernel PID 13) waits on the thread object belonging
to CompositorTileWorker1 (kernel PID 79), which remains in HeapFree. The shared
Win32 heap lock is held at depth one by kernel PID 168, already a zombie after
an injected child-process exit. Other processes also wait in HeapAlloc. The
owner was stopped during GPU-process restart; browser shutdown cannot finish.
The first unqualified GDB `heap_lock` lookup resolved the separate kernel
allocator lock and is not valid evidence for the Win32 lock. The corrected
lookup uses address `ffff800009ec1cc8`, verified from HeapAlloc disassembly,
and reads held=1. Addresses and identities apply only to that frozen ELF/run.

Child TerminateProcess and worker-requested ExitProcess now wake the primary
task without replacing its interrupted instruction pointer. Existing Win32
wait, delay, message-loop and PE32-return checkpoints consume the request on
that task's own exit stack. Delivery is deferred while the current task owns
the Win32 heap or DLL loader lock. NtDelayExecution checks before starting a
new sleep as well as after waking; otherwise a deferred PE64 request can enter
another long sleep after HeapUnlock. Explicit primary-thread ExitProcess keeps
its existing nonreturning path, separate from deferrable remote cancellation.
The scheduler's generic injection API and unrelated forced cleanup paths are
unchanged. GitNexus was unavailable; manual scope review covered these callers,
wait-reference cleanup, heap ownership and the child/main exit contexts.

`test/child_exit_pe.c` uses public Win32 APIs to hold a child's heap lock while
another process requests termination, then repeats with a worker ExitProcess.
After each exit the parent verifies status 83 and allocates/frees memory on a
prestarted worker. The PE32 and PE64 binaries both pass on Windows. They are
byte-identical to the QEMU fixtures, built with a zero COFF timestamp:
PE32 SHA-256 `ef57503d4926627d48e043a76ce95acbdee55a61863a1b7152985c3fabb62991`;
PE64 SHA-256 `29b2f506227aec1b350172651aec84e1c894031b8c5a155e3f6152f12b21a6fa`.
Native logs are in `build/child-exit-fixture-20260927-r1/`. The old-kernel
negative control in `build/child-exit-negative-20260927-r1/` deterministically
reports `CHILD-EXIT FAIL heap probe timed out` after the child exits. That VM
is discarded rather than relying on normal teardown through its orphaned lock.

The final kernel is 7,212,624 bytes, SHA-256
`594ede275ca8eab98160e72d06ca139a8eb29b1782aa892b2c0acb7905834ba5`.
Both ABI fixtures and all eight focused gates pass in
`build/child-exit-positive-20260927-r2/`. The preceding intermediate `-r1`
passes PE32 but times out on PE64; it lacks the pre-sleep checkpoint and is
not counted as a successful run. All fourteen busy-foreground maintenance
gates pass on the final image in `build/ssh-child-exit-maintenance-20260927-r1/`,
including captures, files, exclusive/stale-request rejection, cooperative stop
and SSH afterwards. The shell host suite passes 155 checks under GCC/Clang,
normal and ASan/UBSan, in `build/shell-remote-child-exit-20260927-r2/`.
All 28 general SSH gates pass in `build/ssh-child-exit-full-20260927-r1/`,

### 4.161 Worker cancellation and physical SSH maintenance (2026-09-27)

The preceding primary-task fix does not cover arbitrary forced worker exits.
Process cleanup still called proc_kill_pid on each owned worker, potentially
abandoning the global Win32 heap lock. The public-ABI child-exit fixture now
adds `--L`: a child's worker holds HeapLock, signals readiness, sleeps for
1.5 seconds and unlocks while the parent requests TerminateProcess(83).
After termination, an already-running parent worker must allocate/free memory.
This separates worker-owned heap lifetime from the existing primary-owned
heap cases. All three modes pass on native Windows in both ABIs.

Byte-identical, zero-timestamp fixtures are preserved in
`build/worker-exit-fixture-20260927-r1/`: PE32 SHA-256
`e6a3e5c8cb9a331f932b8d55936a83bbe21093b4332122d8bbf9f39312d67217`
and PE64 SHA-256
`4797cb76cc408e6a2958c5ae675ac380a40a36ebb13f547e1ef2ce398d3a5f43`.
On frozen kernel 594ede27, the negative control passes the previous cases but
reports `CHILD-EXIT FAIL heap probe timed out` after the new worker-lock case.
Evidence is in `build/worker-exit-negative-20260927-r1/`; SSH echo still works
in that negative control. It proves heap abandonment, not a total TCP failure.

Process-wide worker shutdown now publishes a cancellation request and wakes
the worker. The existing wait/delay/message/PE32-return checkpoints deliver it
only after the calling task no longer owns the checked heap or loader lock.
The worker exits on its own kernel stack without guest DLL_THREAD_DETACH
callbacks. Process cleanup waits for the regular reaper to retire all matching
thread contexts before freeing the process image. A newly created suspended
worker also checks cancellation, without requiring ResumeThread.

`proc_disown_zombie_pid` only detaches an already-zombie, non-current task from
its POSIX parent after validating PID identity; it does not kill a live task
or overwrite its exit code. This bypasses the live-parent grace period for
Win32 workers whose handles already have their own lifetime. Cleanup starts
the reaper idempotently before sleeping, so it works from the plain shell
without first starting desktop. The intermediate 34190f70 image omitted that
last step and stalled in the worker-exit fixture; its positive-r1 directory is
failed evidence, not a passing result. GitNexus was unavailable; manual impact
review covered process teardown, scheduler/reaper lifetime, thread-slot reuse,
the common critical-section guards and both ABI checkpoint paths.

The final kernel is 7,212,752 bytes, SHA-256
`5d8f2ac2e66512ee2f87f73f8bc1427fb5006c89e3a96013ae0c6c6ed3210f7d`.

The cancellation contract remains cooperative: an uninstrumented CPU loop or

### 4.162 Explicit seeks on asynchronous file handles (2026-09-27)

Chromium 126's block-file cache opens its primary handle with
FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED, then uses SetFilePointer followed by SetEndOfFile in
File::SetLength. Osito rejected FilePositionInformation whenever the file was
asynchronous, so the public seek returned ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87).
SetEndOfFile could then succeed at the unchanged zero cursor, leaving an empty
file which could not be mapped. This is a concrete compatibility defect, not
proof that every Steam spinner is caused by cache initialization.

FilePositionInformation now permits an explicit nonnegative cursor for either
open mode. The existing file-object lock still protects it. Asynchronous I/O
must still supply an explicit offset and neither consumes nor advances this
cursor; NULL offsets and FILE_USE_FILE_POINTER_POSITION remain rejected.
Negative seeks remain invalid. No filesystem format, append handling, access
rights or async completion policy was changed. GitNexus was unavailable;
manual impact review covered NtSetInformationFile, both SetFilePointer APIs,
the PE32/PE64 calling conventions and SetEndOfFile's cursor query.

The new file_position_pe.c fixture exercises the public ABI, including an
overlapped cache file's extension, mapping, flush and independent-handle read;
shared cursors through DuplicateHandle; explicit-offset read/write preserving
the cursor; negative and relative seeks; truncation; and a position above 4 GiB
without file allocation. Byte-identical fixtures pass on native Windows and
the corrected guest: PE32 SHA-256
`209cb12a35ab57b40e31510798faa5c19fe4c0f716323db886f1b6d715461a42`,
PE64 SHA-256
`24def1dca33b14ec76e0ffabb9d5da7825a95506a30cc12c0d43ddb6564db53d`.
Native evidence is in `build/file-position-fixture-20260927-r1/`.

`build/file-position-negative-20260927-r1/`: both ABIs fail the initial seek,
extension length and mapping, without a guest exception. The corrected full
build uses `CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1` (Ubuntu clang 18.1.3), is 7,258,312
bytes and has SHA-256
`8d2ccf750e04ab9a5fd2a77e98b0ea5fdadacec90d342bfe6a505aaab774a4b8`.
`build/file-position-positive-20260927-r1/` passes both ABI fixtures and all
63 NT file checks. `build/file-position-fs2-20260927-r1/` passes the existing
append fixtures and the same 63 NT checks on OsitoFS2. The complete SSH suite
passes all 28 gates in `build/ssh-file-position-full-20260927-r1/`, including
busy-shell diagnostics/files/capture and automatic reconnection after kexec.

### 4.163 Bounded unhandled-exception diagnostics (2026-09-27)

The default UnhandledExceptionFilter no longer guesses that saved RSP+0x220
contains a FILE pointer. That application-specific SEH64-LOWIO dump caused
the secondary #GP in section 4.162 and is removed, not special-cased for the
poison value. Exception pointers, record headers, the AMD64 saved stack pointer
and each x86/x64 stack entry are now copied to local storage after canonical
range validation. The existing paging_copy_between_cr3 implementation holds
the paging lock over translation and copying, so these diagnostics no longer
use a check followed by an unprotected raw dereference. Unreadable metadata
and unmapped stack entries are explicitly marked and terminate only that
diagnostic walk. The existing EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER return and exception
dispatch/termination paths are unchanged.

Both walks remain bounded: 256 candidate words for AMD64, four EBP frames for
x86. A range-valid x86 EBP can still be an arbitrary register value rather than
a frame pointer; it now undergoes the same checked copy. This is not a general
unwinder, an atomic snapshot of concurrently changing user data, or Windows
Error Reporting parity. GitNexus was unavailable; manual impact review covered
the public shim export, compat32/native exception callers and the existing
paging copy routine. No scheduler, SSH admission or paging implementation was
changed for this fix.

The new seh_diagnostic_pe.c fixtures exercise eight cases per ABI: a valid
stack filled with poison words, a saved stack ending at a committed-page
boundary, an unmapped context, an unmapped exception record, unmapped exception
pointers, a noncanonical AMD64 RSP or unmapped x86 EBP, and partially mapped
pointer/record structures. They run as children with private page tables.
These are Osito diagnostic robustness tests, not native Windows crash-dialog
comparisons. The launcher returning successfully alone is insufficient: the
harness checks the child's PASS marker, expected diagnostic and absence of a
secondary exception, then makes another authenticated SSH request.

`6b97c814c7e776448bab59330854bf77c1bd29f9dea28fa3d3f9174028484442`.

### 4.164 Screen DCs must not target the redirected terminal (2026-09-27)

The P1 photo and authenticated GOP snapshot both show four horizontally
repeated, vertically compressed Steam images inside the desktop terminal.
This is not a remote-capture-only defect. GDI's screen surface used
`fb_get_base()`, which becomes the terminal SHM surface after `fb_redirect()`.
It also copied `fb_get_pitch()` (pixels per row) into `GDI_DC.pitch` (bytes per
row), making native 32-bit row advances four times too small.

Screen DCs now use the display back buffer and its actual geometry. The boot
console remains a fallback only while it has not been redirected. Both paths
convert pixel pitch to byte pitch and retain the native 32-bit format even
when the reported logical display mode is 16-bit. Retained screen DCs refresh
their target on lookup after display startup, buffer rotation or resize.
Their writes present through the selected backend; the desktop HWND no longer
causes the window-damage branch to swallow a screen update.

An ordinary window without a surface no longer falls back to the screen. Its
DC remains attached to that window and can acquire its backing surface later;
otherwise pixel operations fail. Invalid HWNDs passed to `GetDC` return NULL.
`WindowFromDC(GetDC(NULL))` still identifies the desktop, preserving ANGLE's
native-display validation. See the
[GetDC contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-getdc).

`test-gdi-screen.sh` includes the production GDI and framebuffer code. It
checks distinct console/terminal/display targets, padded rows, screen reads,
presentation routing, retained DCs, native versus logical depth, missing
window surfaces and invalid geometry. GCC and Clang, normally and with
ASan/UBSan, each pass 9,243 checks. The preserved pre-change GDI source fails
603 checks in `build/gdi-screen-negative-20260927-r1/`.

`OSITO_SSH_TEST_GDI_SURFACES=1 bash scripts/test-ssh-qemu.sh` runs the existing
GDI paint/DIB/text and USER32 paint PE fixtures as x86 and x64 after starting
the compositor. The paint fixture also checks desktop DC ownership and
invalid HWND rejection. All 16 gates pass, including the window-model test
and post-test SSH, in `build/gdi-screen-qemu-20260927-r1/`. The frozen kernel
is 7,262,664 bytes, SHA-256
`0848b041e9a8713a24d0a30b32321ee61a4ebb5fead0e6ba5c6ac45bae2a1975`.

The real-Steam follow-up `build/steam-gdi-screen-qemu-20260927-r1/` is not a
Steam startup pass: its screenshot shows a #PF at `SystemParametersInfoW`
before the browser renders. The frozen pre-change kernel reproduces the same
instruction offset in `build/steam-gdi-control-qemu-20260927-r1/`. The candidate
passes only 5/15 scheduled maintenance probes, versus 15/15 for that control;

of the different network timing or resolve the pre-existing Win32 fault.

The physical P1 follow-up is preserved in
`build/p1-gdi-screen-20260927-r1/`. Authenticated file sync verified the same

### 4.165 SteamService entry bytes differ from the reference image (2026-09-27)

The combined TCP TX/RX and scheduler-wakeup kernel, SHA-256
`cfb16973b80ff051de1eb66791b3fea17eed853a059c2a5a2bfd9ff5352da513`,
reaches a populated Steam Store in the isolated ten-minute run
`build/steam-runq-qemu-20260927-r1/`. Its connection-log entries for this run
record a successful logon response. SSH recovery, capture and cooperative
stop results, including the initial failures, are in `x86-ssh.md`.

The serial log also retains one unhandled PE32 fault in SteamService:
Win32 owner 77, kernel PID 255, entry RIP `0x005A9944`, CR2 `0x02010048`,
CR3 `0x7BED9000`. The mapped RIP physical address is `0x13DBBD944`, within
the 857-page image allocation at `0x13DA14000`. The allocator trace marks
that page allocated at the fault and records earlier frees/reallocations of
the range; it does not by itself prove double-free or identify a writer.

The reported instruction bytes are repeated `38 18 06 00`, not the entry
sequence in the base-disk reference executable. That 2,963,096-byte file,
extracted read-only to the run's `reference-service/`, has SHA-256
`69c9e3d34ab7b9751e4fb177aadac1117ef16617802d5987fbaedcc622922527`;
objdump shows `E8 89 08 00 00 E9 71 FE FF FF` at `0x005A9944`. The exact
in-flight file contents were not preserved before scratch-disk cleanup, so
the reference comparison does not locate when the bytes changed. Repeated
32-bit values alone are not proof of a graphics overwrite. A follow-up must
compare the load source and mapped page, then trace the first differing
write or remap. No loader/graphics patch or claimed root cause is added here.

The affected child exits with `0xC0000005`; later Steam Store rendering and
remote shutdown succeed. There are also repeated service-pipe failures and
a missing PE32 InternetReadFile thunk contract in crashhandler.dll, separate
from the observed entry bytes. The successful UI is not a clean SteamService,
Steamworks or sustained-application qualification.

The follow-up `build/steam-loader-qemu-20260927-r2/` preserves the in-flight

combined kernel. All 23 observed publications and entries match their load
source bytes. A final 24th load is still in flight when tracing stops. The six
write-watch hits occur after the owning process is ZOMBIE; each retained PMM
history shows the watched page freed and reallocated without a history gap.
They demonstrate normal reuse, not writes corrupting a live service image.
The watcher covers only one HHDM entry-page alias at a time. GDB was manually
terminated before the 300-second checkpoint, so this is not continuous or
complete coverage and does not resolve the earlier entry-point fault.

Two captured load sources are only 1,048,576 bytes, each exactly the prefix
of the full 2,963,096-byte reference. Their entry's raw offset lies outside
the file. The existing PE section validation rejects them and the children
exit with `0xC000000D`; no entry into those truncated images is observed.
Concurrent service-file replacement is a lead, not an established cause.
The final on-disk service again matches the full reference hash. This run
passes 10/15 maintenance queries (all five at 60 seconds fail), later passes
authenticated capture and cooperative stop, and recovers SSH without reboot.
It is therefore neither an all-pass latency test nor a loader fault fix.

### 4.169 AccessCheck and token duplication contracts (2026-10-01)

The next CEF delay-load failure from 4.168 is now implemented as an access
evaluation, not unconditional approval. `AccessCheck` exports eight stdcall
arguments for PE32 and uses the native Microsoft ABI for PE64. It validates
the impersonation token and TOKEN_QUERY access, descriptor owner/group,
privilege buffer size, and ACE/SID bounds within the declared ACL. Ordinary
allow/deny ACEs are evaluated in order against the token user and enabled
groups, with separate handling of INHERIT_ONLY, OWNER_RIGHTS, implicit owner
READ_CONTROL/WRITE_DAC and MAXIMUM_ALLOWED. Missing grants return a completed
check with AccessStatus FALSE; API failures leave the result outputs intact.
The local tokens have no privileges, so ACCESS_SYSTEM_SECURITY is denied with
ERROR_PRIVILEGE_NOT_HELD even for a NULL DACL.

`DuplicateTokenEx` previously returned a handle to the original token object,
ignoring the requested primary/impersonation type and impersonation level.
Immutable variants now preserve those properties without mutating the source.
The source requires TOKEN_DUPLICATE, zero desired access inherits the original
handle rights, and raising an existing impersonation level is rejected.
Handle inheritance is preserved. The current single-user token explicitly
reports Everyone, Authenticated Users and Builtin Users as enabled groups;
the anonymous identity does not acquire those groups. GetTokenInformation and
AccessCheck use that same group model and check query rights.

The expanded test exposed another defect: the root executable launched with
`winexec` had no primary-thread object through the current-thread resolver,
although explicit thread-handle APIs could obtain one. The resolver now
exposes the existing primary object only for the active main execution's
kernel task. Its impersonation is cleared at main-execution begin/end, so it
cannot leak through the legacy primary object into the next shell launch.
Child processes and worker threads retain their existing object path.

Primary contracts: [AccessCheck](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-accesscheck)
and [DuplicateTokenEx](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/securitybaseapi/nf-securitybaseapi-duplicatetokenex).
The same `access_check_pe.c` fixture executes on Windows and OsitoK as PE32
and PE64. Exact result/error/granted-mask/output-buffer assertions cover NULL,
absent and empty DACLs, owner/group requirements, allow/deny ordering, group
membership, inheritance, owner rights, maximum access and generic bits.
Token checks cover requested type/level, source immutability, handle access,
inheritance, anonymous identity and exit while impersonating. Invalid ACE and
SID extents fail without granting access. An unknown ACE is explicitly
unsupported in OsitoK; Windows ignores this test ACE and denies by absence of
an allow rule. That case asserts fail-closed behavior, not identical errors.

Build uses `make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 -j4 build/kernel.elf`.
Final kernel size is 7,267,192 bytes, SHA-256
`9e4a9f8fe69ec76fc1ac454a8777f709c39d18e4e4b7502b7cf6b1e2730632db`.

### 4.170 Restricted-token filtering, access checks and lifetime (2026-10-01)

The next no-argument Steam failure from 4.169 was an unimplemented
`CreateRestrictedToken` import. ADVAPI32 now exports its nine-argument
PE32/PE64 contract and `IsTokenRestricted`. Filtering snapshots guest SIDs,
preserves primary/impersonation type and handle rights, marks disabled user
and group SIDs deny-only, and owns the resulting SID storage. Nested
restricting lists intersect without deduplication; an empty intersection and
weakening a full restriction to write-only are rejected. DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE
uses the existing empty privilege set. LUA_TOKEN remains explicitly
unsupported; SANDBOX_INERT does not grant this non-SYSTEM identity a bypass.

AccessCheck now evaluates both ordinary and restricting SIDs. Write-only
restrictions check the write mask, including DELETE/WRITE_DAC/WRITE_OWNER;
read denials in that second pass cannot incorrectly reject an otherwise
allowed mixed read/write request. Full restrictions require owner membership
in both passes. TokenUser, TokenGroups, TokenRestrictedSids and the one-byte
TokenHasRestrictions query reflect the stored token. TokenLogonSid reports
ERROR_NOT_FOUND when the local identity has no logon SID, rather than treating
the information class as invalid.

Filtered and duplicated tokens are immutable reference-counted allocations.
The handle table retains once per numeric entry, including DuplicateHandle,
and releases after the final inherited owner drops that entry. API lookups
pin tokens under the handle-table lock. Thread impersonation owns a separate
reference, released by replacement, RevertToSelf, thread termination and root
execution cleanup. Heap frees do not occur under the handle-table spinlock.
The internal `g_token_live_objects` counter provides a lifetime regression
oracle; it is not a user-facing allocation limit.

Validation uses the same `restricted_token_pe.c` binary sources on Windows
and OsitoK. Checks cover SID attributes, source immutability, ordered access,
normal/restricting intersections, owner rights, NULL DACLs, maximum access,
write-only restrictions, nested filtering, invalid handles/SIDs, handle
rights, copied SID storage and logon-SID query behavior. Each PE32/64 run
performs 4,096 create/duplicate/impersonate/replace/revert cycles and exits a
worker thread and the root process while impersonating. QEMU GDB snapshots
must report zero live token allocations after each executable returns.

- `restricted-token-cycles-20261001` and `restricted-token-user-object-20261001`:
