### 4.208 Checked caller slot for the physical SSL error probe

The scalar-only operation probes can exhaust their 32-hit budget on ordinary
nonblocking handshake/read retries before the fatal error. The existing
fingerprinted error probe therefore gains an optional `caller32:<offset>` or
`caller64:<offset>` argument. It reads exactly one declared 4- or 8-byte return
slot after the CR3 and instruction checks. The offset is aligned and bounded
to 512; checked canonical arithmetic keeps the entire read in one 4 KiB page.
Both the slot and decoded destination must be present in the target page
tables, and the destination must be executable. An unavailable slot leaves the
scalar trace intact. This does not walk the stack or capture record payloads.
The optional state remains private, preserving the public `hwbp_t` layout.

The first caller QEMU run identifies a real instrumentation assumption:
requiring the PTE USER bit rejects Win32's current CPL0 supervisor mappings.
A separate GDB inspection at the PE32 #DB dispatch confirms CS `0x40`, RSP
`0x2020fb30`, return slot `0x2020fb34`, and correct caller `0x401261`.
All four levels of both the stack and code mapping have USER clear; the stack
leaf is present and NX, while the code leaf is present and executable.
The reader is corrected to require present mappings rather than USER, retaining
canonical range, page-boundary and execute checks. GitNexus impact runs precede
the reader/test edits; the reader's actual call site is checked manually in
`hwbp_dispatch` because the graph misattributes that edge to a nested extern.

The resulting policy/parser has 124 checks passing with GCC and Clang, normally
and under ASan/UBSan; shell admission has 188 passing checks in the same four
configurations. PE fixture metadata verifies the one-push prologue and derives
the expected return addresses from direct call sites. USB-backed QEMU r4 passes
all six cases for both PE32 and PE64: limit, fingerprint mismatch, private-child
CR3 exclusion, clear, existing watch, and checked caller return. Invalid offsets,
extra arguments and other invalid requests are rejected, and SSH remains usable
while the fixtures run. The preceding r3 stops after a PE64 fixture exits zero
with only a partial prompt and an unanswered QMP diagnostic; it is retained as
an incomplete run, not counted as a pass. The r4 repeat does not reproduce that
stop. Evidence: `build/hwbp-caller-20261003/{policy-r2,shell,qemu-r4}/` and
`qemu-inspect-r4/mapping.json`.

### 4.209 Overlapped send completion differential

`wsock_WSASendTo` currently treats a successfully queued prefix as completion
of an overlapped scatter/gather send. The earlier stream-integrity fixture
retries the remainder after every short completion, which preserves bytes but
does not test this completion contract. Microsoft specifies completion after
the transport consumes the send buffers, and distinguishes short sends on
non-overlapped nonblocking sockets. Sources:
[WSASend](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winsock2/nf-winsock2-wsasend)
and [overlapped I/O](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winsock/overlapped-i-o-and-event-objects-2).
GitNexus impact for the provider shows low risk, with direct callers
`wsock_WSASend` and `wsock_WSASendMsg`, and `wsock_selftest` upstream. Exported
API users are broader than the statically resolved call graph.

The new `winsock_send_completion_pe.c` fixture submits one 2 MiB request in
four descriptors, including an empty descriptor. The peer delays reads and
advertises a small receive window; the fixture invalidates its stack descriptor
array immediately after the API returns. Success requires one IOCP completion
for the full request and independent receiver acknowledgement before close.
Native Windows PE32/PE64, with blocking and nonblocking socket modes, all
complete 2,097,152 bytes and verify receiver SHA-256
`32fc9bb661c42068738394121899ab2d03510b5ccda5fc34dfdec44dc273822c`.
The unchanged diagnostic kernel reproduces short successful completions in all
four USB-backed QEMU cases; the fixture correctly exits failure. SSH remains
usable. The negative harness passing means it detects the defect, not that
the provider satisfies the contract. Evidence:
`build/winsock-send-completion-20261003/native-r2-{results,peer}.json` and
`qemu-negative-r2/`.

The initial 256 KiB comparison reproduces the defect in one case, but Slirp
can buffer the entire smaller request in another; immediate socket close also
interferes with peer delivery. That incomplete run is retained. Increasing
the request and requiring receiver acknowledgement isolates the completion
test from close behavior. This is a demonstrated Winsock contract defect;
whether correcting it resolves Steam's fatal peer alert still needs physical
validation. No provider correction has been deployed at this observation.

### 4.210 Ordered pending WSASend and physical backpressure

The provider now captures scatter/gather descriptors and retains unfinished
stream sends in a bounded queue. It advances only bytes accepted by TCP and
reports successful completion only for the complete request. Overlapped calls
return `WSA_IO_PENDING` without waiting for the peer, regardless of the socket's
blocking flag. Non-overlapped blocking WSASend consumes the whole request;
ordinary send and non-overlapped nonblocking sends retain legal short-send
behavior. Datagram framing is preserved.

Requests retain the issuing process, thread, ABI width, immutable CR3, socket
generation and actual progress. FIFO follows the shared socket generation,
including duplicate handles; cancellation holes cannot allow a newer request
to overtake an older one. The worker copies bounded chunks through explicit
address spaces into a shared 16 KiB stage before TCP takes ownership. Close,
CancelIo/CancelIoEx, DisconnectEx, process release and thread/TLS teardown
retire pending sends before their memory is reclaimed. Event-only notification
works without a caller polling IOCP, and issuing a send resets its event.

The worker's default Win32 namespace is 1 even when its CR3 differs from the
active primary PE. `win32_process_cr3` therefore resolves active process
registration before the native-test fallback; IOCP completion checks the
address space as well as the namespace before directly touching OVERLAPPED.
Foreign completions use the existing explicit-CR3 copies. This is covered by
the same fixtures in private PE32 and PE64 child mappings.

The first positive QEMU run delivers all 2 MiB but then stalls in close. Saved
CPU state and the frozen ELF place CPU 0 at closesocket's inlined lifecycle
lock spin. A completion wakes its caller while the lock owner can yield in
serial output. Contended lifecycle/send locks now yield to the scheduler;
subsequent full-send, close and thread-lifetime cases finish normally.
The failed run is retained as `qemu-positive-r1/`.

GitNexus impact: WSASendTo is low (3 upstream), pending-I/O service low (7),
ordinary send low (6), cancellation medium (55), IOCP completion medium (39),
and lifecycle acquisition medium (74). TLS detach graphs report high (198),
including spurious nested-extern edges to serial_puts. Manual direct callers
are thread entry/ExitThread for PE32 and dispatch/forced retirement/ExitThread
for PE64. Public exports and scheduler callbacks extend beyond graph edges.
All analyzed symbols were checked before their corresponding edits; new
fixtures initially needed manual entry/callback scope until indexing finished.

Validated kernel: 7,365,448 bytes, SHA-256
`1005c554ab37bea83c584f8bdaa13a9814a9f52ef85ffe8f6a354d99ee6bcf41`.
Build: `make -C arch/x86 CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1 -j6`.
USB-backed QEMU passes four full-send cases, fourteen queue cases, the same
fourteen cases in private children, and both existing IOCP/Winsock selftests.
The four existing bidirectional private stream cases also pass with independent
2 MiB receiver validation. Evidence under
`build/winsock-send-completion-20261003/`: `qemu-positive-r3/`, `qemu-queue-r1/`,
`qemu-queue-private-r1/`, and `qemu-stream-r1/`.

The queue fixture uses only public Windows APIs and checks FIFO, a cancelled
middle operation followed by slot reuse, close, issuing-thread return,
event-only completion and process exit. Successful completions must always
cover the full request; close/exit can race with an already completed send.
Native Windows passes all twelve ABI/mode cases. Cancelled sends may already
have copied some or all bytes into transport-owned storage, so the independent
peer verifies the allowed prefix and strict ordering of later sends instead
of assuming that cancellation retracts bytes. The initial overly strict native
fixture runs are retained; the successful comparison is
`native-queue-r5-{results,peer}.json`. Both successful native completion and
cancelled completion outcomes were observed for close/thread races.

### 4.212 Physical CEF breakpoint after reaching the store

The operator subsequently reports a breakpoint at saved RIP `0x1859ef906`
after the slow transition to the store, before any Library click. This is a
new blocking failure after successful login, rather than evidence that the
Library selection itself crashes. Physical SSH remains unavailable; no reset
is performed remotely and no post-fault capture or stack is available.

For the exact `libcef.dll` used by the isolated repeat, SHA-256
`c85bf94462b3c79baeac63823db52d15e116eead71ea414e5d3a112c59e434d3`,
the first `int3` is at `0x1859ef905` and its saved RIP is `0x1859ef906`.
This lies in the delayed-load failure hook starting at `0x1859ef880`.
The hook copies the DLL name from `DelayLoadInfo` and deliberately aborts;
the address alone does not identify the missing DLL/export or its error.
Chromium's corresponding behavior is documented in
[delay_load_failure_support.cc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/126.0.6478.183/chrome/common/win/delay_load_failure_support.cc).
The earlier AccessCheck defect at this same hook is already corrected and
must not be inferred to be the current cause.

stock Steam arguments. The first reaches an authenticated store frame; the
second renders store content at its 600 and 900 second captures. A hardware
breakpoint at the verified hook entry does not fire during the second run.

reads succeed without a reset. These repeats do not reproduce or resolve the
physical breakpoint. Evidence is retained under
`build/winsock-send-completion-20261003/steam-qemu-r1/` and
`steam-delay-qemu-r2/`, including the offline DLL fingerprint guard.

### 4.216 Bounded private-stack diagnostics prepared for the P1 reboot

The P1 remains in request 4 with black content at 12:59:24 UTC. The operator
confirms that Library navigation is stuck. The diagnostic therefore adds

correction as the cause or cure of this application stall.

The query copies at most 2 KiB from a saved stack and follows at most sixteen
monotonic frame-pointer links within a bounded range. It reads through explicit
page tables without installing the target CR3 or faulting in absent pages.
Target identity and stack reads are protected by the BSP interrupt mask;
formatting occurs afterward. Current, exited, missing and frameless tasks are
rejected. Present writable source mappings are checked, and executable-looking
stack words are separately labelled as candidates. Upper-half candidates must
lie in the linked kernel text: broadly executable RAM aliases do not establish
that a heap or stack pointer is code. This is not a complete CEF unwinder.

The stack command takes the native PID from PROC-SNAP. NTWAIT-SNAP records
the Win32 owner process, but its tid field is the native scheduler PID;
it must not be substituted for CreateProcess's advertised Win32 thread ID.
The offline selection plan groups tasks by their captured CR3 and includes
the lowest live native PID and representative waits, without claiming that
this alone proves their application roles. Symbolication is checked against
the frozen kernel and the exact CEF image; it preserves the distinction
between frame-pointer links and raw candidates.

Both bounded child fixtures return normally on native Windows. In QEMU the
x86 and x64 children have CR3s distinct from the SSH worker, remain running
through inspection, and return normally afterward. Both inspections read
2,048 bytes. The x64 frame chain includes the fixture's parked caller; the x86
inspection captures its native compatibility path, without establishing the
32-bit application's caller. All twenty polling controls also pass. Invalid
PID, zero PID and malformed PID queries return their expected errors.

the corrected fixture supplies the structure and its size, consistent with
[CreateProcessA's contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessa).

Source inspection finds an independent SRW contract error: shared acquisition
and release are aliases of exclusive acquisition and release, and
SleepConditionVariableSRW rejects the shared-mode flag. Windows requires
concurrent shared readers and a condition wait that releases and reacquires
the supplied mode. The shim now uses bit zero for a writer and increments of
two for readers, with DWORD storage for PE32 and pointer-sized storage for
PE64. Shared release removes only one reader. Condition waits accept flags
zero or CONDITION_VARIABLE_LOCKMODE_SHARED and reacquire the same mode after
wake or timeout. Both contended acquisition loops also use the existing
guarded termination checkpoint. The exclusive CAS helper, loader/heap guards
and scheduler are unchanged.

entry points have LOW indexed impact; the new shared helper and fixture
functions are not indexed. The existing exclusive helper has HIGH impact
with 131 indexed upstream nodes and is left unchanged. The new public
fixture covers parallel shared acquisition, writer exclusion, shared and
exclusive condition timeouts with mode retention, last-reader release,
shared condition wake, and cancellation of two shared or two exclusive
contenders during child termination.

BOOL. Native PE32 then reads unspecified upper return bits and fails the

### 4.225 Fixed-address reservations starve automatic VA allocation

The subsequent physical failure at `0x13f608dc1` is in
`vstdlib_s64.dll+0x8dc1`. The exact DLL copied from the P1 executes
`mov [rcx],eax` with RCX zero; the preceding load reads the IAT slot for
`tier0_s64.dll!g_dwDllEntryThreadId`, a data export. The retained log records
failed tier0 initialization and, before its first DllMain failure, an
automatic allocation rejection with `next64=0x0000010000000000`. That is the
end of the allocator's automatic Win64 range, not evidence that physical
RAM is exhausted. The compatibility loader subsequently enters vstdlib
with unresolved imports. Library remains unvalidated.

Both exact DLLs pass isolated dynamic and eager-import tests on Windows,
QEMU and the P1 with the existing SRW kernel. The eager test also creates
and checks a child process. A separate public-API fixture then reproduces
the allocation failure: reserve a high fixed address, followed by an
automatic reservation. On x64 it also reproduces tier0 initialization
failure after the high reservation. Windows passes x86, x64 and the exact
DLL variant; QEMU and the P1 running kernel `2f3c78f3...` fail all three
controlled cases. Each physical case returns to the console with SSH
responsive; requests 9, 10 and 11 are the negative controls.

The cause is that successful fixed-address reservations and section mappings
advance the same cursor used for automatic placement. The automatic search
then overlooks free address space below the fixed allocation. The correction
limits cursor advancement to automatic placement in
`nt_allocate_virtual_memory` and `sys_NtMapViewOfSection`. Existing conflict
checks still reject overlap with live allocations. GitNexus reports LOW
impact with zero indexed upstream callers for these two syscall routines;
indirect public-API entry paths are covered by the executable fixtures.

Steam request 6 was stopped cooperatively at 01:22 UTC on October 4 and
returned without rebooting the P1. A new kernel is being built from an
isolated source snapshot, including the concurrent GUI changes and new
theme/font/widget modules, with `CLANG=1 QUIET=1 SKIP_MODEL=1
WIN32_LOOKUP_TRACE=1`. Post-fix qualification and a new real Steam Library
interaction are pending at this checkpoint; the installed P1 kernel is
still the qualified SRW image.

### 4.227 Cancelled worker memory must outlive its remaining peers

The `2f338123` Steam instance accepts login at 02:03:09 UTC on October 4,
but the operator confirms that the Library options remain black and the
application is slow. Browser-watchdog kills appear at 02:08:30 and 02:08:32.
The later physical fault is `libcef.dll+0x2e717a6`, in the exact CEF image
with SHA-256 `c85bf94462b3c79baeac63823db52d15e116eead71ea414e5d3a112c59e434d3`.
The instruction `mov [rcx],rax` writes to `0x4005afccd0`, with no owner VMA
and a zero PTE. Native PID 340 belongs to renderer primary PID 335, Win32
PID 78, CR3 `0x8a870000`. This is distinct from the corrected vstdlib null
data import in 4.225.

Immediately before the fault, Steam requests renderer termination and the
reaper retires 21 workers. The faulting code removes a node from a doubly
linked list under EnterCriticalSection/LeaveCriticalSection, identified
from the exact CEF import slots. Its previous-node pointer is near the saved
stack pointer of the already reaped native PID 343 in that same CR3. This
stack association is an inference from the saved scheduler addresses; the
unmapped write and preceding retirement are directly recorded. No private
CEF function name is inferred from the nearest exported symbol.

Cooperative cancellation preserves host heap/loader locks by letting their
owners reach a safe checkpoint. Reaping another cancelled worker previously
freed its guest stack and TLS immediately, although a surviving peer could
still retain a guest reference to them. `win32_kernel_thread_reaped` now
retires the scheduler task and thread handle without releasing those guest
allocations. Reclaim state two pins the context for process TLS/VM cleanup.
`win32_terminate_process_threads` waits for active workers and scheduler reap
state one; retained state two is released by the existing final process
cleanup, after all workers stop. Ordinary thread exits are unchanged.
GitNexus reports LOW indexed impact and zero indexed upstream callers for
both modified functions; their indirect lifecycle paths require executable
coverage. Microsoft documents that
[TerminateProcess stops all process threads](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-terminateprocess).
The deferred host-lock unwind is specific to Osito's compatibility runtime.

`cancel_stack_pe.c` publishes a stack node from one worker and keeps a peer
inside HeapLock during process termination. Windows passes three rounds in
each ABI. The first fixture revision used one Sleep call; the cancellation
wake returned before reclamation, so its x86 negative control passed and
was inconclusive. Revision two waits for an elapsed interval across wakes.
With the previous exact kernel it faults on the unmapped peer stack in
both ABIs. The x86 harness initially expected console return; the actual
negative case faults and then fails its termination wait, so that harness
times out. A separate x64 control explicitly captures the fault and live
SSH without claiming process completion.

The corrected QEMU kernel passes all six new rounds and returns the console.
Logs show two retained stacks transferred to process VM cleanup in each
round, followed by owner mapping release. Existing SRW, heap/CS cancellation
and MsgWait fixtures pass 44 further checks across x86/x64. The isolated
image is `kernel-cancel-retain-diag-r1.elf`, 7,589,088 bytes, SHA-256
`d7be466e3c4879ad58f5e05c882220b983e94938eda6acab6bdb5f999940e6bd`.
It includes the concurrent GUI edits captured in its source manifest.

The earlier performance sample does not establish the black-menu cause.
USB counters cover 92.23 seconds and record 20.61 seconds in IRQ-masked
storage ownership, including diagnostic I/O. BSP profiler samples often
land in compositor copies or immediately after interrupt restoration;
those counts are not all-CPU time attribution. No proposed mapping-duration
trace was installed before this fault. Library rendering and latency remain
unresolved after the synthetic cancellation fix.

An optional `WIN32_LATENCY_TRACE=1` build records bounded per-operation TSC
samples and cumulative counts. VM dispatch measures only its interrupt-
disabled interval; eager section-file reads measure elapsed wall time.
These intervals must not be summed with USB storage time. Records are
capped at 128 per operation and the dmesg ring can overwrite early records.
The normal build leaves this instrumentation disabled. GitNexus reports
23 indexed upstream impacts for dispatch and none for CreateSection; new
diagnostic helpers are unindexed, with unknown scope.

### 4.231 Improved response, black Library menu, and duplicate termination

On kernel `0fc0f9fe`, the operator reports improved Steam responsiveness but
the Library menu remains black. Login reaches Success; the initial bounded
watch records no new Encryption Failure. One large dmesg download times out;
subsequent authenticated queries recover. The 04:19:08 UTC capture shows the

Later webhelper records contain four unresponsive-browser kills at 04:16:55,
04:20:57, 04:24:25 and 04:25:42. USER32 records show CEF destroying its render
windows. These extend the initial monitoring interval, whose watchdog count
was zero. EGL/D3D failures predate this interaction and do not establish the
black-menu cause. Exact-kernel stack samples show message/event waits and
renderer startup in eager mapped-file reads through USB; they do not prove
an individual wait is deadlocked. The later 66-thread collection retains
64 successful stack captures and two disappearing-thread failures.

The lifecycle log exposes a separate recovery defect: a second
TerminateProcess request reaches forced termination after the target has
already entered ordinary cleanup. `exit_ready` is false during that cleanup,
which was being confused with an uninitialized exit context. Forced cleanup
can interrupt the existing owner and replace its exit code. The new
`teardown_started` state is published before clearing `exit_ready`; requests
inspect identity and lifecycle with interrupts excluded and leave an existing
cleanup owner in charge. Process completion remains published after resource
release. No UI backend or unsupported graphics capability is changed.

### 4.234 Hidden owners incorrectly suppressed Steam popup surfaces

The operator reports that Steam is entirely black on the 4.233 kernel.
`capture-now-20261004-053708.png` confirms the black 1280x800 Steam rectangle;
console request eight and SSH remain alive. Fresh bounded logs contain no

`black-current-windows-20261004-054242.log` records Steam showing an SDL
popup with `visible=1 effective=0`, owned by a hidden 32x32 SDL helper.
`window_should_render` incorrectly required every owner to be visible,
unlike the Windows distinction between parents and owners. It also began
the owner walk at a child rather than its top-level root, allowing some
descendant surfaces through while their owned root was suppressed.
The corrected predicate preserves parent visibility, layered initialization
and minimization checks, permits a hidden owner, and checks minimized
owners from the root for the entire subtree. This matches Microsoft's
[window visibility contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/window-features#window-visibility)
and the hidden-owner pattern documented for the
[taskbar](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/shell/taskbar).

The unchanged public-API `owner_visibility_pe.c` fixture passes ten checks
per ABI on native Windows. It covers hidden owners, popup descendants,
explicit parent hiding, owner minimization and restoration. Its first
native version sampled restoration before Windows animations/messages had
settled; r2 pumps messages for a bounded interval and passes both ABIs.
The exact installed `36496a5d` kernel fails six x86 and four x64 checks in
`owner-visibility-negative-qemu-r1/`, including hidden-owner popup hits on
both. The x86 run also exposes the missing POINT-by-value conversion in
WindowFromPoint: two PE32 DWORD arguments must become one native packed
eight-byte argument. A typed compat32 bridge now performs that conversion
without changing the export's two-slot stack cleanup or the native API.

`owner-visibility-positive-qemu-r2/`. The first positive run exposed two
old focus-test assumptions that hiding an owner also hides its popups.
The test now explicitly hides those popups before testing focus transfer
to the remaining window; its original focus assertions remain intact.
No kernel exception is observed and SSH works after both PE fixtures.

### 4.238 Small read-only sections and two exposed cache-path defects

`NtCreateSection` now routes read-only file sections below 1 MiB through the
existing bounded, revision-keyed control-area cache. Small writable/pagefile
sections and SEC_IMAGE retain their previous backing paths. This eliminates
the unconditional whole-file read at creation for small immutable resources.

The first laboratory build (`6014d2eb`) was **not deployed**: the new fixture
found zero data in a shell-hosted PE32 view and inability to delete closed
cached files. PE32's kernel address space inherits RAM identity aliases;
the sparse map had left these present, preventing a file-backed page fault.
`NtMapViewOfSection` now removes those aliases from its conflict-checked view,
splitting huge aliases through the existing mapper when needed. Private
process roots do not need this extra step. `delete_osfs_file` drops inactive
control areas for the target inode before deletion; active section references
remain retained. This does not add deferred deletion for active mappings.

Kernel `12b82271` passes the corrected 16-check small-file fixture on both
ABIs in QEMU, plus 20 owner-visibility, 102 window, 166 input, 10 dialog and
32 GDI checks. The serial log records actual small-file cache hits and no
fatal exception. A later optional probe incorrectly required DeleteFile to
fail while a share-delete handle/view remained open; Windows accepted pending
deletion. That assertion was removed, without changing production code to
match it. The final fixture also runs with a 1,048,713-byte file to cover the
previous large-section path. Physical qualification is pending at this point.

GitNexus reports no indexed upstream callers for the two NT entrypoints;

helper and fixture are unindexed. The delete helper has 12 upstream symbols,

the small-map behavior expected by APIs that validate user buffers.

### 4.252 The repeated fatal hook identifies ReleaseStgMedium

SSH returns on the next retry, allowing all four complete boot slots to be
saved before another Steam launch in `braid-boot-evidence-20261004-164221/`.
The 1,098,569-byte `boot2.log` (SHA-256
`82c915ef0586bb80b9e92a785fa1e2bc8c0970f4b64d28c14d91b02a3a10f9fb`)
ends at the selected normal-context checkpoint. The actual missing function
is now `ole32.dll!ReleaseStgMedium`, error 127, PID 3/TID 7, caller
`0x183b4e899`. It is not a repeated DoDragDrop lookup. The new boot is slot
three with `sshd-ready`; no actual trap line was persisted in the prior slot.

ReleaseStgMedium now reads the correct PE32/PE32+ structure layout and calls
the existing resource destructors. It respects an explicit IUnknown owner,
always releases stream/storage references, releases the filename allocation
even when its owner retains the file, and clears the type/owner fields while
leaving the inactive union untouched. The existing compatibility callback
bridge invokes 32-bit COM Release methods. The ownership rules follow
[Microsoft ReleaseStgMedium](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ole2/nf-ole2-releasestgmedium).
GitNexus reports LOW/zero indexed upstream callers for the resolver; the new
shim and fixture functions are unindexed. The production edits remain in
OLE32 and its header, reusing existing cleanup APIs without changing them.

Metafile creation/destruction is not implemented by GDI. Delegated metafile
owners are released, but direct non-null owned metafile destruction remains
unsupported and emits a diagnostic; opaque handles are never passed to a
heap allocator. This limitation is not presented as complete metafile support.

The identical PE32/PE64 ownership probes pass 53 checks each on native Windows.
They cover COM release order and aliased owner references, fixed-global-memory
reclamation, retained fixed/movable data, file deletion versus delegation,
bitmap retention/recycling, structure canaries and repeated-call stack balance.
An initial bitmap test incorrectly used GetObjectType on a deleted handle as
a liveness oracle. Native Windows still answers queries about that handle,
including after GdiFlush, although a subsequent DeleteObject fails. The final
probe instead checks retained objects and recycles 1,024 bitmaps, exceeding
OsitoK's 512-slot pool. Failed oracle attempts are retained; no GDI implementation
was changed to satisfy them.

### 4.253 Braid install-script NULL call and terminal recovery (2026-10-04)

After the details-page fix, the operator reports a new `#PF` at address zero
when starting Braid. The persisted record recovered after reboot identifies
native PID 36 (`win32_thread`, TGID 1), RIP/CR2 zero, error `0x11` (instruction
fetch), and return address `0x1387071e1`. Steam's last game action is
`RunningInstallScript` for app 26800; this does not establish that the Braid
executable started. The recovered `steamclient64.dll` matches the reference
SHA-256 `caba4826aa3501039d095aee1843a6bfb270fb43a3ab4455b2d6733223579fee`.
Its call at `0x1387071db` goes through IAT slot `0x13916bb30`, the missing
`SHELL32.dll!ShellExecuteExW` import. Evidence: `braid-boot-evidence-20261004-175930/`,
`braid-launch-files-20261004-180640/`, and `braid-launch-fault-imports.json`.

`ShellExecuteExA/W` now parse the guest's 60-byte PE32 or 112-byte PE64
structure, launch executable paths through the existing process machinery,
honor the show command and console flag, and retain a waitable process handle
only for `SEE_MASK_NOCLOSEPROCESS`. Failure returns `FALSE`, a shell error in
`hInstApp`, and `GetLastError`; it does not report a fictitious launch.
Class/PIDL execution, environment expansion, hotkeys, `WAITFORINPUTIDLE`,
service-provider sites and non-executable associations remain unsupported.
The Microsoft contracts are documented in
[ShellExecuteExW](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/shellapi/nf-shellapi-shellexecuteexw)
and [SHELLEXECUTEINFOW](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/shellapi/ns-shellapi-shellexecuteinfow).

The crash also exposed an exception ownership bug: the PE64 dispatcher
rejected a NULL destination because it was not an executable mapping, then
native exception handling killed TGID 1, which contains the synchronous
console owner. Guest instruction-fetch faults now enter Win32 VEH/unwind and
process-exit handling when the interrupted task belongs to the active Win32
process. Unrelated kernel tasks and high-half addresses retain the kernel
fault path. Unhandled faults are persisted before the orderly Win32 exit.

At the operator's request, the terminal now routes Ctrl+C to a cooperative
termination request (signal 15, exit 143) and Ctrl+K to forced termination
(signal 9, exit 137) of its foreground Win32 session. Keyboard/IRQ producers
publish a generation-tagged mailbox; a kernel service dispatches it. Old
requests cannot terminate the next launch. Forced delivery changes only the
interrupted owner's guest execution frame, using its saved host stack and
64-bit selectors; shim critical sections must first reach a safe exit point.
In the GUI the terminal must have keyboard focus. Native ELF and DOS
foreground registration are not implemented by this change.

The NULL-fetch recovery probe also reproduced a PE32 `ExitThread` bug:
the native task became a zombie without signaling its NT thread object, so
the parent timed out. PE32 workers now save a scheduler-stack continuation
like PE64 workers. Explicit exit returns there before resetting callback
state and releasing guest mappings, then signals the retained thread object.

Validation before deployment:

- Windows native: 21 ShellExecuteEx checks per ABI, plus handled NULL-fetch
  recovery and explicit thread exit on PE32/PE64 (`shell-control-native-r1/`).
- QEMU: the same 42 launch checks; Ctrl+C on a sleeping guest; Ctrl+C followed
  by Ctrl+K on a pure guest spin; handled and unhandled worker NULL fetch,
  on both ABIs. Every case returns to the shell and SSH responds
  (`shell-control-qemu-r4/`).
- The terminal mailbox passes 23 host checks normally and with ASan/UBSan.
  Existing keyboard and terminal tests pass on GCC/Clang, normal/sanitized
  (`keyboard-shell-control-20261004/`).
- OLE regression: 106 ReleaseStgMedium checks and 46 DoDragDrop checks
  (`shell-control-ole-regression-r4/`).

The frozen full build includes the current shared GUI and produces
`kernel-braid-launch-diag-r4.elf`, SHA-256
`c08c28a9b8b299effb94010b350bd1b3d42e985cc5de1b7208e2cafb9295f0ac`.
The initial link ran out of host disk space; after removing generated objects
from prior isolated builds, the incomplete output was deleted and linked
again. Sources, logs, manifests and qualified kernels were retained.
The P1 stage verifies all 231 kernel blocks and the ten fixtures. Native

### 4.254 Braid PLAY exits before its window: DirectSound8 and DirectX gaps (2026-10-04)

The operator reports that PLAY does nothing. The physical game-process log
records two real `Braid.exe` children, PIDs 102 and 127, started at 18:55:41
and 18:56:33 UTC and exiting with `0xC000007A` (procedure not found). The
install-script launcher now runs `SteamService.exe /installscript` instead
of calling a missing ShellExecuteEx entry. The current loader blocker is
`[ABI-MISS] PE32 import DSOUND.dll!#11 has no thunk contract`, after reporting
eight unresolved imports. This happens before the game entry point and
therefore before its window or error UI. It is not evidence of another Steam
freeze or of a new NULL-fetch exception.

The verified 19:00 GOP screenshot, `braid-no-launch-screen-20261004-1900.png`,
shows the signed-in Steam Library and Braid details with the green PLAY
button. This supersedes the earlier pending visual observation in 4.253.
Console request 8 and SSH remain responsive; Steam is retained during the
investigation. Evidence is under `arch/x86/build/msgwait-20261003/` and the
raw physical logs under `arch/x86/build/winsock-send-completion-20261003/`
`p1-lookup-diag/braid-load-failure-dmesg-20261004-190027.log`.

Ordinal 11 is confirmed as `DirectSoundCreate8` using the local Windows
SysWOW64 dsound export table. The shim now exposes the existing supported
public ordinals, plus the named and ordinal Create8 entry with three stdcall
arguments. Device objects retain a version flag: legacy Create/QI behavior
stays separate from IDirectSound8, which adds VerifyCertification. Secondary
buffers from version-8 devices support Buffer8 with all 24 vtable slots;
primary and legacy buffers do not advertise that interface. The PE32 vtables
and argument counts are extended with matching native slots. Ordinary PCM
allocation, locking, duplication, playback and release use the existing
mixer. Unsupported effect/deferred-placement buffers return failure, and no
effect object is fabricated. Stereo 3D buffers are rejected on version-8
devices. CLSID_DirectSound8 supports deferred Initialize through COM.

`FatalAppExitA/W`, another missing Braid import, now use the existing message
backend and ExitProcess, with two stdcall arguments. The current MessageBox
backend logs to serial; this change does not add a graphical error dialog.

The ABI checks follow the documented [DirectSound8 interface](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/ee418035(v=vs.85)),
[Buffer8 interface](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/desktop/ee418055(v=vs.85))
and [FatalAppExit contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/errhandlingapi/nf-errhandlingapi-fatalappexita),
with native results recorded before QEMU qualification. Windows preserves
several caller output values on creation failure, so the tests do not require
those outputs to be cleared. AcquireResources without effects or deferred
resources returns DSERR_INVALIDCALL on both tested Windows ABIs.

Validation:

- `dsound8-native-r4/`: 32 checks per ABI against Windows, including a static
  ordinal-11 import, name/ordinal identity, COM activation, versioned QI,

  DSOUND ordinal failure. Its unresolved direct imports decrease from eight

providing a real D3D9 device/shader path are the next compatibility work;
restarting Steam or the P1 does not supply those missing implementations.

### 4.255 Braid DirectX dependencies and a PE32 stack overwrite (2026-10-04)

The 35 missing provider exports identified in 4.254 now resolve. The audit of
381 distinct imports from the actual Braid, D3DX9_43 and D3DCompiler_43
binaries reports zero misses. The original Microsoft DLLs both complete
DllMain. This establishes dependency loading; it does not establish game
rendering or complete GDI font support.

CRT low-level descriptor data is process-owned and uses the native PE32 and
PE64 layouts for `__pioinfo` and `__badioinfo`. Descriptor updates track file
open/close, text mode, append, EOF and pipe/character state. The extra string,
classification, temporary-file and floating-point functions are checked
against native Windows. The double-precision math subset comes from musl
1.2.5, with its copyright retained and symbols namespaced under
`osito_libm_`. PE32 `_CI*` adapters consume the x87 operands and return their
results through ST(0), preserving the remaining caller FPU stack. Full-range
trigonometric reduction is tested separately from the inaccurate huge-angle
results observed in the legacy native MSVCRT.

The GDI additions reuse the existing font objects and implement charset
translation. Unsupported outline and character-placement operations return
failure; they do not manufacture glyphs or report successful rendering.
Kernel32 adds the ANSI temporary-file wrapper and the modern FreeResource
no-op contract.

An actual D3DCompile call then exposed a separate corruption: the PE32 DLL
passes a four-byte `lpFilePart` output to GetFullPathNameA. The shim wrote an
eight-byte host pointer, clearing the adjacent saved EBP at `0x2020f19c`.
The eventual return fetched address zero. The debugger trace is retained in
`directx-runtime-gdb-r3/`; the complete serial trace confirms that the Win32
exception is contained and SSH/shell survive. GetFullPathNameA and W now
store the output using the guest pointer width. No path-normalization
behavior is changed.

### 4.257 Braid's original SDL2 loads; raw keyboard/mouse delivery works (2026-10-04)

The six SDL2 imports identified in 4.256 now have implementations. The Unicode
wave-output capability query uses the existing PCM device, accepts open output
handles and marshals the 84-byte wide structure separately from the 52-byte ANSI
structure. Zero-length queries succeed; partial copies stay within the supplied
buffer. Native WinMM's unsafe short-buffer writes are not reproduced.

CreateIconFromResource/Ex decode bounded DIB resources into owned GDI bitmap
handles. Coverage includes indexed and true-color pixels, bottom-up orientation,
requested dimensions, cursor hotspots and monochrome AND/XOR masks. The latter
also corrects the icon drawing path to use the mask's logical half-height.
PNG-compressed icon resources are not supported by this decoder.

Raw Input enumerates the OS's merged system mouse and keyboard streams; it does
not invent physical HID product IDs or gamepads. Registrations belong to the
process and replace the previous target for the same usage. Delivery uses the
existing PS/2 and USB paths, preserves unaccelerated relative mouse motion,
handles absolute coordinates separately, and marshals RAWINPUTHEADER as 16/24
bytes for PE32/PE32+. NOLEGACY suppresses normal window messages for registered
consumers. INPUTSINK and EXINPUTSINK are routed according to foreground ownership;
their multi-process behavior remains to be qualified separately. Generic HID
usages may be registered, but no HID report producer is advertised.

Raw packets have generation-tagged handles and process/thread ownership. Queue
insertion and packet allocation share the message lock. Peek without removal
retains the queued packet; delivery of the next raw message retires the preceding
payload. DefWindowProc and window/thread/process cleanup release outstanding
packets. GetRawInputBuffer and physical device arrival/removal notifications are
not implemented by this change.

### 4.259 Original VC2013 runtimes load and execute with timer queues (2026-10-04)

The missing KERNEL32 imports no longer prevent the original `msvcr120.dll`
and `msvcp120.dll` from loading. The PE32 runtime fixture now executes real
CRT heap, string, number and x87 math code and starts a thread through the
DLL's `_beginthreadex`. The child allocates/frees memory, has a distinct errno
slot, returns its exit code and leaves the parent's errno intact. All 17 checks
pass in Windows and QEMU; no older CRT alias replaces these DLLs.

`FindFirstFileExA/W` share the real directory cursor and retain case-sensitive,
directory-only and on-disk filtering across `FindNextFile`. Both information
levels are supported; invalid levels, search operations and flags are rejected.
`QueryDepthSList` reads the correct PE32/PE64 header under the existing SList
lock. `GetNumaHighestNodeNumber` reports the kernel's actual single allocation
domain. `SignalObjectAndWait` retains both objects, checks signal and wait
access, handles event/semaphore/mutex signaling and uses scheduler-backed waits.
Internal retained references are released independently of user close-protection
flags. The PE32/PE64 contract fixture passes 31 checks per architecture in Windows
and QEMU, including output guards, enumeration and cross-thread wakeups.

The new `win32/timer_queue.c` implements explicit/default queues, relative
deadlines, periodic and one-shot callbacks, changes, synchronous deletion,
asynchronous deletion, completion events, timer-thread callbacks and deletion
from a callback. A dispatcher schedules deadlines separately from four persistent
callback workers, so periodic callbacks can overlap. Tokens are process-owned
and never reused; queued/running callbacks keep their timer alive, and completion
is signaled only after they finish. Process cleanup runs after terminating all
Win32 workers. The output handle is four bytes for PE32 and eight for PE64.
The 38-check fixture passes natively for both architectures and four QEMU runs
(32/64 plus repeated launches), including process teardown with a live disabled
timer. Limits are 64 queues and 512 timers system-wide, four callback workers
per queue; `WT_TRANSFER_IMPERSONATION` explicitly fails with ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.

Two newly exported imports expose existing subsystem limitations rather than
claiming success: `ReadConsoleInputW` reports ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED for a valid
console because there is no console INPUT_RECORD backend; `CreateHardLinkW`
reports the same error because writable OsitoFS has no inode-link operation.
Neither capability is exercised by the passing original CRT fixture. Hardlinks,
console record input and impersonation transfer remain unfinished features.

### 4.260 GDI state and legacy FLTK contracts qualified (2026-10-04)

The original Braid launcher now reports **23 unresolved FLTK imports**, down
from 43 with the qualified VC2013 runtime. The launcher's separate
`KERNEL32!CompareFileTime` import is resolved. The real run still stops before
FLTK renders a window, at `OPENGL32!wglSetLayerPaletteEntries`; the shell and
SSH survive and no kernel exception is observed. This is further dependency
progress, not a running Braid game or a D3D9 rendering backend.

GDI now has a per-DC SaveDC/RestoreDC stack with absolute and negative relative
levels. Restoring consumes the target and newer states. Supported colors,
text alignment, current position, mapping/world transforms, clipping and
brush/font/bitmap/palette selections are preserved. Saved brush references
are retained; bitmap/font/palette deletion checks live and saved selections.
Memory bitmaps are rebound by handle. Window surface pointers, resized geometry
and nested BeginPaint clip ownership are not restored from stale snapshots.
Owned DC stacks are released at process teardown before brush/palette storage.
The state contract follows [SaveDC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-savedc)
and [RestoreDC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-restoredc).

Window/viewport origins and extents, mapping modes, LPtoDP/DPtoLP and GetDCOrgEx
have real state and transformations. SetPixel and GetPixel use those transforms,
clip against the DC and read/write the selected bitmap's actual pixel format.
GetPixel no longer assumes a top-down 32-bit surface or returns raw ARGB as
COLORREF. Logical palettes support creation, selection, entry reads/edits,
object queries and PALETTEINDEX pixel colors. A true-color display realizes
zero physical palette entries; UpdateColors fails because RC_PALETTE is absent.
StartDocA/StartPage/EndPage/EndDoc reject non-printer DCs with SP_ERROR rather
than claiming a printed job. See [UpdateColors](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-updatecolors).

CompareFileTime compares the two unsigned 64-bit values without alignment
assumptions. RegOpenKeyW uses the existing registry implementation and its
PE32/PE64 output-handle writer. EnumFontFamiliesW uses the existing wide-font
callback path; COMCTL32's _TrackMouseEvent delegates to USER32. Native comparison
exposed a preexisting TME_QUERY bug: it now queries the calling thread's tracking
without requiring an input HWND, and returns zero HWND/time when inactive.

`gdi_state_pe.c` has 41 native checks per architecture for DC levels, independent
clip copies, selected objects, mapping/world transforms, 16/24/32-bit pixels,
bottom-up rows, palette edits and pointer guards. `fltk_legacy_pe.c` adds 22 per
architecture for timestamp ordering, callback parameters, temporary registry
readback/cleanup, tracking structures, print rejection and client/nonclient DC
screen origins. Native baselines are `gdi-state-native-r2/` and
`fltk-legacy-native-r3/`; all **126 new PE checks** pass on Windows and QEMU.

The combined QEMU qualification is **536 passing checks**: 186 PE checks
(including icon and earlier DirectX/GDI regressions), 40 region checks, 32 DIB
checks, 102 window-model checks, 10 dialog checks and 166 input checks. SSH
responds afterward. GCC and clang clipped-blit/DIB-row host regressions pass
normally and with ASan/UBSan; the screen regression also passes with sanitizers.
Evidence is `gdi-state-qualified-qemu-r1/`, `gdi-state-blt-r1/`,
`gdi-state-dib-rows-r1/` and `gdi-state-screen-r1/` under `arch/x86/build` (the
QEMU directory is under `msgwait-20261003/`).

Limits remain explicit: the other text/blit/shape drawing paths have not all
been migrated to the full transform; pens and further DC attributes are still
incomplete. Selected/saved bitmap and font deletion is refused, without Windows'
deferred-deletion behavior. Font enumeration inherits the limited font mapper,
and registry names inherit existing wide-to-ANSI conversion. Physical display
dimensions are derived from the existing 96-DPI virtual display, not EDID.
Fractional conversion rounding is not claimed to exactly match Windows' cached
fixed-point arithmetic. Existing DC concurrency remains caller-synchronized.

### 4.261 FLTK WGL imports and bitmap display lists (2026-10-05)

The six missing WGL imports now resolve with PE32/PE64 thunk contracts. The
original Braid launcher, with its original SDL2, FLTK, VC2013 and P1 Mesa module,
reduces FLTK's unresolved imports from **23 to 17**. It stops at
`USER32!OpenIcon`; the shell returns without an exception. This is loader
progress, not a running game or a qualified P1 graphics backend.

`wglCreateLayerContext(dc, 0)` delegates to the existing main-context creation.
The advertised format has no overlays or underlays: their context, descriptor
and palette operations fail, and a failed descriptor query preserves its output.
`wglSwapLayerBuffers` requires a current context with a backend. The main-plane
bit delegates to real readback/presentation; empty or absent-plane sets have no
work. Native Windows probes confirmed that the latter fail without a context
and succeed with one. See Microsoft's
[layer-swap contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-wglswaplayerbuffers).

`wglUseFontBitmapsW` obtains glyph pixels through the same raster helper used by
GDI text and compiles actual Mesa `glBitmap` display lists. It does not use the
query fallback functions. It preserves the unpack settings and PBO binding,
handles a blank space's advance, and creates empty lists for glyphs absent from
the bitmap face, as required by the
[font-bitmap contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/nf-wingdi-wglusefontbitmapsw).
Missing native operations, invalid ranges, nested list compilation and a full
client-attribute stack fail rather than reporting a completed list.

### 4.262 OpenIcon and clipboard ownership (2026-10-05)

The original Braid launcher now reduces FLTK's unresolved imports from **17 to
15**, stopping at `USER32!GetDCEx`. `OpenIcon` and `GetClipboardOwner` have real
implementations and PE32/PE64 export contracts. The shell returns without an
exception; this does not establish game startup or rendering.

`OpenIcon` sends `WM_QUERYOPEN` only for an iconic window, respects a veto and
revalidates the handle after the callback, which can destroy the window. A
hidden non-iconic window stays hidden. Native Windows confirms that a formerly
maximized window restores to its normal placement through this API, and that a
valid request returns TRUE even when the callback vetoes restoration.

Clipboard state now separates the opening process/thread/window from the
content owner. Repeated opens by the same thread and window are non-nesting;
another thread cannot open or close it. Data access requires an open clipboard,
while the existing job UI restrictions retain their error precedence.
`EmptyClipboard` transfers ownership and notifies the previous owner after
releasing the IRQ lock. Window destruction clears stale HWNDs; thread/process
exit releases an abandoned open lock. The native fixture uses a private desktop
and read-only clipboard access; it never empties or replaces the user's data.
Ownership mutation tests run only in an isolated QEMU instance.

the prior GDI state, FLTK legacy, icon, DirectX/GDI, region, DIB, window, dialog
and input tests give **606 counted QEMU checks**. In addition, both complete

SSH responds after the QEMU tests. Evidence is under

`user-owner-qemu-r1/`, `braid-launcher-user-owner-r1/` and
`user-owner-qualified-checkpoint.json`.

### 4.263 GetDCEx common contexts and retained visibility (2026-10-05)

The original FLTK DLL calls `GetDCEx` at `0x10035372`, through IAT entry
`0x100ee564`, with `DCX_CACHE` and a NULL region. This path now has a real
common-context implementation and both PE ABI contracts. The original launcher
reduces its unresolved FLTK imports from **15 to 14**, stopping at
`USER32!MessageBeep`; it returns to the shell without an exception.

Each common DC has independent attributes and a thread-owned borrow. Release,
thread exit, process exit and window destruction dispose of its resources.
`ReleaseDC` now rejects invalid and memory DCs. The existing pooled contexts
used by `GetDC` and `BeginPaint` remain on their previous lifecycle.

The system-visible region is separate from the application's selected clip,
and is therefore not removed by `SelectClipRgn(NULL)` or `RestoreDC`.
Intersection/exclusion inputs start in screen coordinates, while a retained
extra clip stays relative to the window after a move, as confirmed on Windows.
Transferred input regions are released with the borrow. The visible region is
refreshed for drawing after moves, resizes, show/hide and sibling destruction.
Client and whole-window contexts share the appropriate underlying pixels.
Both simple fast copies and complex pixel paths honor the clip. See the
[GetDCEx contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-getdcex).

### 4.264 MessageBeep through the PCM mixer (2026-10-05)

The original Braid launcher now resolves `USER32!MessageBeep`, reducing its
FLTK imports from **14 to 13**. Its next failure is `USER32!ValidateRgn`;
the original DLLs return to the shell without an exception or kernel halt.
This still does not establish game rendering or successful game startup.

`MessageBeep` has both PE ABI contracts and queues real PCM through WinMM.
The five alert types select their registry WAV events, with a default event
and then a 200 ms PCM tone as fallbacks. Explicitly empty current events stay
silent. Alert voices are separate from application `PlaySound` voices, so
replacement and cancellation do not interrupt the other kind. Both use the
existing mixer, asynchronous dispatcher and process cleanup. See the
[MessageBeep contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-messagebeep)
and [PlaySound contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/dd743680(v=vs.85)).

QEMU checks per architecture with HDA**, and **5 per architecture without
an audio backend**. The existing full WinMM waveOut/PlaySound/MCI regression
and no-device regression both exit with code 0; SSH responds afterward.
The actual QEMU stereo PCM passes **19 additional checks** for event
selection, fallback tones, silence, simultaneous application/alert audio,
an 800 ms alert surviving `PlaySound(NULL)`, and cleanup on process exit.
Eighty consecutive replacements also retain voice capacity.

The final audio fixture keeps an independent silent waveOut voice active.
This matters because the HDA backend stops after its last active source;
the first WAV capture omitted those inactive intervals and could not prove
silence durations. A subsequent observer verifies that exiting a process
does not leave either audible voice playing. Sound-scheme modifications
are confined to the disposable QEMU image; native mode only calls the API.

### 4.265 Exact update regions and reentrant background erasure (2026-10-05)

The original Braid launcher now resolves `USER32!ValidateRgn` and
`GetUpdateRgn`, reducing unresolved FLTK imports from **13 to 11**. The
next failure is `GDI32!CreatePolygonRgn`. The launcher returns to the shell
without an exception or kernel halt; game rendering is still unverified.

Windows now retain a bounded rectangle region instead of a single bounding
box. Invalidation unions areas, validation subtracts them, and both clip to
the client. `InvalidateRgn` copies its input; `GetUpdateRgn` copies into an
existing caller region without validating. Updates commit under the message
lock only after all region operations succeed. BeginPaint and background
erasure carry exact clips through PatBlt, BitBlt and DIB drawing, including
disjoint areas and holes that application clip changes cannot remove.

Native probes established callback order: BeginPaint consumes its update
before WM_ERASEBKGND, preserving any callback reinvalidation. GetUpdateRgn
and GetUpdateRect instead return the region after that callback, including
an empty result when it destroys the window. A query sends an erase request
once; an unhandled erase remains visible through PAINTSTRUCT.fErase without
repeated callbacks. A subsequent erasing invalidation renews the request.
No application callback runs while the update lock is held.

The extracted `dxwsetup.exe` calls `WinVerifyTrustEx` with

and provider flags `0x1580`. It then obtains signer zero through the two
`WTHelper*` functions and passes its real `pChainContext` to policy **7**,
`CERT_CHAIN_POLICY_MICROSOFT_ROOT`. This is a public-key identity policy,
separate from authenticating the file and validating its certificate chain.

The four missing exports in this path now have implementations:

- `CertVerifyCertificateChainPolicy` implements policy 7 with SHA-256 hashes
  of the Microsoft root **public keys**, not certificate names. Native Windows
  x86/x64 established the acceptance matrix for 13 public roots and three
  altered certificates. Product roots and the 2011 application root have
  different acceptance sets. The application/test flag combination reports
  `E_INVALIDARG` in the policy status. The BOOL result and status error retain
  their different meanings. Other policy IDs return unsupported.
- `WinVerifyTrustEx` shares the existing PE Authenticode verifier with
  `WinVerifyTrust`. It retains independently owned certificate contexts and
  the verified signer/countersigner chains. The provider, signer and provider
  certificate structures have explicit x86/x64 layouts; the x86 signer chain
  pointer is at offset `0x28`, as required by DirectX.
- `WTHelperProvDataFromStateData` and `WTHelperGetProvSignerFromChain` resolve
  only the calling process's retained state and validate signer indexes.
  CLOSE releases it and clears the caller's state handle. Normal/forced
  process exit and Win32 reset also reclaim this state. A guest test leaves
  all 64 state slots open and exits; the next process verifies files normally.

The actual Microsoft `dsetup.dll` signature exposed two legacy algorithms
missing from the old verifier: RSA/SHA-1 for the CMS signature and its signing
certificate, and the OIW RSA/SHA-1 identifier `1.3.14.3.2.29` on the Microsoft
Code Signing PCA certificate. The new legacy certificate-link entry point
checks these signatures, including agreement between the inner and outer
AlgorithmIdentifiers. TLS continues to use the existing modern link verifier
and its cache; SHA-1 acceptance is confined to the Authenticode path.

The verified timestamp on this fixture is Unix time `1301508758`. The
signature, chain, EKU, validity at the applicable time, and trust-anchor policy
are checked before any signer chain is exposed. An unavailable clock is not
treated as a valid date. `WTD_LIFETIME_SIGNING_FLAG` uses the current date.

WinTrust reads Software Publishing `State` from the guest's current-user
registry, with the native-observed default `0x23c00`. Its offline and timestamp
revocation settings are applied separately from digest/signature/chain
validation. Individual/commercial signing statements select the matching
offline policy. Permitted unavailable revocation remains marked as unknown
in the retained chain; an authenticated revocation fails validation. A guest
test sets strict policy zero, verifies rejection, then restores the original
registry value. The native Windows host's trust settings are never modified.

The original signed DLL is accepted with both the basic test options and the
exact DirectX provider flags. Tests reject changed PE content, a changed CMS
signature, and a changed signature on the signer certificate. A damaged
embedded intermediate alone is not a reliable negative native test: Windows
can replace it with a valid intermediate from its certificate cache.

### 4.270 HTTP transport groundwork for URLMON downloads (2026-10-05)

The remaining DirectX import uses an HTTP URL, a destination filename, NULL
`pCaller`, reserved zero and an `IBindStatusCallback`. Disassembly shows real
OnProgress cancellation (`E_ABORT`) and progress-bar updates. OnStartBinding
retains an `IBinding` reference; OnStopBinding releases it. GetBindInfo and
OnDataAvailable return `E_NOTIMPL`. This still requires a URLMON provider and
proper callback/IBinding lifetime implementation; merely resolving the import
does not constitute a downloader.

The kernel HTTP client now has `http_open_port(session, host, port, use_tls)`
for an explicit HTTP/HTTPS scheme and port. Existing `http_open` remains
HTTPS on 443; asynchronous HTTPS behavior is unchanged. Plain HTTP uses the
same session ownership and parser with TCP I/O, including partial-send
completion and cleanup that does not send a TLS close record on plaintext.

The body reader previously returned a positive partial byte count after a
premature close. It now rejects truncated Content-Length and chunked bodies,
missing terminal chunks, malformed chunk sizes/separators and integer
overflow. Content-Length zero completes immediately. Connection-delimited
bodies require EOF instead of accepting an idle timeout as completion.
Content-Length syntax/overflow is checked before body delivery. Callback
cancellation remains a failure rather than successful partial output.

`test-http-transfer.sh` runs the real parser over scripted fragmented
transports. Per compiler, 204 response/cancellation/timeout scenarios exercise
plaintext, TLS 1.3 dispatch and TLS 1.2 fallback with receive fragments of
1/2/7/4096 bytes and partial plaintext sends. **8,030 checks pass**, plus the
existing **151 session-ownership checks**, with both GCC and Clang under
AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. These are host transport
tests, not real network or TLS-handshake integration results.

SHA-256 `dc24a9199e6178fe3298a4605e4f0cf5520de229921ed53d9db0ee798d5951b5`.
Evidence is `http-transfer-progress-review.json` and
`http-transfer-probe-r1/` under `arch/x86/build/msgwait-20261003/`.

### 4.271 URLDownloadToFileW: actual transfers and installer entry (2026-10-05)

Added `win32/urlmon_shim.c` and registered `urlmon.dll` and its PE32 ABI
provider. `URLDownloadToFileW` now performs synchronous HTTP/HTTPS transfers
through the kernel HTTP client, with up to ten redirects, a destination-side
CREATE_NEW temporary file and a replace rename only after a complete download.
Local `file:///` input is supported as well. Caller-supplied destination paths
remain UTF-16. The external installer and its Microsoft payloads remain outside
the OS build.

The guest receives a real IBinding vtable with matching PE32 stdcall thunks or
Microsoft x64 callbacks. The object owns references independently of callback
lifetime, and supports QueryInterface, AddRef/Release, Abort and priority state.
OnStartBinding receives that object; progress and OnStopBinding are delivered to
the caller. Callback references balance on both successful and failed binds.
Native Windows probes establish the wrapper's unusual distinction: cancellation
returns S_OK from URLDownloadToFileW, with E_ABORT in OnStopBinding; successful
completion reports S_FALSE to OnStopBinding. The observed wrapper does not
forward OnDataAvailable to the caller. Missing HTTP resources return
INET_E_OBJECT_NOT_FOUND, while missing file resources return
INET_E_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND. A destination failure remains a callback failure,
not a fabricated downloaded payload.

Added strict numeric IPv4 handling to synchronous HTTP opens, avoiding a DNS
query for addresses such as 10.0.2.2. `http_abort` releases a stopped owner's
session even during a handshake; URLMON teardown is connected to existing main
and child process cleanup paths. `MoveFileExW_k32` is exposed internally so
URLMON uses the existing Unicode replace-rename implementation. Its API behavior
is unchanged.

### 4.272 DirectX administrator gate and explicit native launch role (2026-10-05)

Added advpack IsNTAdmin, backed by the process/impersonation token model.
Enabled Administrators membership is required, including restricting-SID
intersection. IsUserAnAdmin and TokenElevation now use that same effective
membership instead of unconditional success. Native advpack preserves reserved
arguments and caches a positive result; the shim follows that legacy behavior
per process, with cache cleanup on normal and forced exits. Access checks do
not use the advisory cache.

The trusted native shell supports `winexec --admin file.exe [args...]`, creating
a primary token with enabled Administrators membership and high integrity before
PE code runs. Child processes inherit it; subsequent ordinary launches receive
the original normal token. This is an explicit local launch role, not a UAC UI
or automatic manifest elevation. No Windows privileges were added. The inner
DirectX executable requests requireAdministrator; the original installer stays
external to the OS build.

### 4.276 Visible read-only EDIT text and scroll contracts (2026-10-05)

The black license area was an EDIT class without a drawing procedure. EDIT now
shares the refcounted standard-control lifetime and draws its stored Unicode
text with the parent control-color brush and borrowed font. Multiline display
supports word wrapping, explicit formatting rectangles, line counts, vertical
line/page/wheel scrolling, and read-only navigation. Password controls mask their
display and support the password-character messages without changing stored text.
Printing intersects the client and formatting clips. Destruction from a color
callback is covered. This is not a complete editable control: selection, caret,
typing/undo/clipboard, horizontal scrolling and edit-handle APIs remain pending.

The corrected native fixture passes 88 checks per ABI. It also retains existing
BUTTON/STATIC, owner drawing, lifetime and cross-thread text checks. Native EDIT
rounds a custom formatting rectangle down to whole text lines; the initial test
incorrectly expected its raw requested bottom. The oracle also measures the
first visible line after bottom scrolling. Before the implementation, QEMU has
nine failures per ABI in the new EDIT checks.

handler both targeted the wrong button and passed the kernel literal "Close"
through a PE32 window-procedure thunk. The resulting truncated pointer
0264a467 faults in MultiByteToWideChar. The native oracle and Microsoft's message
contract establish that Cancel keeps its label and is disabled; only IDOK, when
present, changes to Close. The corrected handler implements that distinction
and copies any nonempty internal text into the owning guest heap before sending.

### 4.278 WOW64 file redirection for external runtime installation (2026-10-05)

The 32-bit DirectX installer queries System32 but its file operations must use
SysWOW64. A dedicated filesystem resolver now applies that redirection once,
without changing GetSystemDirectory/GetFullPathName or other lexical directory
queries. System32, lastgood/System32, regedit.exe, the six documented excluded
subdirectories and the 32-bit-only Sysnative alias are covered. The redirector
is case-insensitive and requires whole path components. Microsoft documents the
[filesystem contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winprog64/file-system-redirector)
and the [per-thread disable/restore contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wow64apiset/nf-wow64apiset-wow64disablewow64fsredirection).

Wow64DisableWow64FsRedirection, Revert and Enable use thread-owned state. Nested
restoration preserves the previous disabled state; new threads, child processes
and subsequent shell launches start with redirection enabled. PE32 output values
are four bytes wide. The native 64-bit API returns ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION without
changing its output, as observed by the read-only Windows oracle.

A process keeps both lexical and physical current directories. Relative Win32
opens remain attached to the physical directory after disabling redirection.
A child instead reopens its initial lexical directory with its own architecture
and default state: the native oracle demonstrated this for both inherited CWD
and explicit dot. A child explicitly rooted at C:\ no longer falls back to its
parent's global current directory. Direct NT RootDirectory opens are redirected,
including a separately opened native System32 handle, matching the native probe.
Kernel-resolved Win32 file opens bypass a second NT redirection pass.

The filesystem consumers updated here include CreateFile A/W, copy/move/delete,
attributes, directory creation/removal, FindFirstFile, process image selection,
DLL search and explicit loading, CRT stat/chmod, file-security paths, GDI font
paths and INI cache/persistence. Loader application/dependency directories already
resolved to physical paths are retained. INI writes use their physical cache
identity, so writing through Sysnative is not redirected back into SysWOW64.
NtCreateFile also gains the missing PE32 marshalling for OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES,
UNICODE_STRING, output handles and IO_STATUS_BLOCK; guards and status/information
checks cover both output layouts. Other direct NT I/O entry points are not
claimed to have been fully audited by this change.

### 4.279 InstallEngine2 catalogs, downloads and TLS record tails (2026-10-05)

The original DirectX web installer now activates InstallEngine2, loads its CIF,
selects DXUpdate, downloads the real Microsoft cabinet and receives successful
completion callbacks. The redistributable and its payload remain external files;
neither is part of the kernel image or build inputs. No Microsoft installer or
setup DLL was executed on the Windows development host.

New installengine.c registers the class through the existing OLE activation
registry. winexec now calls ole32_shim_init; previously that initializer was not
called. COM objects expose ABI-correct PE32/PE64 vtables, keep file/enumerator
references, and release kernel metadata on owner-process teardown. CIF parsing
uses bounded file, section, line and expansion limits. It implements the observed
catalog queries, neutral Strings substitution, component/group enumeration,
version/size/platform metadata and action selection. The component/group/mode
views are owned by ICifFile and do not begin with IUnknown. The public interface
layout is described by [Wine's inseng.idl](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/include/inseng.idl)
and its [staging interface additions](https://github.com/wine-staging/wine-staging/blob/master/patches/inseng-Implementation/0001-inseng-Implement-CIF-reader-and-download-functions.patch);
behavior was measured with the native Windows probes rather than copied from
that implementation.

Native observations include an initially non-null empty CIF object while the
engine is NOTREADY; READY after SetLocalCif; zero-based URL indices; successful
truncation of GetID; packed version DWORDs; a 32-byte GetSizes result; and action
values limited to NONE/INSTALL. The query fixtures never download or install.
The separate transfer fixture copies only its own small local file and exercises
success, default trust rejection, explicit IGNORETRUST, cancellation and balanced
callback references. Windows DownloadComponents copies the payload even with
URLF_EXTRACT; it does not extract it in this operation.

Downloads run in an owner Win32 worker, retain the callback independently of
registration, and report start/progress/completion through the guest ABI. A
reserved temporary file prevents failure from overwriting the final file. Trust
checking is required unless the caller explicitly supplies IGNORETRUST; the real
DirectX bootstrap supplies 0x10. Unsigned non-PE data is rejected by default.
CAB/CAT verification and general InstallComponents are still unsupported. URLMON
has a separate non-exported kernel callback entry; public callbacks continue to
require valid executable guest addresses. This fixes PE64 internal dispatch
without weakening the public callback validator.

The first real HTTPS transfer exposed an independent TLS 1.2 bug: tls_recv copied
only the caller's capacity and discarded the rest of the authenticated record.
HTTP requests 4095/4096-byte reads while records can carry 16384 bytes. Per-connection
application buffers now retain the tail until the caller consumes it. Zero-length
reads consume nothing, close clears pending data, and malformed short alerts are
rejected. The TLS fixture uses the real AES-GCM record decoder, 40 combinations of
transport fragmentation and caller capacity, and two interleaved connections.
It fails before the fix (112 checks) and passes afterward (410771 checks), also
under AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. The bad-tag case verifies that
unauthenticated plaintext is never returned. HTTP's existing host suite passes
8044 checks. TLS 1.3 behavior is not claimed to be qualified by this change.

## 4.280. Manifest version policy and the DirectX core prerequisite (2026-10-05)

GetVersion and GetVersionExA/W now use the main executable's embedded
RT_MANIFEST/ID 1 compatibility declaration: legacy 6.2.9200, Windows 8.1
6.3.9600, or the configured Windows 10 platform version. PEB/system/file
versions remain the platform version. The bounded manifest reader handles
UTF-8, UTF-16 LE/BE, namespace prefixes, comments, processing instructions and
CDATA. Unknown namespaces and malformed/truncated resources do not enable a
newer version. External sidecar manifests and general activation-context
processing are not implemented by this reader.

GetVersionEx accepts exactly the basic or extended structure size, preserves
that size and LastError on success, fills the extended service-pack/suite/
workstation fields, and returns ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER without writing on
invalid sizes. It validates guest memory before reading/writing the structure.
VerifyVersionInfo uses the same process version and hierarchical version tuple.
Native probes additionally establish signed DWORD tuple comparisons, strict
comparison behavior when the final service-pack field is omitted, and the
condition constructor's highest-field selection and OR accumulation. Probes
compare the defined condition fields, not Windows' opaque reserved high bit.

References: Microsoft's [version policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sysinfo/targeting-your-application-at-windows-8-1),
[GetVersionEx](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/sysinfoapi/nf-sysinfoapi-getversionexa)
and [VerifyVersionInfo](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-verifyversioninfoa).
The same PE32/PE64 probes run on native Windows and Osito-K. version-probe-r7
passes 642 checks on each system, including 2700 mixed-condition requests with
matching BOOL/LastError digests. The earlier r3 probe reports 388 failures on the
previous kernel and none after the initial fix. The manifest host suite passes
20283 cases/checks under ASan/UBSan, including exact-size allocations, every
truncation of a complete manifest and 20000 random inputs. Early probe failures
also exposed incorrect test assumptions; those evidence directories are retained.

### 4.281. DirectX CAB Authenticode and RFC 3161 timestamps (2026-10-05)

The original web installer downloads the complete dxupdate.cab, but the previous
WinVerifyTrust backend recognizes only PE certificate tables and returns a file
error for CAB. authenticode.c now selects the CAB format from its MSCF signature,
validates the signed-CAB header and bounded CMS range, and verifies its file hash,
CMS signature, timestamp, code-signing chain and existing revocation policies.
No installer, Microsoft DLL or Microsoft CAB is added to the kernel or OS image.

The CAB SIP contract was measured with read-only CryptSIPCreateIndirectData and
WinVerifyTrust calls on native Windows, using the original file and controlled
mutations. The supported layout has a 20-byte header reserve and zero folder/data
reserves. The main hash includes iCabinet and excludes signature metadata and
reserved padding. For this layout, the enhanced SPC_LINK serialized attribute
binds the four-byte little-endian CAB length with the same digest algorithm.
Both hashes are checked. Header reserved-byte mutations which Windows accepts
remain accepted; changes to body, cabinet index, signature, certificate,
timestamp or enhanced digest are rejected. Appended/truncated CAB files and
out-of-bounds signature ranges fail before any trust result is emitted.

RFC 3161 support verifies the TSTInfo messageImprint against the primary
signature, the nested CMS content type/signature, the ESSCertID/ESSCertIDv2
certificate hash and optional issuer/serial, the dedicated time-stamping EKU,
and the timestamp chain at genTime. Valid decimal fractional seconds are
accepted without relaxing X.509 certificate-time parsing. Future timestamps
are rejected when a clock is available. Invalid present timestamps no longer
silently fall back to the current time. Legacy PKCS#9 countersignatures remain
supported. Microsoft's TSA certificate in this CAB has a noncritical EKU;
native Windows accepts it, so the verifier follows that observed contract
while still requiring id-kp-timeStamping instead of anyExtendedKeyUsage. The
intermediate r2 experiment requiring critical EKU correctly exposed that
compatibility difference and is retained as failed evidence, not deployed.

References: Microsoft [CAB format](https://download.microsoft.com/download/4/D/A/4DA14F27-B4EF-4170-A6E6-5B1EF85B1BAA/%5BMS-CAB%5D.pdf),
[Authenticode constants](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/hh968145(v=vs.85)),
[CryptSIPCreateIndirectData](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/mssip/nf-mssip-cryptsipcreateindirectdata),
[RFC 3161](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3161) and
[RFC 5035](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5035). CAB hash details above are
native-oracle observations, not a claim that the short OID documentation
fully specifies CAB hashing.
