### 4.282. Cabinet extraction and explicit resource languages (2026-10-05)

The web installer now has SetupIterateCabinetA/W callbacks instead of failing
GetProcAddress during DXUpdate extraction. The callback selects each target,
skips members or stops iteration, with the measured native error contract.
Both pointer layouts (PE32 packed and PE64) and ANSI/Unicode strings are handled.
Paths pass through ordinary Win32 I/O, so the caller's WOW64 redirection applies.
Payloads remain external files; no Microsoft executable, DLL or CAB becomes a
kernel/build input. The original installer remains on the P1 USB separately.

The shared CAB reader now validates bounded filenames, folder/block ranges,
optional CFDATA checksums, stored sizes and exact MSZIP output sizes. It retains
MSZIP history across blocks and caches the decoded folder prefix. Metadata-only
iteration does not decompress skipped members; an early file can still be read
when a later block is truncated. Empty members and the case-insensitive name
extraction interface used by MSI remain supported. LZX, Quantum and cabinets
spanning volumes are still unsupported.

File-system integration fixes distinguish a missing containing directory from
a missing final component in NtCreateFile, and connect regular-file DOS
attributes to OsitoFS's existing persistent metadata APIs. FileBasicInformation
sets/queries those attributes and timestamps. Newly extracted files receive the
archive bit, including cabinets which omit it. A failed decompression removes
the incomplete target; a callback error after successful extraction retains it.
Native FILEPATHS.Flags is unspecified/uninitialized in the oracle and is not an
exact comparison target; Osito-K initializes it to zero.

The first installer rerun extracts dxupdate.dll/inf/cif and identifies the next
missing import, KERNEL32!FindResourceExA. FindResourceExA/W now share the resource
parser with FindResourceA/W. Explicit languages try exact, primary-neutral and
neutral entries, then report ERROR_RESOURCE_LANG_NOT_FOUND. Neutral/default-user/
default-system requests use the configured UI preference and fallback order.
Successful calls preserve LastError. Per-thread UI-language storage and MUI
satellite files are not added by this change.

### 4.283. SetupAPI INF navigation and compact line text (2026-10-05)

SetupFindFirstLineA/W, SetupFindNextLine and SetupGetLineTextA/W now operate on
the existing process-owned INF handles. Contexts use the PE32/PE64 layout and
contain integer handles instead of kernel pointers. Lookup merges repeated
section names case-insensitively, preserves duplicate-key order and supports
in-place iteration. Invalid/stale contexts are rejected. Failed lookups and
end-of-section leave the caller's context unchanged.

The shared parser now joins backslash continuations, normalizes quoted keys and
preserves quoted whitespace/doubled quotes in fields. A comment-only physical
line terminates a continuation; joining ordinary tokens adds no space. Physical
line numbers are retained for parse errors. String substitution is one pass,
including percent escaping, unknown tokens and nested Strings references.
The file-copy implementation uses the same corrected field/substitution helpers.

GetLineText assembles comma-separated fields after those transformations. Size
queries include the terminator, null output buffers are accepted, and short
buffers remain unchanged while RequiredSize is returned. Successful queries set
LastError to zero. Fields are bounded to 4096 bytes including NUL, compact output
to 1 MiB, matching the existing source-file bound. The parser still does not add
localized Strings-section selection, percent directory-ID expansion or full
Unicode source-INF support. SetupOpenInfFileW is not added by this change.

### 4.285. DLL reload and failed-attach cleanup (2026-10-05)

The original DirectX wizard reached the optional-component selection page,
then reloaded dxupdate.dll. The loader skipped PROCESS_DETACH for PE32 DLLs,
leaving DXUpdate's singleton mutex alive. The second DllMain returned FALSE
with "DXUpdate is running already", but the PE32 loader published the image
anyway. Its uninitialized CRT subsequently called address zero.

Final FreeLibrary now calls DllMain(PROCESS_DETACH) for both bitnesses, even
when DisableThreadLibraryCalls was used; its return value is ignored. A normal
FALSE return from PROCESS_ATTACH triggers PROCESS_DETACH before unmapping,
removes the module and reports ERROR_DLL_INIT_FAILED (1114). LoadLibrary keeps
that error instead of overwriting it with ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND. The PE32 cleanup
also removes the image's static-TLS descriptors and blocks, then releases its
TLS index, so later thread creation does not read an unmapped template.
Abnormal process teardown still avoids invoking arbitrary DLL code.

This follows the documented [DllMain lifecycle](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/dlls/dllmain).
The static-TLS tests cover sequential unload/reload and subsequent thread
creation. They do not establish all concurrent unload/thread-start interleavings
or implement missing TLS PROCESS_DETACH callback behavior.

### 4.293. Legacy CRT aligned allocations for XAudio2_1

The original XAudio2_1 DLL stops import binding on _aligned_malloc and
_aligned_free. These exports now allocate from the existing process heap,
retain the original base in a guest-width hidden header, and release that
base through the same heap. The alignment is rounded up to pointer width.
Size plus metadata/padding is checked against the guest's maximum request
before allocation, including 32-bit overflow on the 64-bit kernel. Failure
sets ENOMEM; a non-power-of-two alignment uses the existing invalid-parameter
path with EINVAL. NULL free does nothing, and heap calls preserve LastError.

Native legacy msvcrt.dll accepts zero size and zero alignment. The newer
documented CRT rejects zero size, so this implementation explicitly follows
the legacy provider imported by the original audio DLL, not the full modern
UCRT validation contract. Native legacy MSVCRT does not export the public
invalid-handler setter: the first probe failed that export check; r2 was built
but not run. Qualified r3 covers returning zero/overflow cases and skips
non-power-of-two fatal native cases, which need separate processes. The shim's
existing returning-handler mechanism is not established by those native rows.
No aligned realloc, offset allocation or msize exports are added.

Native PE32 and PE64 each pass 153 checks and 43 comparison rows: alignments
1 through 65536, allocation sizes 1 through 4097, writable ranges, overflow,
zero cases, NULL release and 48 simultaneous independent allocations. QEMU
and P1 each pass 486 checks, including math and CPU-feature regressions, and

original XAudio2_1.dll now loads, registers, unregisters and unloads. It is

Read-only disassembly of unmodified dxwsetup.exe identifies the section source:
InitInstallEngine at 0x1008271 formats object+0x260 with the language suffix;
SetAction is called at 0x10082b0. The constructor selects legacy 5.1/5.2
platform strings at 0x1007e9f..0x1007f2b. A modern 6.2 result follows the
architecture-only branch at 0x1007f62 without initializing object+0x260.
This static path explains the observed uninitialized section; a runtime
memory watchpoint has not been used. GetVersionEx's manifest-based modern
behavior already matches the native oracle and is not globally changed to
make this legacy path pass. The simulated registry Version is not installed
on P1, and optional-runtime success is not relabeled as a clean install.

### 4.300. Standalone DLL registration utility and alternate loader search

Osito-K now has its own freestanding PE32/PE64 regsvr32 source under
arch/x86/win32/programs. `make -C arch/x86 win32-system-tools` builds
build/win32-system-tools/Windows/SysWOW64/regsvr32.exe (PE32) and
Windows/System32/regsvr32.exe (PE64), with clang/llvm-dlltool/lld-link.
They are ordinary files for the OS system directories, not kernel payloads.
No Microsoft executable, DLL or CAB enters this target. An OsitoFS image can
receive each EXE with tools/ositofs/ositofs-write3 and the corresponding
--dest /Windows/SysWOW64/regsvr32.exe or /Windows/System32/regsvr32.exe.

The utility parses the native switches, initializes OLE in an STA, loads the
actual requested DLL, calls its registration/unregistration/DllInstall export,
keeps the module loaded across a combined operation, and releases it. It
preserves native stage exit codes, HRESULT failure handling, last-error
selection across multiple files, silent mode, quoted arguments and UTF-16
installation arguments. Native installed Windows regsvr32 and the Osito-K
program produce identical callback traces and exit codes for 34 cases per
ABI. These native checks execute only the custom regsvr_fixture.c DLL,
which writes a local diagnostic log and does not modify the host registry.
The in-process test launcher passes 207 checks per ABI on native Windows.

The QEMU run exposed a separate loader defect: flags=8 incorrectly excluded
all normal directories for a bare DLL name. dll_find_file now distinguishes
legacy alternate search from restricted LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_* policies;
dll_load_from_fs_ex temporarily prioritizes the target DLL directory for
its imports and restores the prior search context. Mixing these policies
is rejected with ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER before a cached-module lookup.

and UNKNOWN for the wrapper/new program/test symbols. The full kernel build
includes all 14 GUI source inputs.

### 4.307. HDA startup and hotreload DMA ownership

Investigation of the P1 audio incident found an independent ordering defect:
hda_init enabled PCI bus mastering before stopping or resetting engines
inherited from the previous kernel. kexec had cleared PCI bus mastering but
left HDA RUN bits, DMA pointers and the codec link live. Re-enabling it could
therefore resume DMA against memory now owned by the replacement kernel.
Reset assertion was also unchecked and the reset/codec detection delays
were CPU-dependent loop counts. This is a demonstrated driver defect, not
yet a confirmed diagnosis of the physical P1 sound.

HDA now enables MMIO with bus mastering blocked, stops and verifies CORB,
RIRB and every input/output/bidirectional stream, disables position DMA,
and verifies entry into reset. Measured 100-us reset and 521-us discovery
delays have finite polling limits. Bus mastering is enabled only after all
inherited streams are reset and fresh zeroed command rings are installed.
CORB/RIRB then start before codec discovery; audio streams stay stopped while
their new buffers and route are prepared. Late initialization errors
stop the engines and reset the link while DMA remains disabled. This follows
the RUN/reset and codec-discovery requirements in Intel's
[HDA specification, sections 3.3.7 and 4.3](https://www.intel.com.br/content/dam/www/public/us/en/documents/product-specifications/high-definition-audio-specification.pdf).

The irreversible kexec commit also stops HDA and holds the codec link in
reset after PCI DMA and other CPUs have stopped, before overwriting the
old kernel's memory. Failure to confirm shutdown aborts the handoff through
the existing reboot-required path. The receive-side startup fix still
handles a predecessor that does not implement this shutdown.

GitNexus reports LOW/0 indexed upstream dependencies for hda_init, LOW/1
for kexec's commit, LOW to MEDIUM/8-17 for the MMIO accessors, and UNKNOWN
for new helpers/tests. Actual startup is also called by the HDA driver
service, which the indexed upstream result misses. The host test substitutes
only MMIO/PCI, time, allocation and logging at the production driver's boundary.
Its original-startup baseline fails 75 of 133 assertions. The second startup
and handoff test passes 155 assertions under both GCC and Clang, each normally
and with ASan/UBSan. Cases include inherited running streams, bidirectional
channels, stuck RUN/reset bits, a stopped clock, allocation failures, missing
codec/route and rejected PCI command writes.

The initial receive-side candidate completes an old-kernel-to-new-kernel
hotreload followed by another active-audio hotreload in QEMU. Both return
with all stream RUN bits clear, HDA ready and SSH responsive. WaveOut and
PE32/PE64 alert regressions pass afterward; audio is captured to a WAV file

streams are stopped; this is not a physical speaker measurement. Evidence:
hda-startup-research, hda-startup-baseline-r2, hda-startup-fixed-r1/r2 and
hda-startup-qemu-r1. Subsequent P1 deployment is recorded below.

### 4.308. Win32 platform metadata for the original DirectX installer

The clean-install blocker in 4.297/4.303 was missing platform metadata.
Registry initialization now supplies HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\DirectX\\Version
for both WOW64 views, identifying the legacy DirectX compatibility profile
4.09.00.0904. This describes the OS-provided API namespace used by setup;
it does not register any optional runtime DLL as installed or add a rendering
backend. Existing values, including empty values, differently typed overrides
and shared-view values, are preserved. Missing metadata is added after the
persistent hive loads and uses the ordinary dirty/flush mechanism.

Microsoft's [web installer description](https://www.microsoft.com/en-US/download/details.aspx?id=35)
distinguishes the OS core from the optional SDK libraries it installs. The
[Wine platform initialization](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/master/loader/wine.inf.in)
also publishes this compatibility-version value. Osito's own implementation
initializes only its platform value and parent keys. The previously simulated
QEMU prerequisite is no longer supplied by a test EXE in these runs. All
Microsoft executables, CABs and DLLs remain external installation inputs.
Direct3DCreate9 still reports no rendering backend; successful installation
does not imply that Braid can create a device.

### 4.309. Registry string payload encoding and persistence

RegSetValueExW stored UTF16 bytes without identifying their encoding, while
RegQueryValueExW delegated to the ANSI API without converting data. A value
written through A was therefore returned unchanged through W, and vice versa.
New string values now retain whether they came from A or W. Queries and
enumeration convert REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ and REG_MULTI_SZ payloads for the
requested API, preserve explicit byte lengths/embedded terminators, and leave
binary/DWORD payloads unchanged. Short-buffer sizes use the requested
encoding. RegQueryInfoKey reports a bound that covers the Unicode data size.
The conversion helper preserves LastError.

The encoding uses one previously reserved byte of the existing version-1
value record; record sizes and raw stored data remain unchanged. Untagged old
values retain the former opaque-byte behavior, since their original encoding
cannot be reliably reconstructed. A subsequent A/W write tags the value.
Older kernels can still read the record layout but ignore the new tag. This
change reuses the existing code-page converters; their broader non-ASCII
mapping limitations and conversion of wide key/value names are not resolved.
UTF16-to-UTF16 data, including surrogate pairs, is preserved exactly.

The native probe passes 158 checks per ABI using private HKCU keys. It covers
both write/read directions, expansion/multiple strings, Latin-1 text, empty
data, binary data, short buffers, enumeration, LastError and Unicode-only
round trips. The initial native probe incorrectly required a reduced maximum
size after overwriting a longer value; Windows retains a high-water bound.
The corrected probe checks that bound and preserves the first result. The
metadata-only kernel fails 40 of these checks per ABI. Kernel
kernel-directx-platform-r2.elf passes all 316 string checks, all 72 platform
checks and the existing root/WOW64 selftest before the original wizard runs.

### 4.311. Polygon drawing and real thin-pen state

GDI32 now exports Polygon/PolyPolygon and renders their fill and solid thin
outline. LineTo and Polyline use the same clipped rasterizer. Logical pens
have process ownership, LOGPEN queries, selection and references held by live
and saved DCs. SaveDC/RestoreDC also retain the polygon fill mode, ROP2 and
DC_PEN color. DC destruction and process cleanup release their references.
This replaces the previous fixed CreatePen handle and successful line stubs.

The implementation supports ALTERNATE/WINDING fills, null/solid/DC pens,
solid and existing pattern brushes, clipping, mapping transforms and the
16 binary raster operations. Rasterization clips the major-axis iteration
before walking a line, keeping work bounded by the destination. Native
comparison exposed two initial mistakes: half-way line coordinates must
prefer the smaller device coordinate regardless of direction, and a fill
must precede every outline visit at overlapping pixels. Pen visit parity
retains repeated XOR/NOT effects. The shared point conversion also needed
floor(value + 0.5), including negative half-way coordinates; -4.5 maps to -4.

The same PE32 and PE64 fixture passes 158 checks on Windows and Osito-K,
with all 144 off-screen scenes matching their native RGB row hashes. Cases
cover concave, crossed, degenerate and overlapping contours, both fill
modes, all ROP2 modes, translated/reflected/scaled clipping, negative
fractional coordinates, all eight line directions, LineTo/Polyline position
rules and shared/saved pen lifetime. Invalid argument results are also
compared. The existing surface-lifetime host suite, extended with selected
pen deletion guards, nested saved states, multi-DC references and process
cleanup, passes 1,813 checks under GCC and Clang, with and without ASan/UBSan.
Its missing host adapters for thread ID, path resolution and readable ranges
were supplied in the fixture only.

### 4.312. Extended pens and the next Braid launcher import

GDI32 now exports ExtCreatePen with its five-argument PE32 thunk contract.
FLTK's actual line_style implementation calls it even for a default line:
PS_GEOMETRIC | PS_ENDCAP_FLAT, width zero and a solid LOGBRUSH. These calls
now create owned objects, retain selection/saved-DC references, draw pixels
and release their resources. They no longer stop the launcher at an absent
import. No Microsoft DLL or application binary was embedded in the kernel.

The pen stores its logical style, width, brush, hatch and up to 16 custom
style entries. Pattern pens copy the source bitmap, which may subsequently
be deleted. Validation and GetObjectA/W use the caller's PE32/PE64 structure
layout; GetObjectType reports OBJ_EXTPEN and GetCurrentObject accepts the
pen/extpen aliases. Native probes distinguish NULL_PEN's special exact-size
EXTLOGPEN query from ordinary LOGPEN queries, and stock drawing pens report
zero logical width. CreatePen retains its requested style in queries but
renders wide dashed/dotted legacy pens as solid, matching Windows.

Drawing now covers cosmetic dashes, alternate/custom patterns, geometric
strokes, caps and joins, solid/hatched/bitmap pen brushes and ROP2. Geometric
pieces are unioned before applying the raster operation. Opaque legacy
dash backgrounds precede the foreground, including crossings between
segments. Extended pen gaps remain transparent independently of BkMode.
The native comparison corrected hatch origins, a missing miter wedge and
the diamond support vector of a one-pixel geometric nib. Widened vertices
are quantized to 28.4 device coordinates. Destination clipping and a bounded
fragment budget prevent iteration over arbitrarily long off-screen dashes.

This is not complete raster equivalence. Of 328 native drawing scenes,
259 match exactly; 69 wide-stroke scenes differ by 211 pixels in total,
at most nine pixels in one 16-by-16 image. The remaining differences involve
wide normals, caps/joins and dashed boundaries. They are preserved as failed
image comparisons, not accepted as exact matches. DIB-pattern brush styles
are not implemented, hatch indices above five fail drawing explicitly, and
the wider transform/style combinations are not all covered by this fixture.
The 96 native WidenPath/GetPath outlines reproduce all 96 corresponding
solid reference images and are retained for further geometry work.

### 4.313. Arc/Pie paths and Braid launcher progress

GDI32 now exports Arc and Pie with nine-argument PE32 thunk metadata, plus
GetArcDirection and SetArcDirection. Direction belongs to the DC and survives
SaveDC/RestoreDC. Drawing preserves the current position; Arc draws only the
pen, while Pie closes the sector through its center and applies the brush.
Native invalid-handle probes corrected the distinction between the direction
queries, which preserve last error for NULL, and the drawing calls, which
set ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE. Invalid direction preserves last error on PE32 and
sets ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER on PE64, matching the native reference.

Curves are split into cubic pieces of at most a quadrant, transformed into
28.4 device coordinates and flattened with a second-derivative chord-error
bound. A midpoint-only bound missed curvature on elongated ellipses. The
new bound reproduces all 96 native FlattenPath paths when supplied the
captured native cubic controls; production control construction still differs
in some rounding details. GM_COMPAT excludes the bottom/right device pixel;
GM_ADVANCED transforms logical geometry. The fill and fractional pen paths
reuse the existing clipping, ROP2 and brush/pen composition. Wide strokes
reuse the geometric pen engine through a double-coordinate entry point.

Off-screen control hulls are skipped, major-axis raster walks are clipped,
and path subdivision/allocation have explicit limits. Draw scopes retain
window surfaces through replacement/destruction. The surface lifetime suite
now includes Arc and brush-only Pie and passes 2,044 checks in each GCC/Clang
normal and ASan/UBSan configuration; all 109 tracked surfaces are released.

### 4.314. Filesystem common dialogs and shell allocator ABI

COMDLG32 now implements ANSI/Unicode Open and Save dialogs over the shared
USER32 controls. The picker enumerates directories, applies file filters,
accepts a file name/default extension, exposes the selected path and title,
and distinguishes cancellation from initialization or buffer errors.
Explorer hooks receive their original OPENFILENAME and CDN_INITDONE/FILEOK
notifications, including application veto. The parser handles the 76/88-byte
PE32 and 136/152-byte PE64 descriptors without native-pointer stores into
32-bit fields. CommDlgExtendedError is stored per process/thread and cleared
when the owning process is released.

SHELL32 adds SHBrowseForFolderA/W, SHGetPathFromIDListA and SHGetMalloc. Folder
callbacks can select a filesystem path; the returned owned PIDL interoperates
with both path accessors and CoTaskMemFree. CoGetMalloc now exposes a guest
32-bit object/vtable with stdcall thunks and ABI-sized output pointers. Its
QueryInterface accepts IUnknown and IMalloc, rejects other interfaces, and
preserves adjacent memory. DidAlloc returns the documented indeterminate
answer because the existing shared CRT/task heap does not tag allocation
origin. Proxy mappings are owned by the process address space and the cache
is invalidated during process cleanup.

The first guest run caught a native dialog procedure incorrectly dispatched
as PE32 code. Native procedures now have explicit guest thunks. Control
messages carrying kernel-stack text also use temporary guest-heap buffers;
internal text never relies on truncating a high pointer at the callback
boundary. The corrected kernel-filedialog-r2.elf passes 110 fixture checks
in each ABI, as does the native Windows reference filedialog-probe-r6. These
cover old/Explorer cancellation, accepted Open/Save, default extension and
filename offsets, short output buffers, hook veto, truncated titles, ANSI/
Unicode folder selection and IMalloc query/allocation/reallocation/free.

This is not complete common-dialog equivalence. Custom templates/custom
filters and legacy multiselect return initialization errors; virtual shell
namespaces are unsupported. Existing wide filesystem helpers still limit
Unicode path handling. The native Windows fixture returns TRUE with
FNERR_BUFFERTOOSMALL when a hook is installed; Osito follows the documented
FALSE/error/required-size contract. Raw records preserve that difference.
Interactive multi-selection and every optional OFN/BIF flag are not qualified
by the current fixture. No successful game rendering is inferred from these
API tests.

### 4.316. Cache thread-context misses and accept the PE32 current-thread handle

The real Braid launcher exposed another cost in the Win32 dispatch path.
The existing scheduler-slot cache remembered worker-thread hits, but primary
Win32 threads and native services have no worker-table entry. Every miss
scanned all 224 allocated contexts in this QEMU configuration. In the first
BSP profile, buckets in find_ctx_by_pid accounted for approximately 37% of
samples. This is a sampled BSP hot spot, not all-CPU utilization or a frame-time
measurement. The quieter baseline also puts the scan at the top of its profile.

The cache now stores the native PID alongside the context, including NULL
results. A scheduler-slot reuse invalidates the entry by PID. Positive hits
still validate the context's active state and native PID; arbitrary-PID
lookups retain the full scan. A miss for the current task is stable because
CreateThread binds its context to a newly allocated native PID before making
that task runnable. Primary threads and kernel services never acquire a
worker-table entry under their current PID. Allocation failure still falls
back to scanning. No scheduling, wait, or cancellation semantics are changed.

The new thread_lookup_pe.c fixture independently caught a pre-existing x86
identity error: GetThreadId(0xfffffffe) returned zero/ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE,
while GetCurrentThreadId, GetCurrentProcessId and TLS returned the expected
values. The PE32 thunk zero-extends the pseudo-handle. GetThreadId_k32 now
recognizes that representation only in compat32 mode; PE64 retains the full
native pseudo-handle comparison. The original kernel and cache-only r1 both
produce 78 cascading x86 failures in the fixture; the original x64 run passes.

Native Windows and the final kernel each pass 245 checks per ABI: primary
and worker identity, current-thread pseudo-handles, last-error preservation,
TLS isolation across yields, suspended creation/resume, return codes, and
three child-process lifetimes. Each ABI creates 36 worker threads across
the parent and children. The same binaries run on Windows and in QEMU;
their hashes and native results are in thread-lookup-probe-r2. Existing
cancel-stack and repeat-terminate fixtures pass three and four rounds,
respectively, for both ABIs. No CPU exception occurs.

The initial regression driver stops at a native-shell process selftest
after the final PE has exited. Separate fresh-boot and after-PE controls on
both kernels reproduce exactly the same 14 selftest outcomes: 12 pass and
two fail. The process identity test passes fresh, then fails to create process
objects after PE teardown, where the primary token has been released. IOCP
has an existing fresh-state "closed port rejected" failure and passes after
the PE initialization path. TLS, module, registered-wait, input and COM
selftests pass in both orders, and the message-wait PE32 fixture passes.
These two order-dependent findings remain open and are not counted as
successful checks or blamed on the cache change. Raw controls are retained
in thread-lookup-selftests-baseline-r1 and thread-lookup-selftests-r2.

Four main-thread samples per ABI measure 20,000 pairs of process/thread-ID
queries using guest QueryPerformanceCounter:

| ABI | Original median | Corrected median |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PE32 | 15.240 ms | 7.974 ms |
| PE64 | 3.219 ms | 0.980 ms |

These are component timings from two QEMU boots, not Steam FPS or physical
P1 performance. The original x86 worker timing is absent because its
pseudo-handle check fails before that loop. Raw worker timings are retained
as well; no worker speedup is claimed.

and UNKNOWN for the new fixture helpers. The frozen r2 build has 907 inputs,
including all 14 GUI files. Only kernel32_shim.c differs from section 4.315.

The source snapshot is build/thread-lookup-20261006-r2. The combined
machine-readable audit is thread-lookup-progress-review.json.

### 4.317 Shell return preserves a surviving child GUI (2026-10-06)

The Braid launcher exposed a race after the lookup optimization in 4.316.
The original Braid.exe starts launcher.exe and exits. The child can finish
creating its window before the shell handles the parent's return. The shell
then called user32_shim_init and ddraw_shim_init, resetting every process's
GUI state. The already submitted compositor surface remained visible, but
window_count, active_hwnd and user32_foreground_active became zero; keyboard
and mouse input could no longer reach the launcher.

A QEMU hardware watchpoint captured the destructive write at
user32_shim_init+445, called by shell_reset_win32_state from shell_dispatch.
The trace and zero-window snapshot are in braid-window-watch-r2. A prior
run with three watchpoints happened to launch successfully: debugger timing
masked the race, so that isolated pass was not accepted as validation.

shell_reset_win32_state now resets only the current shell task's compat32
mode and invokes user32_release_process(1) and ddraw_release_process(1).
Those owner-specific releases are also safe after normal main-process
cleanup and retain the fallback for non-local shell recovery. Children keep
their windows, classes, queues, timers and DirectDraw state. This change
does not alter the global initialization performed when starting a new root
Win32 execution.

The new orphan_ui_pe.c fixture creates a child window and timer before
allowing the parent to exit. Identical PE32/PE64 binaries pass all 18 checks
on Windows. On the old kernel, each ABI has 8 passes and 10 failures. On the
corrected kernel, each has 17 passes and one remaining failure: the child's
wait on its exited root parent times out. The legacy root NT process object
spans shell executions and is not signaled on this return. That separate
lifetime defect is still open; the full fixture is deliberately recorded as
failed, not relabeled a pass. All nine checks for the child's surviving
window/class, text, callbacks, posted messages, timer and cleanup now pass
for both ABIs. The existing thread-lookup fixture again passes 245 checks
per ABI.

Two fresh QEMU boots without GDB validate the actual launcher: one uses
Enter and the other clicks Launch. Both retain a live, active USER32 window,
start braid.exe -no_launcher, load the original installed DirectX runtime,
reach the explicit SteamAPI_Init failure / Steam-is-required message, and
retain SSH with zero CPU exceptions. Evidence is in
braid-orphan-ui-enter-r1 and braid-orphan-ui-mouse-r1. QEMU has no Steam
session, so these runs do not qualify gameplay or physical P1 performance.

The first post-fixture desktop input selftest reports two failures involving

### 4.319 Preserve synchronization objects across shell launches (2026-10-06)

The root-parent lifetime probe exposed a second, independent defect. A child
could create named events and wait for the next shell-launched PE, but the
second PE could no longer open those events. nt_sync_register_syscalls reset
all event, mutant and semaphore allocations, the waiter count, and every
active wait whenever nt_syscall_init registered another SSDT. Handles and
child scheduler tasks survived that reset; their synchronization state did
not.

Registration now preserves system-lifetime object pools, pending waits and
diagnostic identities. Static storage supplies their initial zero state.
The waiter allocation remains lazy, protected by the existing synchronization
lock, and each supplied SSDT still receives its handlers.

The dedicated cross-launch probe also found missing OpenMutexA/W and
OpenSemaphoreA/W exports, and CreateSemaphoreA/W discarded the supplied name.
The new opens retain existing objects and honor the handle inheritance flag.
Semaphore creation now publishes named objects through the existing object
registry and reopens an existing semaphore without changing its count or
maximum, reporting ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS. This follows the
[named-object contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/sync/object-names)
and [CreateSemaphore contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-createsemaphorea).
The existing common registry's name conversion, namespace handling and
security-descriptor limitations are not repaired by this change; the new
fixture uses matching ASCII names in A/W calls and NULL creation attributes.

sync_lifetime_pe.c keeps an observer alive after its first parent exits, then
opens its objects from a second shell-launched PE. The 35 checks cover a
pending child wait waking after reinitialization, manual-event state,
recursive mutex ownership, shared semaphore counts, A/W reopening,
ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS, missing-object opens, independent handle closure and
inheritance flags. The same PE32 and PE64 binaries pass all 35 checks on
Windows and QEMU. sync-lifetime-qualified-r2 records both completions,
working SSH and zero CPU exceptions. The initial probe on the prior kernel
stopped at missing OpenMutexA, before testing object persistence; that run is
not a successful baseline of the synchronization behavior.

The separate root_lifetime_pe.c does not use the new mutex/semaphore APIs.
Its earlier input-workarea kernel run recorded 15 passes and six failures per
ABI, with the observer stranded before completing the remaining assertions.
With synchronization preserved, all 28 assertions execute: 20 pass and eight
fail per ABI, and the second root completes successfully. All remaining
failures concern the exited root process/primary-thread handles retaining
STILL_ACTIVE and remaining unsignaled, including while the next root is alive.
This is still an unresolved lifecycle defect, not a passing root-lifetime
test. See root-lifetime-baseline-r1 and root-lifetime-sync-fixed-r2.

The regression boot passes thread lookup/identity (245 checks per ABI,

registered waits, input and COM selftests pass. The previously observed

### 4.321 Growable JIT unwind tables for Steam's renderer (2026-10-07)

The renderer trace in 4.320 immediately precedes its NULL call with failed
lookups for the growable function-table APIs. NTDLL now exports
RtlAddGrowableFunctionTable, RtlGrowFunctionTable and
RtlDeleteGrowableFunctionTable. They use the existing per-process dynamic
unwind registry and RtlLookupFunctionEntry/RtlVirtualUnwind implementation.
This implements registration and unwind data; it does not merely report
success for a missing API.

Registration supports an initially empty published prefix, a fixed capacity,
an explicit address range and an opaque registration identity. Growth
publishes the larger initialized prefix with release/acquire ordering while
keeping the existing prefix visible to other threads. Removal and process
teardown release the slot; ordinary RtlAddFunctionTable registrations keep
their separate removal contract. Concurrent growable registrations serialize
their range-conflict check and publication. Callers retain the metadata and
registration while lookup/growth is in progress, and unregister before freeing
the code. See Microsoft's [registration contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/nf-winnt-rtladdgrowablefunctiontable),
[growth contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/nf-winnt-rtlgrowfunctiontable)
and [removal contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/nf-winnt-rtldeletegrowablefunctiontable).

The native Windows oracle returns STATUS_CONFLICTING_ADDRESSES (0xc0000018)
for equal or overlapping ranges and accepts adjacent ranges. The first
cleanup fixture mistakenly registered overlapping ranges in each child;
Windows rejected its second registration. The corrected fixture uses 16
adjacent ranges per child. Its 604 checks pass on Windows and QEMU, covering
zero entries, growth to 64 entries alongside a concurrent reader, range and
function boundaries, virtual unwind of a grown function, ordinary table
interoperation, 160 slot reuses, and nine child exits releasing 144 owned
registrations. No generated code is executed by this fixture.

growable-unwind-qualified-r2 also passes the complete existing UNWIND64 test,
40 deliberate SYSCALL-return child faults and the message-wait PE32 fixture.
SSH survives all four cases. Only unwind64.c, unwind64.h and ntdll_shim.c
differ from the 4.320 production manifest. GitNexus reports LOW/9 for dynamic
lookup, LOW/2 for each ordinary registration/removal function and LOW/8 for
process cleanup; the newly added growable functions are not yet indexed.

The frozen build includes all 907 inputs and 14 GUI files in
build/growable-unwind-20261007-r2. kernel-growable-unwind-r2.elf is 8,027,552
bytes, SHA256
64ffcb206099dec1b1bf4f53e46930fc29e6d292b53c318e1ec3b36d7917d0ae.
growable-unwind-review-r2.json retains native/QEMU qualification and scope.

### 4.323 Cabinet FDI for the original VC2013 bootstrapper (2026-10-07)

The VC2013 import inventory requires cabinet.dll ordinals 20, 22 and 23:
FDICreate, FDICopy and FDIDestroy. The new cabinet_shim.c registers these
names and ordinals with explicit cdecl contracts for PE32. Native calls use
the Microsoft x64 ABI. The adapter invokes the application's allocation,
file and notification callbacks; input need not be a standalone filesystem
CAB, so bootstrapper callbacks can expose a container inside their EXE.
Stored, MSZIP and LZX decompression reuse the existing CAB reader.

Notifications use the actual 40-byte PE32 / 64-byte PE64 layout, guest
addresses for strings/data, signed pointer-sized output handles, and the
caller-supplied context. Skip, callback abort, short write, missing input,
bad checksum, truncated data, and initial enumeration stop preserve their
native result and ERF behavior. Contexts belong to the creating Win32
process. FDIDestroy frees callback allocations; process teardown releases
abandoned kernel buffers/context slots without calling dead application
callbacks. Guest allocations are then reclaimed with that process's VM.

The supported scope is a single cabinet of at most 128 MiB, using stored,
MSZIP or LZX folders. Split-cabinet continuation, Quantum, and decryption
callbacks remain unsupported. Enumeration supports a stop or a cursor to
a real remaining CFFILE suffix; arbitrary shorter enumeration windows are
not implemented. The adapter does not install extracted files itself or
claim that an MSI product is installed. See Microsoft's
[FDICreate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fdi/nf-fdi-fdicreate),
[FDICopy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fdi/nf-fdi-fdicopy)
and [notification contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fdi/nf-fdi-fnfdinotify).

cabinet_fdi_pe.c passes on native Windows in both ABIs, 1,417 checks each.
QEMU passes 1,346 checks each; allocation and write callback counts are
implementation-dependent. The 17 result/ERF rows and 26 content records
match Windows exactly on each ABI. After the PE64 run, all 24 extracted
files match the native SHA256 and size, including both original installer

### 4.324 CryptoAPI streaming hashes for VC2013 setup (2026-10-07)

ADVAPI now exports CryptCreateHash, CryptHashData, CryptGetHashParam and
CryptDestroyHash with their actual PE32/PE64 contracts. RSA_FULL contexts
support MD5/SHA-1; RSA_AES contexts additionally support SHA-256, SHA-384 and
SHA-512. The implementation uses unmodified BearSSL 0.6 primitives from the
same archive already pinned for WLAN. Seven additional upstream hash/codec
files retain their license; the vendor manifest records their SHA256. Typed
calls avoid generic vtable function-pointer casts. TLS, RNG and certificate
trust policy are unchanged.

Hashes retain independent streaming state in a bounded, process-owned table
of 256 contexts. Opaque identities are never recycled, and exhaustion fails
explicitly. The provider lock protects short identity/state transitions;
bulk hashing runs with that lock released and yields between 64 KiB chunks.
Concurrent operations on one hash serialize through its busy state. Destroy
and process cleanup clear retained state. The existing cleanup hook runs
after owned threads stop, including a process that abandons live hashes.

The native oracle confirms several relevant details: a NULL-buffer size query
and ERROR_MORE_DATA do not finalize a digest or modify its output buffer.
Only successful retrieval of HP_HASHVAL completes it. Later nonempty updates
fail with NTE_BAD_HASH_STATE, but zero-byte updates still succeed. HP_ALGID
and HP_HASHSIZE, repeat digest reads, unsupported algorithms and flags,
CRYPT_USERDATA, NULL handles, failure output preservation and successful-call
last-error preservation are covered. Keyed hashes, other CSP hash algorithms,
CryptDuplicateHash and CryptSetHashParam remain unsupported; callers must
destroy hashes before releasing their provider, as required by the API.
The provider's existing named-container/key-pair limitations remain in force.
See Microsoft's [creation contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-cryptcreatehash),
[stream update](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-crypthashdata),
[result query](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-cryptgethashparam)
and [destruction contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincrypt/nf-wincrypt-cryptdestroyhash).

empty input, split "abc" updates and a 262,397-byte stream in 1,021 updates.
Python hashlib independently verifies all 64 native digest records. Per ABI,
four real children each abandon 96 live hashes; the parent's digest survives,
and 600 further create/destroy cycles succeed. The existing installer-security
fixture also passes its 39 assertions in both ABIs. SSH survives and no CPU
exceptions appear. The installer inventory decreases from 44 to 40 missing
imports. The original VC2013 installer still lacks other imports, including
Windows Installer, and has not installed the runtime on P1.

### 4.325 MSI database access and condition groundwork (2026-10-07)

The existing native MSI installer could report success after failing to read
the first external cabinet: the VC2013 minimum package produced zero files,
18 registry writes and a committed success manifest in a host reproduction.

declared tables now fail the operation. Registry application and success
manifest commit are withheld on these failures. This is not a rollback
transaction; files written before a later failure are not yet restored.

The database reader exposes read-only typed table views, column metadata,
codepage and binary field streams. NULL differs from integer zero, empty
declared tables open successfully, and present empty binary streams remain
valid. Binary stream names use the table's primary keys, including multiple
keys and signed integers. Pool/schema bounds, duplicate or missing columns,
invalid row widths and string references are checked. Binary markers remain
two bytes when ordinary string references grow to three bytes.

The OLE reader now checks the CFB header's version, sector sizes and byte
order before shifting; validates physical sector bounds and complete FAT
loading; bounds DIFAT/FAT/mini-FAT walks; rejects short stream chains; and
validates directory name lengths. The previous parser triggered UBSan on a
mutated mini-sector shift of 518. The corrected reader survives truncated
prefixes, 1,600 mutations and allocation failures under ASan/UBSan, with

[CFB header](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-cfb/05060311-bfce-4b12-874d-71fd4ce63aea)
and [size rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-cfb/d4c8084a-e583-473f-b2f4-4af13b3101d9).

and additional packages, including their 70,144-byte WiX dependency action
streams (data only, never executed). Two databases created by Windows add
66,048 matching cells: empty tables, nullable and negative integers,
70,000-character text, zero/one/4,095/4,096-byte binary streams, composite
keys, and 66,000 distinct short strings requiring three-byte references.
System tables such as _Tables are deliberately not synthesized by this API.

The new, allocation-free condition evaluator preserves MSI distinctions
between quoted literals, numeric operands and property values, implements
operator precedence and access-prefix callbacks, and bounds nesting. It
matches 32,021 native results and survives 20,000 malformed expressions with

[restricted, machine-independent handle](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/msi/nf-msi-msiopenpackageexw)
and executes no installer actions. The host test supplies native Windows NLS

the kernel's existing partial linguistic collation. Case-insensitive ordering
delegates to CompareStringW; other comparisons use CompareStringOrdinal.
See [MSI condition syntax](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/msi/conditional-statement-syntax).

### 4.331. MSI installation API and cooperative cancellation (2026-10-07)

MsiInstallProductW now invokes the real fresh-install engine from PE32/PE64,
including the bootstrapper's ordinal 88. It validates and copies guest strings,
uses the caller's effective token, and serializes installation ownership. A
protected installing thread observes cancellation without unwinding its host
stack before the transaction has rolled back and released its buffers. The
apply backend polls before forward operations and after flush, but never aborts
rollback. TerminateThread queues cancellation for an MSI owner; other threads
retain their existing path. Cancelled Win32 workers exit as detached scheduler
tasks, allowing the reaper to signal their NT thread object after they stop,
without waiting for their live parent to perform a POSIX wait4.

The first QEMU run exposed that missing detach: rollback completed, but the
parent's thread wait timed out. The corrected kernel passes both ABIs. Each
guest cancels an installing worker (19 checks), cancels an installing child
process (21), verifies absent product/DLL state, and immediately installs the
same original MSI successfully. Non-administrative installation returns 5 and
changes nothing. The test retries 1618 in its child because the parent's busy
probe can briefly acquire the installation scope first. These guest
cancellations occur during preparation; they do not claim a physical mid-write
cancellation. The ASan/UBSan apply tests separately cover all 95/131 cancellation
checkpoints, including after flush, and 210/282 injected I/O failures, with
25,229/38,730 checks and no retained allocations. Preparation passes another
551,023/570,799 checks with 800 allocation-failure positions per package.

The two fresh QEMU disks install the unmodified VC2013 Minimum and Additional
packages through the exported API. Product queries pass 1,191 absent and 3,413
installed checks per ABI; record/lifetime probes pass 5,365 each. Three rounds
per ABI verify cancelled peer stacks remain pinned until process teardown.

branches CLSID, DirectShow, Interface, Media Type and MediaFoundation retain
separate views. This follows the [Windows 7+ registry rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winprog64/shared-registry-keys).

Loading a v1 hive normalizes legacy copies of newly shared values in memory,
without immediately rewriting the file. Existing shared values take priority;
if old ABI-specific copies conflict, 64-bit precedes 32-bit consistently,
because this format stores no modification timestamps. Subsequent writes,
enumeration and deletion operate on the single normalized value. The P1's
original hive and previous kernel are retained as update evidence/backups.

### 4.336. Steam client path and Unicode imports (2026-10-07)

The r17 physical trace identified two missing PE32 imports before Braid could
finish loading the Steam client: tier0_s.dll needs GetShortPathNameW and
vstdlib_s.dll needs FoldStringW. Kernel32 now exports these with three and
five stdcall stack arguments, respectively. The implementation is separate
from the large kernel32 shim. GitNexus reports LOW impact (three upstream
functions) for the resolver; newly added symbols are not yet in its index.
Static inspection bounds the new modules to these exports and their tests.

GetShortPathNameW checks that the path exists and returns its spelling because
OsitoFS has no DOS aliases. It supports in-place output, reports a size including
the terminator when querying or short, preserves last-error on success, and
validates guest pointers. A null destination is a size query even with nonzero
capacity. This behavior is permitted for filesystems without short names by the
[Win32 API contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getshortpathnamew).

FoldStringW implements canonical/compatibility decomposition, stable combining
order, composition including Hangul, digit folding and ligature expansion.
The tables derive from Unicode facts filtered against native Windows build
26200, with native digit/ligature mappings. Combining runs use stable counting
sort; scratch storage is per call and allocation failure leaves no allocation
behind. Explicit lengths preserve embedded NULs; negative lengths include the
terminator. Invalid flags, aliases, UTF-16 and guest ranges fail explicitly.
Digit-only size queries preserve the native maximum; with normalization, the
digit pass precedes normalization and can reduce the required UTF-16 length.
Failed conversions leave the destination unchanged; their in-capacity partial
contents are not treated as a portable API result. Tests compare all successful
output and always check out-of-capacity canaries. See the
[FoldStringW contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/stringapiset/nf-stringapiset-foldstringw).

The 4,146 folding and 126 path cases pass 281,122 checks per ABI in native
Windows and in QEMU. GCC and Clang ASan/UBSan each pass 294,692 host checks,
including forced allocation failures, long combining runs and four concurrent
callers. The independent Unicode 11.0 normalization corpus passes 375,840
checks over 18,792 rows. Trying the Unicode 12.0 corpus first exposed characters
outside the native Windows normalization profile; those differences were also
reproduced against Windows, rather than changing this profile to newer Unicode.
The generated tables carry the Unicode data license.

### 4.337. Binary classification and Unicode file paths (2026-10-07)

Kernel32 now exports GetBinaryTypeW with two stdcall arguments. The separate
binary_type module reads executable headers without loading code or resolving
imports. It classifies DOS, PIF, Windows NE, x86/x64 PE and POSIX images, rejects
DLLs and invalid PE layouts, keeps the output unchanged on failure, closes its
handle on all paths, and preserves last-error on success. Native Windows also
checks the last section's raw end against file size; under WOW64 a PE64 POSIX
image reports SCS_64BIT_BINARY rather than SCS_POSIX_BINARY. Both distinctions
are captured in the reference cases. See the
[GetBinaryTypeW contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-getbinarytypew).

Clang ASan/UBSan each pass 5,184 host checks, including partial reads, injected

and closes. One synthetic PE sample rejected by host security was excluded;
it was not retried or used as an OS API reference. Research and fixture hashes
are under binary-type-native-r1/r2 and binary-type-probe-r1/r2.

GetFileAttributesW truncated UTF-16 code units to bytes. Names such as
unicode-á-日.exe could not be found. These two entrypoints now encode valid

still carries the resulting bytes in widened units. This is a correction to
these entrypoints, not a conversion of every W/NT file API. Empty/null paths
return ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND as observed natively. The encoded path limit
remains 259 bytes; overflow returns 206 rather than opening a truncated name,
and malformed UTF-16 returns 1113. Long paths and unpaired-surrogate filenames
remain unsupported, beyond the general
[CreateFileW contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-createfilew).

### 4.339. Thread-directed synchronous I/O cancellation (2026-10-07)

`CancelSynchronousIo` now has a PE32/PE32+ thunk and targets the referenced NT
thread object, including duplicated and `OpenThread` handles. It requires
`THREAD_TERMINATE`, rejects non-thread handles, returns error 1168 when there
is no pending request, and preserves last-error on success. The request state
lives in the kernel thread object rather than a process-private stack. The
issuer clears it on completion; primary-process entry/exit clears abandoned
state, and ordinary thread reaping already resets the whole object.

Synchronous pipe reads, pipe writes waiting for buffer space, and blocking
byte-range lock requests register their current operation and observe the
cancellation mark between wait iterations. Cancellation completes with
`STATUS_CANCELLED` / error 995. A failed `ReadFile` or `WriteFile` now leaves
its byte-count output at zero. The cancellation call does not wait for the
issuer to finish, touch another reader, cancel an overlapped request, or arm
the next operation. Normal completion may win the race, as allowed by the
[Windows contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/ioapiset/nf-ioapiset-cancelsynchronousio).
This adds cancellation to those three backends; disk, socket and console I/O
cancellation are not implemented by this change.

The native `sync_io_pe.c` probe passes 258 checks per ABI on Windows and the
same 258 per ABI in QEMU. It exercises two readers on the same pipe, access
restrictions, duplicate and terminate-only handles, idle/terminated threads,
subsequent I/O on the cancelled thread, blocked writes, conflicting file
locks and isolation from an overlapped named-pipe request. The file-lock host
test additionally exercises cancellation cleanup, ownership and re-entry:
GCC and Clang, each with and without ASan/UBSan, pass 18,586 checks per run.

GitNexus reports LOW upstream impact: four symbols each for `nt_pipe_read`
and `nt_pipe_write`, six for `nt_file_lock_range_request`, 11/12 for
`ReadFile`/`WriteFile`, three for the Kernel32 resolver, and 22 each for the
primary-process accounting entry/exit hooks. Those last changes only reset
the new state. New helpers are not indexed; their local consumers are the
three synchronous backends and the export. No GUI code is changed.

with the [documented return contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-setsystempowerstate).
The power probe calls it only inside the guest and checks 32 cases per ABI;

### 4.340. Automation scalar conversion and guest VARIANT layout (2026-10-07)

The next original Steam client import, `OLEAUT32.dll!#12`, now resolves to
`VariantChangeType` with four arguments on PE32 and PE32+. The original
client's call at 0x38c5eb18 requests VT_BSTR with flags zero. Conversion is
implemented in `win32/variant.c`: integer widths, real values, currency,
96-bit DECIMAL, Boolean, en-US strings/dates, borrowed BYREF values and COM
default-value invocation. Numeric rounding uses ties-to-even without changing
the caller's rounding mode. IDispatch/IUnknown conversions use guest-width
vtable calls; PE32 callback argument/result storage is allocated in guest
address space. VARIANT_NOVALUEPROP prevents default-property invocation.

Conversion stages the result before releasing the destination, so in-place
conversions and failures preserve ownership. `VariantInit`, `VariantClear`
and `VariantCopy` now respect the 16-byte PE32 / 24-byte PE32+ layout.
Clear changes the type while preserving the now-unowned payload. Copy keeps
embedded NULs and odd BSTR byte lengths, allocates an empty BSTR for a NULL
source BSTR, and calls AddRef/Release through the correct ABI. Invalid type
tags fail before modifying the destination. Non-NULL SAFEARRAY and RECORD
ownership remain unsupported and return E_NOTIMPL; this change does not add
a SAFEARRAY or IRecordInfo backend. Locale support follows the OS's en-US
locale, not arbitrary LCIDs or localized month/Boolean dictionaries.
The relevant contracts are [VariantChangeType](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/oleauto/nf-oleauto-variantchangetype)
and [VARIANT](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/oaidl/ns-oaidl-variant).

VariantChangeTypeEx with explicit LCID 0x409. Native PE32 and PE32+ runs pass
28,420 and 28,428 checks respectively, including buffer guards, in-place
conversion, BSTR lifetime, BYREF handling and COM callbacks. Comparisons
exclude reserved bytes, which native x86 leaves unspecified. Native x86
also uses the legacy nonfinite string spelling, removes negative zero when
formatting, and rejects NaN-to-CY; x64 differs on those cases. Those ABI
differences are covered explicitly. Windows last-error is not part of this
HRESULT API's contract; the Osito wrapper additionally preserves it. The
implicit-year date fixture was generated in 2026 and must be regenerated
when the test year's clock changes.

### 4.341. IPv4 best-interface lookup (2026-10-07)

`GetBestInterface` now resolves with two arguments on PE32 and PE32+. The new
`win32/iproute.c` uses the kernel's current IPv4 address, netmask and gateway.
It returns loopback index 2 for 127/8 and configured-link index 1 for local,
broadcast or default-gateway routes, matching the existing IP Helper tables.
Without a configured address/default route, off-link destinations fail with
ERROR_HOST_UNREACHABLE. No multicast route is advertised by this backend;
reserved 0/8 and class-E destinations fail with ERROR_NETWORK_UNREACHABLE,
except the default-query address zero and limited broadcast. This reflects
the kernel's one-link IPv4 routing model, not a general Windows route table.

The [GetBestInterface contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/iphlpapi/nf-iphlpapi-getbestinterface)
defines the returned index and IPv4 address format. A NULL output returns
87. Native tests on both Windows ABIs return 998 for a non-NULL unwritable
output, including a DWORD spanning a writable and read-only page; the shim
matches that observed behavior and validates the full range before writing.
On failure it preserves the output. The public documentation instead lists
87 for unwritable memory, so this distinction is based on the native probe.

The host test covers disconnected/default/on-link routing, a non-/24 mask,
loopback addresses, network byte order and invalid output ranges. GCC and
Clang each pass 1,742 checks normally and with ASan/UBSan. Native PE probes
compare route selection with GetBestInterfaceEx and learn interface indices
from GetIpAddrTable; each passes 856 checks on this host. In QEMU, both ABIs
pass 850 checks (two IPv4 address rows rather than the host's four), including
the cross-page failure without a CPU exception. The full r28 run passes
870,049 PE checks plus 169 input checks (870,218), with SSH available and
zero CPU exceptions.

### 4.342. Interface identities and MIB_IF_ROW2 (2026-10-07)

`GetIfEntry2` and `ConvertInterfaceGuidToLuid` now have PE32/PE64 thunk
contracts (one and two arguments). The pointer-free MIB_IF_ROW2 is 1,352
bytes, aligned to eight, on both Windows ABIs. SDK-compiled native probes
verify field offsets independently of the shim header. LUID takes precedence
over index, including rejection of nonzero reserved bits. Invalid identifiers
leave the row untouched; an unknown GUID clears the LUID output, whereas a
NULL GUID preserves it. Guest buffers are range-checked before mutation;
inaccessible non-NULL buffers return 998 without a CPU fault. That defensive
behavior is tested in the guest, not claimed as a native invalid-pointer rule.

The [GetIfEntry2 contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/netioapi/nf-netioapi-getifentry2)
and [MIB_IF_ROW2 fields](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/netioapi/ns-netioapi-mib_if_row2)
are represented by the active NIC at index 1 and TCP loopback at index 2.
GUIDs are UUIDv5 values derived from the active NIC MAC and interface kind;
LUIDs encode the same index/type. GetAdaptersAddresses now exposes that LUID
and a parseable GUID adapter name. GetAdaptersInfo and GetIfTable share this
identity and real driver description. Existing DNS/unicast/prefix layout and
flags remain covered by the DNS regression probe. Native Windows can report
different IP and link MTUs for tunnel/loopback interfaces; the test does not
incorrectly demand equality between those two native views.

An occupied WLAN probe lock is an unknown link observation, not a link-down
event or a new interface. Identity uses net.c's retained MAC because the raw
WLAN get_mac callback may return zeros while busy. A negative control against
the first local candidate fails both ABI-mode identity tests; the corrected
implementation passes. GCC and Clang each pass 486 checks normally and with
ASan/UBSan. Tests include UUIDv5 values generated independently with Python,
LUID precedence, output guards/overlap, absent/down/busy links, WLAN type,
concurrent frame accounting, and byte counts beyond 32 bits. The same PE
executable passes 2,202 checks on native Windows x86 and x64.

Successful nic_send/nic_recv frames increment atomic 64-bit unicast,
multicast and broadcast counters. TCP software loopback accounts IP bytes in
both directions before delivery. Empty RX and failed TX do not count as
successful packets. Hardware errors/discards, negotiated speed and network
profile GUID are unavailable and remain zero; no synthetic speed is reported.
The six TCP/link/waiter host suites pass with both compilers and sanitizers.
GitNexus reports MEDIUM impact (54 upstream references, five direct) for
tcp_send_segment_at and LOW for the existing IP Helper functions and NIC
wrappers. Its older index does not include the new helpers or reliably track
inline callers; direct source review and network regressions supplement it.

### 4.343. PE certificate-table operations (2026-10-07)

`imagehlp.dll` now exports ImageAddCertificate, ImageEnumerateCertificates and
ImageRemoveCertificate with PE32 stack contracts of three, five and two
arguments. The new `win32/imagehlp_shim.c` checks process-owned disk handles,
access rights, guest buffers and file bounds. It handles both PE optional
header formats, eight-byte certificate alignment, ordinal/filter enumeration,
insertion/removal, file length, cursor behavior and PE checksum updates. File
contents are streamed through bounded buffers; an existing overlay preceding
the certificate table is preserved. Certificate payloads remain opaque; these
APIs do not replace signature or trust validation.

The [ImageAddCertificate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/imagehlp/nf-imagehlp-imageaddcertificate),
[ImageEnumerateCertificates](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/imagehlp/nf-imagehlp-imageenumeratecertificates)
and [ImageRemoveCertificate](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/imagehlp/nf-imagehlp-imageremovecertificate)
contracts are supplemented by native tests on disposable, owned files. The
same PE probes pass 6,821 checks on Windows x86 and x64 and on each guest ABI.
They check byte preservation, exact length/checksum, output guards, cursor
position, read-only access, missing indices and enumeration capacities.
Fourteen native operation sequences are replayed against the production shim:
GCC and Clang each pass 7,358 checks normally and with ASan/UBSan. Malformed
headers and injected I/O failures pass 6,330 additional checks per sanitized
compiler, including both compatibility modes.

This is bounded certificate-table support, not complete parity for malformed
PE files. Native Windows accepts some inconsistent directory/record sizes;
the shim keeps physical file bounds. The native PE32 old-linker-version
rejection is not yet reproduced. I/O failure can leave a partially modified
file, so these operations do not promise transactional rollback. Callers must
serialize ImageHlp use, as required by its public contract.

### 4.344. SSPI provider absence and original Steam client load (2026-10-07)

`secur32.dll` now has typed entry points for AcquireCredentialsHandleA,
InitializeSecurityContextA, CompleteAuthToken, DeleteSecurityContext and
FreeCredentialsHandle. Their PE32 argument counts are 9, 12, 2, 1 and 1.
Osito has no installed SSPI provider: acquisition reports
SEC_E_SECPKG_NOT_FOUND and leaves credential/expiry outputs untouched.
Initialization, token completion and credential release reject invalid
handles without creating a security session or token. This is support for
capability/error handling; NTLM, Kerberos, Negotiate and Schannel authentication
remain unavailable. Existing TLS/cryptographic implementations are unchanged.

These outcomes follow the [acquisition contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthn/acquirecredentialshandle--general)
and [context initialization contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secauthn/initializesecuritycontext--general).
Native probes additionally establish output preservation and LastError
behavior for invalid handles. After native package discovery, DeleteSecurityContext
treats dwLower tags 0 and 1 as empty/already deleted, regardless of dwUpper.
A fresh native process accepts tag 0 but rejects tag 1 before discovery; the
shim models the initialized case. It reads only the guest-sized lower word
through a validated range and does not alter either word. Acquisition's
LastError side effects are not part of this test contract; its SECURITY_STATUS
is authoritative.

The loader now carries an explicit NTSTATUS through filesystem loads, recursive
imports and forwarded exports. Resource, image-format, protection, TLS and
initialization failures abort PE32/PE32+ binding before writing a null import or
entering the dependent image. The existing compatibility policy for genuinely
missing DLLs/exports is unchanged. LoadLibrary preserves the loader's error;
the NTSTATUS translator now covers failed initialization, missing DLL/export and
generic failure. Forwarders also append the provider's `.dll` extension when
loading it. This does not implement full dependency reference rollback.

`load_dependency_pe.c` checks that a failed dependency prevents the parent's
attach callback and publication, preserves error 1114, and still permits a later
healthy load. A second chain reaches the failing DLL through an export forwarder.

PE file with a 2.25 GiB zero-fill section, exceeding the 2 GiB VM; it must return
error 8 without calling the parent's attach callback. All these checks, the
existing 136-check DLL lifecycle fixture on each ABI, and module/TLS/wait
selftests pass on r34: 557 counted checks, no CPU exceptions, SSH available.

### 4.347 Grow completion-port storage for original Steam DLL reloads

The r35 diagnostic of full Steam startup records CreateIoCompletionPort returning

new completion port after each unload. Native Windows completes all 485 checks

previous record-lifetime guarantee. Allocation happens outside the association
spinlock, then rechecks for a reusable slot before publishing a new record.
Readers scan only the published high-water count; they do not scan all 4096
potential slots. Per-port active-thread storage is still released on final
event close. The pool intentionally retains its peak record allocation.

executable is byte-identical to the original 2,962,584-byte source. The generated

exits with 0xfffffffe because the 1.5 GiB volume has only 106 MiB free after its
update download; its message requires 250 MB. This is a fixture-space limit,
not evidence of a service-start failure. No CPU exceptions occurred and SSH
remained available. The next fixture uses 2.5 GiB and this actual installed
service state. Build/duplicate cleanup freed another 109,709,844 bytes, while
canonical kernels, frozen inputs and raw logs were retained.

### 4.348 Avoid unused GDI snapshots on the caller's stack

The 2.5 GiB / 32,768-inode Steam fixture completes its update without an
`OSFS3-CREATE-FAIL`. Later CEF children fault in `SelectObject+0x63`: the
indirect call to `dc_from_handle` pushes its return address into the reserved
bottom page of the caller's stack. In the first complete trace, RSP is
0x4000130dc0, CR2 is 0x4000130db8 and the reservation starts at 0x4000130000.
The object argument is NULL. `steam-service-qemu-r36-32k/service-final.json`
records nine exceptions and working SSH. UART interleaving leaves only four
RIPs cleanly parseable: three in `SelectObject` and one CEF path-service #BP.
The initial runner result predates those exceptions. Post-update guest DLL
hash verification was attempted after the VM ended and did not complete.

`SelectObject` allocated full brush and pen snapshots, including pattern
palettes, without using their contents. Acquisition now accepts a NULL
snapshot and still validates the handle, owner and stock-object type and
retains the reference. Drawing and inspection callers continue requesting
snapshots. Selection alone skips the copies. The exact r36/r37 disassembly
reduces its local `sub rsp` allocation from 0xa40 to 0xd8 bytes; saved registers
and callees also use stack space. GitNexus reports 14 upstream symbols for
`brush_acquire`, no indexed upstream callers for the exported `SelectObject`,
and no indexed `gdi_pen_acquire`; the latter's six callers were inspected
directly. Only `gdi32_shim.c` differs between the frozen 969-input builds,
and all 14 GUI inputs remain included.

The new `select_stack_pe.c` probe creates a 64 KiB worker stack and places an
explicit inaccessible page within its reservation, then calls
`SelectObject(dc, NULL)` with about 2.2 KiB remaining above it. This avoids
depending on Windows' extra space reserved for stack-overflow handling; an
initial probe against the true stack bottom overflowed on both Windows ABIs
and was rejected as an oracle. The final r2 binaries pass nine checks per ABI
on native Windows. In QEMU, r36 passes x86 but faults at the same
`SelectObject+0x63` on x64. r37 passes both ABIs without exceptions and keeps
SSH operational. This establishes a stack-cost regression test, not a general
Windows API stack-size guarantee or the cause of CEF's deep call stack.

The existing GDI state and extended-pen probes pass 1,646 checks on each
kernel (both ABIs combined), with unchanged result rows across r36/r37 after
removing complete interleaved MEMSTAT/HEAP-SITE telemetry records.
Extended-pen tests also pass natively (782 checks per ABI). The GDI state
fixture has four native x86 and six native x64 pixel-check failures, so its
guest results serve only as a regression comparison, not native parity.
The host surface-lifetime test passes 2,044 checks with GCC and Clang, both
normally and under ASan/UBSan; all 109 allocations are freed and no pins remain.
The extended-pen host run also passes under ASan/UBSan.

Evidence is retained in `select-stack-probe-r2`, `select-stack-qemu-r36`,
`select-stack-qemu-r37`, `select-stack-regression-r1`,
`select-regression-qemu-r36`, `select-regression-qemu-r37`, and
`select-stack-host-r37`. Kernel r37 is 8,385,584 bytes, SHA256
f30c93f4fac1944f34747478daf86c23afb6f1d2697573b8ee7b7a14e05af7eb.
The general r37 suite passes 885,562 counted checks, both DNS probes and all

The full `steam-service-qemu-r37-32k` run completes its update but still fails

### 4.350 Logical-font capacity, lifetime and owned handles

Candidate r38b replaces the fixed 256-entry logical-font table with dynamically
allocated records in 128 hash buckets. Allocation and caller LOGFONT copying
occur outside the IRQ-safe object lock; completed records are published under
that lock. Handles use nonzero 24-bit identifiers and skip live collisions at
wrap. DeleteObject removes owned records and frees them outside the lock;
process teardown also removes that process's logical fonts after DC cleanup.
Readers copy LOGFONT metadata while holding the lock, so no borrowed record
pointer survives deletion or process teardown. This fixes the demonstrated
capacity and lifetime failures; it does not establish Windows' resource quota
or deferred deletion of fonts still selected in a DC.

Native tests show that GetObjectW can read another live process's font metadata,
while DeleteObject refuses that handle. The initial ownership oracle wrongly
expected the metadata query to fail and was rejected. The final r4 fixture
keeps read-only metadata queries available and restricts SelectObject and
DeleteObject to the owner. It also tests stale handles and retained caller
metadata. Native Windows and r38b QEMU each pass 1,584 checks per ABI:
1,538 capacity checks, 29 child-lifetime checks and 17 handle checks. Both guest
ABIs retain SSH with zero CPU exceptions.

The host font test adds allocation failure, identifier wrap and live collision,
selected/saved-DC references, process-specific teardown and four concurrent
create/query/delete workers. GCC and Clang each pass 13,853 checks, both normally
and under ASan/UBSan, with 4,232 allocations and releases per run. The existing
surface-lifetime regression also passes all four variants: 2,044 checks,
109 allocations and releases, and zero pins per run. The host allocator and
process-ID adapters are opt-in test hooks with unchanged defaults.

GitNexus reports six direct callers and ten upstream symbols for
font_from_handle, and 18 upstream symbols for gdi32_release_process. New helpers
and host adapters are unindexed and were reviewed manually. The frozen r38b
build contains 969 inputs; only gdi32_shim.c differs from r37 and all 14 GUI
inputs remain identical and included. r38b is 8,385,664 bytes, SHA256
4578446788c8294b55a3fdb0937f725e63ea0c816ac23f929ce22688bd4a0a01.
The initial r38 build predates the corrected foreign-query contract and is
superseded. Compiled snapshot intermediates were removed after verifying the
retained canonical ELF hashes. Neither font candidate is deployed on the P1.

Evidence: font-lifetime-probe-r4, font-lifetime-qemu-r38b-{32,64},
font-lifetime-host-r38b and font-surface-host-r38b under the ignored
arch/x86/build/msgwait-20261003 tree.

The final font-gdi-regression-qemu-r38b run passes 18 reduced-stack checks and
1,646 GDI state/extended-pen checks, with SSH and zero exceptions. Its GDI rows
match r37 after removing only complete interleaved MEMSTAT/HEAP-SITE telemetry
records; the raw logs are retained. The GDI state fixture still has the known
native pixel-check failures described above, so this comparison establishes
guest regression stability rather than native parity. The full Steam client
has not been run with r38b. Qualification is recorded in
sspi-research/qualification-r38b.json.

### 4.352. External D3D9 provider and real softpipe rendering (2026-10-08)

The r45 candidate forwards Direct3DCreate9/Ex to an installed
`d3d9-provider.dll`, resolved through the process DLL search path and pinned
until process exit. PE32 enters the provider through the existing callback
transition; PE64 calls its Microsoft ABI directly. Export lookup is restricted
to that PE image to avoid falling back to the shim itself. An absent provider
continues to return a null interface / D3DERR_NOTAVAILABLE. No Microsoft or Wine
DLL is linked into the kernel.

The external Mesa 25.0.0 module now supplies a softpipe context with a null
software winsys and actual color/depth resources and pixel readback. Win32-owned
heap arenas are reclaimed with the process; successive PE32/PE64 runs no longer
consume the root task's small, persistent brk arena. CPU rendering continues to
report WGL_NO_ACCELERATION_ARB. Its pixel format does not claim to be Windows'
generic GDI renderer. WGL resolves Mesa's proc-address table as well as ELF
exports, exposing 2,333 typed GL wrappers, including glGetInternalformativ.
The PE32 ShaderSource bridge widens the array of string pointers before entering
64-bit Mesa, preserving explicit lengths and the ARB alias.

Two build defects blocked real shaders: the ARB parser had been replaced by an
always-failing placeholder, and standalone_scaffolding.cpp overrode Mesa's
reference-counting functions with assignments. The runtime now builds the
original ARB lexer/parser and excludes the standalone compiler scaffolding.
Invalid ARB source still reports GL_INVALID_OPERATION; valid GLSL and ARB
programs render green and blue triangles respectively. Deleting a linked
program preserves attached shader names until their explicit deletion.

The WineD3D fixtures also exposed circular DLL initialization: a dependency's
DllMain called into its importer before its IAT was complete. DLL mapping now
finishes the import graph before draining pending TLS/DllMain initialization.
CRT/Win32 contracts required by the original providers are covered separately.

Qualification: `d3d9-system-qemu-r45/results.json` passes PE32/PE64 circular
initializers, 246 import resolutions, 2,694 runtime API checks, GL pixels,
GLSL/ARB compilation and deletion, and system-path Direct3D9 creation,
backbuffer readback (0xff224466), presentation and teardown. No CPU exception
or Mesa assertion was recorded; SSH responded afterward. Native Windows
oracles are `gl-softpipe-r5/native.json`, `d3d9-system-r1/native.json`,
`graphics-dependency-r2/native.json` and `wined3d-runtime-r2/native.json`.
Earlier `d3d9-lifetime-fixed-qemu-r44b` verifies the external DLL directly.

Kernel r45: 9,463,968 bytes, SHA256
e29d4d57c4ea3f1ee5b7b2f256a615bff8f877c2fa696ede1a30dd8ada84a540.
Its frozen build includes the shared GUI. The physical P1 was updated from r37
to r45 with verified backups and hotreload. All four physical GL and system
D3D9 probes pass (PE32 and PE64), including shader pixels and D3D9 readback
0xff224466, without CPU exceptions. Provider DLLs are installed externally in
