### 4.354. WineD3D window DC and visible Direct3D9 presentation (2026-10-08)

GetDCEx rejected DCX_USESTYLE (0x10000), including WineD3D's
DCX_USESTYLE|DCX_CACHE request for its swapchain window. WineD3D 3.8 then
falls back to a zero-sized hidden window. Successful backbuffer readback and
Present return codes did not establish that pixels reached the real window.
The relevant upstream paths are context_create in Wine's
[context.c](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/wine-3.8/dlls/wined3d/context.c)
and GetDCEx in
[painting.c](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/wine-3.8/dlls/user32/painting.c).

r47 implements style-derived child/sibling clipping, replacing the explicit
clip flags when USESTYLE is requested. Window DCs ignore child clipping and
force a cached DC; top-level DCs clip siblings. Parent/class/private DC cases
that still lack the required backing-surface semantics remain unsupported.
No provider DLL is embedded in the kernel. GitNexus did not index GetDCEx or
the two test entry points; the manual scope review covers DC allocation,
visible-region clipping, and the GL swapchain's window association.

dcex-probe-r4 passes 54 native Windows checks per ABI on a private desktop,
and 53 guest checks per ABI (the private-desktop cleanup is native-only).
The added cases verify USESTYLE acceptance, the DC's window identity,
replacement of explicit flags, style-derived child/sibling clipping, and
the WINDOW exception. dcex-graphics-qemu-r47 also passes the existing circular
DLL initialization, 246 import checks, 2694 runtime contracts, GL sharing,
and D3D9 shader drawing tests without CPU exceptions or Mesa assertions.

d3d9-draw-r5 is native-qualified for both ABIs and checks the actual
swapchain DC association before device creation. Its optional --hold interval
allows a QEMU framebuffer capture after the final blue shader triangle.
d3d9-present-long-qemu-r47 passes both ABIs: present32.png and present64.png
show the triangle in the application window, and framebuffer-pixels.json
verifies 11,750 blue pixels plus interior/exterior samples in each capture.
This is visible presentation evidence, beyond internal readback. The r46
negative control's full dmesg records ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87) at
swapchain-dc-target in both ABIs (the PE32 UART copy dropped that output).
The earlier five-second capture interval missed the window
and is superseded by the thirty-second capture run. A native GetPixel-based
screen experiment did not produce a valid presentation oracle and was not
retained as a passing test.

With both external provider architectures installed, steam-graphics-qemu-r47
shows Steam's login and survives 120 seconds with SSH responding, no CPU
exceptions and no Mesa assertions. Its webhelper log explicitly records GPU
disable and a browser reload, so this qualifies visible software fallback,
not Chromium GPU compatibility. Physical Braid gameplay and performance
remain unverified; the P1 still has r45 and is not accepting SSH.

A 12-second BSP timer profile retained 1,223 samples. Exact PCs place 421 in

and the resource idle wait used by
[wined3d_resource_map](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/wine-3.8/dlls/wined3d/resource.c).
The supported `csmt` configuration is read by
[WineD3D initialization](https://github.com/wine-mirror/wine/blob/wine-3.8/dlls/wined3d/wined3d_main.c).
Comparing its threaded/default and synchronous modes is a pending performance
experiment; no configuration or binaries were changed on the strength of this
profile. Raw samples and symbol analysis are retained in
`d3d9-p1-r48/render-profile{,-raw}.log` and `render-profile-analysis.json`.

### 4.358. External WineD3D configuration and command-stream comparison (2026-10-08)

The r48 kernel, external Mesa module and WineD3D DLLs are unchanged. An optional
`wined3d-config.exe` program now queries, writes and removes the supported
global WineD3D `csmt` DWORD. It flushes and reads back changes, reports failures,
and does not embed renderer code or Microsoft runtime files in the kernel.
Build and guest invocation are documented in [the backend guide](x86-d3d9-backend.md).
GitNexus returned UNKNOWN for the test entry point and new utility entry point;
manual scope is the standalone PE diagnostics/configuration and build scripts,
with no kernel callers changed. The GUI work remains included in r48.

The D3D9 probe has an optional benchmark build. It warms up, then alternates
fixed-function green and shader blue triangles for 16 frames. Every frame
checks center and background pixels through readback before calling Present.
There is no successful-check logging inside the measured loop. The isolated
`csmt0`/`csmt1` variants set the value before loading WineD3D and restore the
previous value during normal cleanup. Native variants never write the setting.
Both native ABIs pass the rendering checks.

QEMU runs the same work in mode order 1,0,0,1,1,0 for each ABI. PE32 medians are
5,940 ms with csmt=1 and 220 ms with csmt=0; PE64 medians are 2,010 and 240 ms.
All 12 runs pass the pixel checks and registry restoration, without CPU
exceptions or kernel assertions. WGL context thread IDs independently confirm
caller-thread execution versus a separate command-stream worker. This matters
because the PE64 provider does not emit the PE32 winediag message: the original
collector's message-only gate reports false for PE64, while the separate
`qualification.json` records the thread evidence and passes both ABIs.
A first collection ended on a partially written serial completion line; the
second waits for the complete line. Neither issue is a renderer failure.

The benchmark measures API-loop time, not display completion, Steam latency
or game frame rate. The first PE32 csmt=1 screenshot still has the preceding
green frame. The other three captures contain 11,750 blue pixels, including
both csmt=0 captures. Evidence is in `d3d9-benchmark-r1/` and
`d3d9-csmt-qemu-r48-r2/` under `arch/x86/build/msgwait-20261003/`.

`steam-csmt-qemu-r48/` then verifies 11 configuration/query/default/invalid
argument cases across PE32/PE64. Independent render processes inherit csmt=0
and pass both ABI probes (220/250 ms) without writing the setting themselves.
Steam launches without flags on the existing clean-account base and visibly
renders the login form and QR. Twelve ten-second observation intervals retain
SSH without CPU exceptions or kernel assertions. Current-run CEF records have
the same error categories as the previous r48 baseline: no D3D9 initialization
failure, GPU-process exit or fatal message; D3D11/GLES3 fallback and the two
existing NOTREACHED diagnostics remain. This is not error-free CEF or gameplay

The two configuration binaries are staged on P1 at
`/Diagnostics/Win32/d3d9-csmt/config{32,64}.exe`. Steam console request 6 remains
running. The setting has not been applied on P1 and Steam has not been restarted.
Physical Braid validation is still pending. No kernel backup was created by

The broader backend audit remains incomplete. Both pinned MSYS2 archives have

## 5. Open questions / notes
- `WINAPI` selects the Microsoft x64 ABI for native shims, not the kernel's
  SysV ABI. Export arg-count metadata also drives the **32-bit thunk's `RET n*4`**.
  So GT-argc must be the count of
  **32-bit stack DWORDs the 32-bit caller pushed**, not the 64-bit ABI.
- Variadic CRT fns (printf family) are cdecl → caller cleans, so a too-large
  argc (12) is harmless for cleanup; it only affects how many stack DWORDs the
  dispatcher copies. Keep but document.
- COM vtable methods (DD_*, Surf_*) are stdcall-with-`this`; argc includes `this`.
